SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f1.claim: Sībawayh distinguishes three treatments of hamza: full realization, softening, and replacement.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f1.anchor: اعلم أن الهمزة تكون فيها ثلاثة أشياء التحقيق والتخفيف والبدل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f2.claim: An open hamza after fatḥa may be softened to a sound between hamza and a long alif, retaining its measure while weakening the sound.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f2.anchor: مفتوحة كانت قبلها فتحة فإنك تجعلها إذا أردت تخفيفها بين الهمزة والألف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f3.speaker: أهل الحجاز
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f3.claim: The Hijazis soften the hamza in سأل between hamza and alif; Tamimis pronounce it fully.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f3.anchor: يحقق بنو تميم وقد قرأ قبل بين بين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f4.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f4.claim: An open hamza preceded by kasra is replaced by yāʾ in softening, rather than being made between-between.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f4.anchor: مفتوحة وكان قبلها حرف مكسور فإنك تبدل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f5.claim: An open hamza preceded by ḍamma is replaced by wāw; the preceding vowel prevents between-between softening.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f5.anchor: ضمة وأردت أن تخفف أبدلت مكانها واوا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f6.claim: A vowelless hamza is replaced with the long-vowel letter matching the preceding vowel: alif after fatḥa, wāw after ḍamma, and yāʾ after kasra.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f6.anchor: ساكنة الحرف الذي منه الحركة التي قبلها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f7.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f7.claim: A vowelless hamza cannot undergo between-between softening or deletion, so the matching long-vowel letter must replace it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f7.anchor: هذه السواكن بين بين أنها حروف ميتة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f8.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f8.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f8.claim: A moving hamza after a vowelless consonant is deleted and its vowel transferred to that consonant.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f8.anchor: متحركة كان قبلها حرف ساكن فأردت أن تخفف حذفتها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f10.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f10.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f10.claim: Frequent forms from رأيت are commonly softened because of their frequent use; Arabs treat the hamza as alternating in these forms.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f10.anchor: فقد اجتمعت العرب على تخفيفه لكثرة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f11.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f11.speaker: أبو الخطاب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f11.claim: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb heard trusted Arabs retain the original hamza in قد أرآهم despite the widespread softened forms.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f11.anchor: وحدثني أبو الخطاب أنه سمع من يقول قد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f12.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f12.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f12.claim: A moving hamza after alif is not deleted, since changing the alif would turn it into another letter; it may instead be softened between-between.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f12.anchor: تحذف لأنك لو حذفتها ثم فعلت بالألف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f13.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f13.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f13.claim: A moving hamza after a long added wāw or yāʾ is replaced by the matching letter rather than softened or deleted, preserving the preceding glide.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f13.anchor: ياء زائدة ساكنة لم تلحق لتلحق بناء ببناء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f14.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f14.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f14.claim: Root consonants, derivational additions, and meaningful suffixes behave differently from long added glides; root wāw and yāʾ remain, as in يدعو and يرمي.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f15.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f15.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f15.claim: Hamza is difficult to articulate because it is produced deep in the throat with force, making it the farthest articulation point among the letters.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f15.anchor: وهي أبعد الحروف مخرجا فثقل عليهم ذلك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f16.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f16.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f16.claim: When two hamzas from separate words meet, speakers ease one because fully articulating both together is avoided; each word can otherwise occur independently.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f21.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f21.speaker: أهل الحجاز
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f21.claim: The Hijazis soften both hamzas in a two-word sequence, as in their pronunciation of اقرأ آية.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f22.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f22.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f22.claim: In اقرأ آية, the result depends on which hamza is softened: a vowelless hamza is replaced, while a moving hamza after a consonant is deleted and transfers its vowel.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f23.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f23.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f23.claim: Sībawayh reports that Abū ʿAmr prefers a Hijazi pronunciation inserting an alif between the interrogative alif and a following softened hamza; insertion prevents two hamzas from meeting.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f24.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f24.speaker: بنو تميم
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f24.claim: Some Tamimis insert an alif between interrogative alif and hamza to avoid adjacent hamzas; other Tamimis fully realize both without insertion.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f25.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f25.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f25.claim: When two hamzas occur in one word, the second must be replaced; the word-internal sequence cannot be handled like two separate words.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f25.anchor: لم يكن بد من بدل الآخرة ولا تخفف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f26.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f26.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f26.claim: In derived forms, hamza replacement follows the preceding vowel: the form from جئت uses yāʾ, while آدم uses alif after fatḥa.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f26.anchor: أبدلت مكانها الياء لأن ما قبلها مكسور

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f27.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f27.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f27.claim: Al-Khalīl gives جيأى as the intensive-pattern form derived from جئت, with the pattern measured like جيعا.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f27.anchor: عن فعلل من جئت فقال جيأى وتقديرها جيعا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f28.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f28.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f28.claim: The form خطايا has two hamza adjustments: the final yāʾ becomes alif after kasra, and the preceding hamza becomes yāʾ opened before that alif.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f28.anchor: فكأنهم قلبوا ياء أبدلت من آخر خطايا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f29.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f29.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f29.claim: Replacement of a realized hamza with alif, yāʾ, or wāw is generally lexical rather than a fully productive analogy; poets may extend it under metrical necessity.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f29.anchor: وليس ذا بقياس متلئب نحو ما ذكرنا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f30.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f30.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f30.claim: Poetic necessity can regularize the otherwise lexical replacement pattern; Farazdaq substitutes alif for hamza in منساة to preserve meter.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f30.anchor: ولو جعلها بين بين لانكسر البيت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f31.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f31.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f31.claim: Ḥassān ibn Thābit and Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl use سالت and سالتا for سألت; Sībawayh says these are not their dialect, though سلت تسال is another reported language.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f32.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f32.speaker: العرب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f32.claim: Sībawayh reports سلت تسال as a dialectal pair and cites ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥassān's واجي for الواجئ.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f33.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f33.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f33.claim: Words such as نبي and برية have conventional hamza replacement, but the pattern is not extended to every similar word.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f33.anchor: وقالوا نبي وبرية فألزمها أهل التحقيق البدل وليس كل شيء نحو

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f34.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f34.speaker: أهل الحجاز
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f34.claim: Some Hijazis who otherwise articulate hamza retain it in نبي and بريئة; Sībawayh calls this rare and poor.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f34.anchor: قوما من أهل الحجاز من أهل التحقيق

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f35.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f35.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f35.claim: Across word boundaries, open hamza may be replaced by the matching glide, as in أو أنت becoming أونت; within one word, forms such as سوأة may instead delete it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f35.anchor: واعلم أن العرب منها من يقول

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f36.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f36.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f36.claim: When successive wāws, yāʾs, or kasras would accumulate across words, some speakers delete hamza to ease the sequence, as in أحلبني بلك and أبومك.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f37.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f37.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f37.claim: Some speakers delete hamza in forms such as يجيك and يسوك; in يرم خوانه they also delete yāʾ to avoid adjacent vowelless sounds.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f37.anchor: يجيك ويسوك يحذف الهمزة ويكره الضم مع الواو والياء

STUDYQURAN:2:114/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r1.claim: Masājid, singular masjid, derives from sajada, “to prostrate.”

STUDYQURAN:2:114/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r2.claim: Some commentators identify the mosques as the Jerusalem Temple and the Kaʿbah in Makkah, both called masjid in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r2.anchor: Some point to the Temple in Jerusalem (the Farthest Mosque mentioned in 17:1) and the Kaʿbah in Makkah

STUDYQURAN:2:114/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r3.claim: Commentators give differing accounts of the Temple's destruction; some say Christians connived in it.
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r3.anchor: They also give differing accounts of the destruction of the Temple, which according to some took place with the connivance of Christians.

STUDYQURAN:2:114/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r4.claim: Some connect the verse to the Makkans stopping the Prophet from entering Makkah to pray at the Kaʿbah at Ḥudaybiyah in 628, after which the pilgrims returned to Madinah to come back the next year.
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r4.anchor: Some say this verse refers to when at Ḥudaybiyah the Makkans stopped the Prophet from entering Makkah to pray at the Kaʿbah

STUDYQURAN:2:114/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r5.speaker: al-Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the verse refers to the Jerusalem Temple, since even idolaters never tried to destroy the Kaʿbah.
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r5.anchor: For al-Ṭabarī, since even the idolaters never tried to destroy the Kaʿbah, it must refer to the Temple.

STUDYQURAN:2:114/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r6.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r6.claim: Others read the verse generally as applying to anyone who prevents people from entering any house of worship.
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r6.anchor: Others see it more generally, saying that it applies to anyone who prevents people from entering any house of worship (Q).

STUDYQURAN:2:114/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r7.claim: A broader gloss, given by IK, Q, and R, says idolaters sought the Kaʿbah's ruin by filling it with idols: it ceased to be a mosque of the One God and became a temple of idols.

STUDYQURAN:2:114/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r8.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r8.claim: R mentions that Abū Bakr had a small mosque in Makkah before the Hijrah which the Makkans later destroyed.
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r8.anchor: Some also mention that Abū Bakr had a small mosque in Makkah before the Muslims migrated to Madinah, a mosque the Makkans later destroyed (R).

STUDYQURAN:2:114/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r9.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r9.claim: Some specify disgrace or fear as the jizyah paid by Christians.
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r9.anchor: Some try to identify specific ways in which disgrace or fear is evidenced by Christians, such as the payment of the jizyah

STUDYQURAN:2:114/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r10.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r10.claim: Others understand disgrace broadly and note that the Prophet often prayed that disgrace would not befall him and his community in this world.
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r10.anchor: But others point out that the notion of disgrace can be quite broad, and that the Prophet would often pray

STUDYQURAN:2:114/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r11.speaker: some Sufis
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r11.claim: Some Sufis read the heart as the house of love and knowledge of God, like the Kaʿbah as God's House, and say false desires destroy it.
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r11.anchor: Some Sufis discern another level of meaning, saying that the heart is the “house” of love and knowledge of God

STUDYQURAN:2:114/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r12.claim: The verse is connected with 9:17, which says idolaters may not maintain God's mosques while bearing witness to their disbelief.
STUDYQURAN:2:114/r12.anchor: See also 9:17: It is not for the idolaters to maintain the mosques of God, bearing witness of disbelief against themselves.

TAB-FULL:v2p441/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p441/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p441/r1.claim: A mosque is any place where God is worshipped, literally the place where prostration to God occurs; preventing worship there is especially transgressive.
TAB-FULL:v2p441/r1.anchor: يجلس فيه: المجلس، وللموضع الذي ينزل فيه: منزل

TAB-FULL:v2p441/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p441/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p441/r2.claim: Masjid is the singular and masājid its plural, formed like majlis/majālis and manzil/manāzil.
TAB-FULL:v2p441/r2.anchor: ثم يجمع منازل ومجالس نظير مسجد ومساجد

TAB-FULL:v2p441/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p441/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p441/r3.claim: A use of masājid as a singular form is reported from some Arabs, but al-Ṭabarī regards it as an error by the speaker.
TAB-FULL:v2p441/r3.anchor: وقد حكي سماعا من بعض العرب مساجد في واحد المساجد، وذلك كالخطأ من قائله

TAB-FULL:v2p442/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p442/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p442/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports a grammatical view that supplies a missing preposition, construing the phrase as preventing God's name from being mentioned there; أن is accusative after loss of its genitive marker.
TAB-FULL:v2p442/r1.anchor: يذكر اسم الله في مساجده، فتكون أن حينئذ

TAB-FULL:v2p442/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p442/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p442/r2.claim: The other analysis paraphrases it as preventing God's name from being mentioned in His mosques; أن is accusative by repetition of the syntactic position of مساجد.
TAB-FULL:v2p442/r2.anchor: يذكر اسم الله في مساجده، فتكون أن حينئذ في موضع نصب تكريرا على موضع المساجد وردا عليه

TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r1.claim: The phrase describes one who prevents God's mosques from being used and one who strives to ruin them; سعى is coordinated with منع.
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r1.anchor: في قول الله: {ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه وسعى في خرابها}

TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the people who blocked worship as Christians; the mosque in this interpretation is Jerusalem's sanctuary.
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " قوله: {ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه} [البقرة: 114] أنهم النصارى

TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says Christians defiled Jerusalem's sanctuary and prevented people from praying there.
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: " في قول الله: {ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه وسعى في خرابها} [البقرة: 114] النصارى كانوا يطرحون

TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r4.claim: Qatāda says Christians, urged by some Jews, helped Nebuchadnezzar the Babylonian Magian destroy Jerusalem's sanctuary.
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة: " قوله: {ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه} [البقرة: 114] الآية، أولئك أعداء الله النصارى

TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r5.claim: In another report Qatāda says Nebuchadnezzar and his companions destroyed Jerusalem's sanctuary with Christian help.
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة: " في قوله: {ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه وسعى في خرابها} [البقرة: 114] قال: هو بختنصر وأصحابه

TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says the Romans allied with Nebuchadnezzar to destroy Jerusalem and dump corpses there, in revenge for Israel's killing John son of Zechariah.
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r6.anchor: عن السدي: " {ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه وسعى في خرابها} [البقرة: 114] قال: الروم، كانوا ظاهروا بختنصر

TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r7.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r7.claim: Another view identifies the perpetrators as Quraysh polytheists, who barred the Messenger from the Sacred Mosque.
TAB-FULL:v2p442#2/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: بلى عنى الله عز وجل بهذه الآية مشركي قريش، إذ منعوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من المسجد الحرام

TAB-FULL:v2p444/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p444/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v2p444/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies Quraysh at al-Ḥudaybiyya: they stopped Muhammad entering Mecca until he sacrificed at Dhū Ṭuwā and made a truce; they cut off pilgrims and worshippers who maintained the sanctuary.
TAB-FULL:v2p444/r1.anchor: ابن زيد: " في قوله: {ومن أظلم ممن منع

TAB-FULL:v2p444/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p444/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v2p444/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd explains striving to ruin the mosque as deterring people who maintained it through remembrance and came for pilgrimage or ʿumra.
TAB-FULL:v2p444/r2.anchor: قالوا: إذ قطعوا من يعمرها بذكره ويأتيها للحج والعمرة

TAB-FULL:v2p444/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p444/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p444/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers Christians and Jerusalem's sanctuary: they helped Nebuchadnezzar ruin it and later barred Israelite believers from praying there. Quraysh barred prayer temporarily but never sought to demolish the sanctuary, which they had built and celebrated; the surrounding passage concerns Jews and Christians, not Quraysh.
TAB-FULL:v2p444/r3.anchor: فالذي هو أولى بالآية أن يوجه تأويلها إليه، هو ما كان نظير قصة الآية قبلها والآية بعدها

TAB-FULL:v2p446/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p446/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p446/r1.claim: The immediate case is those who barred Israelites, obligated to pray at Jerusalem's sanctuary, and sought to ruin it; the general wording also condemns anyone who prevents obligatory or voluntary worship in any mosque or works to destroy one.
TAB-FULL:v2p446/r1.anchor: إنما ذكر ظلم من منع من كان فرضه الصلاة في بيت المقدس من مؤمني بني إسرائيل

TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r1.claim: Those who obstructed worship and ruined the mosques were not to enter them while hostile, except in fear of punishment for entering.
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة: " {ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين} [البقرة: 114] وهم اليوم كذلك، لا يوجد نصراني

TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says Christians were then severely beaten and punished if found in Jerusalem's sanctuary.
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: " {ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين} [البقرة: 114] وهم اليوم كذلك، لا يوجد نصراني

TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r3.claim: In another report Qatāda says Christians enter the sanctuary secretly and are punished if caught.
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة: " قال الله عز وجل: {ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين} [البقرة: 114] وهم النصارى، فلا يدخلون المسجد

TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says no Roman enters without fearing execution or fearing the levy of jizya, which he pays.
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r4.anchor: عن السدي: " {أولئك ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين} [البقرة: 114] فليس في الأرض رومي يدخلها اليوم إلا وهو خائف

TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd connects the warning to Muhammad's proclamation that after that year no polytheist could perform pilgrimage or circumambulate naked; the polytheists complained they were barred from lodging.
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " في قوله: {أولئك ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين} [البقرة: 114] قال: نادى رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r6.claim: The wording uses a plural predicate about all perpetrators because man is singular in form but collective in meaning.
TAB-FULL:v2p446#2/r6.anchor: فأخرج على وجه الخبر عن الجميع وهو خبر عمن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه؛ لأن «من» في معنى الجميع

TAB-FULL:v2p448/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p448/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p448/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains khizy as disgrace, evil, or abasement, realized either by killing and captivity or by humiliating subjection through jizya.
TAB-FULL:v2p448/r1.anchor: فإنه يعني بالخزي: العار والشر والذلة إما القتل والسباء، وإما الذلة والصغار بأداء الجزية

TAB-FULL:v2p448/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p448/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p448/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses the worldly disgrace as paying jizya while subdued.
TAB-FULL:v2p448/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: " {لهم في الدنيا خزي} [البقرة: 114] قال: يعطون الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون "

TAB-FULL:v2p448/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p448/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v2p448/r3.claim: Al-Suddī predicts the Mahdi's rise and conquest of Constantinople, where they will be killed; the great punishment is Hell, whose inmates neither receive relief nor die.
TAB-FULL:v2p448/r3.anchor: عن السدي: " قوله: {لهم في الدنيا خزي} [البقرة: 114] أما خزيهم في الدنيا: فإنهم إذا قام المهدي وفتحت القسطنطينية قتلهم

TAB-FULL:v2p448/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p448/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p448/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī concludes their worldly penalty is abasement, killing, and captivity for obstructing worship and ruining mosques; their disbelief and corruption merit Hell.
TAB-FULL:v2p448/r4.anchor: وتأويل الآية: لهم في الدنيا الذلة والهوان والقتل والسبي، على منعهم مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه

TABATABAI:2:108-115/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:108-115/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:108-115/r5.claim: The promise that God will bring his command hints at a later ruling concerning them; the next verse's fearful entry and the ban in 9:28 are parallel, while 17:85 discusses God's command.
TABATABAI:2:108-115/r5.anchor: فيه كما مر إيماء إلى حكم سيشرعه الله تعالى في حقهم، ونظيره قوله تعالى في الآية الآتية

TABATABAI:2:108-115/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:108-115/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:108-115/r10.claim: The context points to Meccan unbelievers before the Hijra as the people who barred worshippers from God's mosques.
TABATABAI:2:108-115/r10.anchor: ظاهر السياق أن هؤلاء كفار مكة قبل الهجرة فإن هذه الآيات نزلت في أوائل ورود رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم المدينة

TABATABAI:2:108-115/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:108-115/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:108-115/r11.claim: The past-tense wording fits Quraysh's completed acts: they prevented Muslims from praying in the Sacred Mosque and in mosques in the Kaaba's precinct.
TABATABAI:2:108-115/r11.anchor: يدل على مضي الواقعة وانقضائها لمكان قوله كان، فينطبق على كفار قريش وفعالهم بمكة

TABRISI:2:114/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:114/r1.claim: Manʿ, ṣadd, and ḥaylūla are synonyms; the opposite of prevention is release. Manīʿ means inaccessible or protected, and manīʿa describes a woman who will not yield to lewdness.
TABRISI:2:114/r1.anchor: المنع والصد والحيلولة نظائر وضد المنع الإطلاق يقال منعته فامتنع ورجل منيع أي لا يخلص إليه

TABRISI:2:114/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:114/r2.claim: Saʿy is synonymous with running and racing, opposite to stopping; seeking livelihood means earning for one's family, while seeking authority may mean administering charity. A couplet uses saʿā for collecting annual alms.
TABRISI:2:114/r2.anchor: والسعي والركض والعدو نظائر وضد السعي الوقف وفلان يسعى على عياله أي يكسب لهم

TABRISI:2:114/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:114/r3.claim: The idiom sāʿā al-ama means a man committed fornication with a slave woman; musāʿāt is used only of slave women.
TABRISI:2:114/r3.anchor: وساعى الرجل الأمة إذا فجر بها ولا تكون المساعاة إلا في الإماء

TABRISI:2:114/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:114/r4.claim: Kharāb, demolition, and dismantling are synonyms. Kharba is a broad earlobe piercing or any round hole.
TABRISI:2:114/r4.anchor: والخراب والهدم والنقض نظائر والخربة سعة خرق الأذن وكل ثقب مستدير

TABRISI:2:114/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114/r5.speaker: الأصمعي
TABRISI:2:114/r5.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says khārib means a thief, specifically a camel thief, and khirāba is camel theft.
TABRISI:2:114/r5.anchor: قال الأصمعي: يختص بسارق الإبل والخرابة سرقة الإبل

TABRISI:2:114/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:114/r6.claim: Min is interrogative and occupies a nominative position; aẓlam is the predicate of the initial subject.
TABRISI:2:114/r6.anchor: موضع من رفع وهو استفهام وأظلم رفع لأنه خبر الابتداء

TABRISI:2:114/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:114/r7.claim: An is an accusative appositional replacement for masājid, specifically a بدل اشتمال construction.
TABRISI:2:114/r7.anchor: موضع أن نصب على البدل من مساجد وهو بدل الاشتمال

TABRISI:2:114/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:114/r8.claim: Alternatively, an is an accusative object of purpose: they prevented worship because they disliked God's name being mentioned there.
TABRISI:2:114/r8.anchor: أن نصبا على أنه مفعول له فيكون تقديره كراهة أن يذكر فيها اسمه

TABRISI:2:114/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:114/r9.claim: Another analysis supplies a deleted min, giving the sense of preventing people from mentioning God's name there.
TABRISI:2:114/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون على حذف من وتقديره من أن يذكر

TABRISI:2:114/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:114/r10.claim: An yadkhulūhā is the nominative subject of kāna; alternatively, kāna is redundant and the clause is an initial subject.
TABRISI:2:114/r10.anchor: وأن يدخلوها في موضع رفع بأنه اسم كان وقيل إن كان ها هنا مزيدة

TABRISI:2:114/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:114/r11.claim: Illā here cancels the preceding negation, and khāʾifīn is an accusative circumstantial qualifier.
TABRISI:2:114/r11.anchor: وإلا حرف الاستثناء وهو هنا لنقض النفي وخائفين منصوب على الحال

TABRISI:2:114/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:114/r12.claim: Khizy is nominative either as a subject or because of the preceding lam; the phrases in this world and in the next function as circumstantial qualifiers of the implicit subject in lahum.
TABRISI:2:114/r12.anchor: وقوله خزي مرفوع من وجهين أحدهما: الابتداء والآخر:

TABRISI:2:114/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114/r13.speaker: الطبري
TABRISI:2:114/r13.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects the Quraysh identification because they did not physically demolish the Sacred Mosque; mosque ruin means preventing prayer, and reports describe their destruction of prayer sites in Mecca.
TABRISI:2:114/r13.anchor: الطبري بأن قال إن مشركي قريش لم يسعوا في تخريب المسجد الحرام

TABRISI:2:114/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114/r14.speaker: الطبري
TABRISI:2:114/r14.claim: Al-Ṭabarī also says the Quraysh reading fits the preceding rebuke of the People of the Book less well than the reading about Christians and Jerusalem.
TABRISI:2:114/r14.anchor: وهو أيضا لا يتعلق بما قبله من ذم أهل الكتاب كما يتعلق به إذا عنى به النصارى وبيت المقدس

TABRISI:2:114#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:114#2/r1.claim: The author answers the contextual objection: verse 2:113 had already mentioned people who lack knowledge, and the condemnation can alternate among Jews, Christians, and idolaters.
TABRISI:2:114#2/r1.anchor: وهذا أقرب لأن الكلام خرج مخرج الذم فمرة توجه الذم إلى اليهود ومرة إلى النصارى

TABRISI:2:114#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:114#2/r2.claim: No one is more unjust than one who stops God's name being mentioned in His mosques and prevents congregational prayer and worship there.
TABRISI:2:114#2/r2.anchor: لا أحد أظلم ممن منع أن يذكر في مساجد الله اسمه سبحانه وعمل في المنع من إقامة الجماعة والعبادة فيها

TABRISI:2:114#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:114#2/r3.claim: If the plural means Jerusalem or the Kaaba, it can denote the many prostration places within a great mosque, the whole mosque, or all mosques built by Muslims.
TABRISI:2:114#2/r3.anchor: فإنما جاز جمعه على أحد وجهين إما أن تكون مواضع السجود فإن المسجد العظيم يقال لكل موضع منه مسجد

TABRISI:2:114#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114#2/r4.speaker: علي
TABRISI:2:114#2/r4.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī transmits from his forefathers, from ʿAlī, that the phrase means the whole earth, based on the Prophet's teaching that the earth is a mosque and its soil a purifier.
TABRISI:2:114#2/r4.anchor: وروي عن زيد بن علي عن آبائه عن علي ع أنه أراد جميع الأرض

TABRISI:2:114#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:114#3/r1.claim: Ruining a mosque can mean expelling believers during migration, barring them from it, or preventing prayer and obedience there; both first senses may apply.
TABRISI:2:114#3/r1.anchor: أي عمل في تخريبها والتخريب إخراجهم أهل الإيمان منها عند الهجرة وقيل هو صدهم عنها ويجوز حمله على الأمرين

TABRISI:2:114#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:114#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Christians may enter Jerusalem only after severe beating and punishment, as remains the case today.
TABRISI:2:114#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس معناه أنه لا يدخل نصراني بيت المقدس

TABRISI:2:114#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114#3/r3.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:114#3/r3.claim: If the verse concerns the Sacred Mosque, the Prophet ordered an announcement barring polytheist pilgrimage after that year and naked circumambulation; they stopped entering afterward.
TABRISI:2:114#3/r3.anchor: أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مناديا فنادى:

TABRISI:2:114#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114#3/r4.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:2:114#3/r4.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says polytheists may not enter the Sacred Mosque or other mosques, and those who enter are expelled except litigants visiting a judge briefly under fear of removal.
TABRISI:2:114#3/r4.anchor: قال الجبائي بين الله سبحانه أنه ليس لهؤلاء المشركين دخول المسجد الحرام

TABRISI:2:114#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114#3/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:2:114#3/r5.claim: Abū Jaʿfar says the verse proves unbelievers may be barred from every mosque and polytheists from the Sacred Mosque even for litigation; 9:17 and 9:28 support the latter rule.
TABRISI:2:114#3/r5.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو جعفر قدس الله روحه

TABRISI:2:114#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114#3/r6.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:114#3/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets this as God's promise of Muslim ascendancy, such that opponents cannot enter their mosques except fearfully, paralleling 9:33.
TABRISI:2:114#3/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج أعلم الله سبحانه في هذه الآية

TABRISI:2:114#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114#3/r7.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:2:114#3/r7.claim: Qatāda says worldly humiliation is payment of the poll tax in a state of subjection.
TABRISI:2:114#3/r7.anchor: أحدها: أن يراد بالخزي أنهم يعطون الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون عن قتادة

TABRISI:2:114#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114#3/r8.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:114#3/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj says humiliation entails killing and captivity when they are at war, or poll tax when they are protected subjects.
TABRISI:2:114#3/r8.anchor: وثانيها: أن المراد به القتل وسبي الذراري والنساء إن كانوا حربا وإعطاء الجزية إن كانوا ذمة عن الزجاج

TABRISI:2:114#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114#3/r9.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:2:114#3/r9.claim: Al-Suddī says the Mahdi will kill them after rising and conquering Constantinople.
TABRISI:2:114#3/r9.anchor: وثالثها: إن المراد بخزيهم في الدنيا أنه إذا قام المهدي وفتح قسطنطينية فحينئذ يقتلهم عن السدي

TABRISI:2:114#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114#3/r10.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:2:114#3/r10.claim: Abū ʿAlī says their humiliation is exclusion from mosques.
TABRISI:2:114#3/r10.anchor: ورابعها: أن المراد بخزيهم طردهم عن دخول المساجد عن أبي علي

TABRISI:2:114#3/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:114#3/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:114#3/r11.claim: On Judgment Day they will be punished in Hell with the greatest punishment, because they are the most unjust of wrongdoers.
TABRISI:2:114#3/r11.anchor: يعني يوم القيامة يعذبهم الله في نار جهنم بالعذاب الأعظم

THALABI:v1p260#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p260#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p260#2/r1.claim: One occasion report names the Roman Titus son of Istesanus and his allies: they invaded Israel, killed its fighters, captured children, burned the Torah, wrecked Jerusalem's temple, polluted it with carcasses, and slaughtered pigs; it remained ruined until Muslims rebuilt it under Umar.
THALABI:v1p260#2/r1.anchor: نزلت في ططيوس بن استيسانوس الرومي وأصحابه وذلك إنهم غزوا بني إسرائيل فقتلوا مقاتليهم وسبوا ذراريهم

THALABI:v1p260#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p260#2/r2.speaker: قتادة والسدي
THALABI:v1p260#2/r2.claim: Qatada and al-Suddi identify the destroyer as Nebuchadnezzar and his forces, who attacked Jerusalem with help from Titus and the Romans.
THALABI:v1p260#2/r2.anchor: قتادة والسدي: هو بخت نصر وأصحابه غزوا اليهود وخربوا بيت المقدس وأعانهم على ذلك النصارى ططيوس

THALABI:v1p260#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p260#2/r3.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v1p260#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the Romans acted because John son of Zechariah had been killed.
THALABI:v1p260#2/r3.anchor: قال السدي: من أجل إنهم قتلوا يحيى بن زكريا

THALABI:v1p260#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p260#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v1p260#2/r4.claim: Qatada says some Jews induced Nebuchadnezzar, the Babylonian Magian, to aid them.
THALABI:v1p260#2/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: حملهم بعض اليهود على معاونة بخت نصر البابلي المجوسي

THALABI:v1p260#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p260#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p260#2/r5.claim: The author glosses the wrongdoer as most unbelieving and culpable.
THALABI:v1p260#2/r5.anchor: أي أكفر وأغثا ممن منع مساجد الله

THALABI:v1p260#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p260#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p260#2/r6.claim: The mosques here mean Jerusalem's temple and its prayer niches.

THALABI:v1p260#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p260#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p260#2/r7.claim: The clause is the second object of prevent, since the verb takes two objects, or may be accusative through removing a preposition.
THALABI:v1p260#2/r7.anchor: في محل نصب المفعول الثاني لأن المنع يتعدى إلى مفعولين

THALABI:v1p260#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p260#2/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p260#2/r8.claim: The phrase means striving to bring about the mosques' destruction.
THALABI:v1p260#2/r8.anchor: وسعى في خرابها أي في عمل خرابها

THALABI:v1p260#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p260#2/r9.speaker: أبي بن كعب
THALABI:v1p260#2/r9.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's codex reads khīfāʾ, conveying fear.

THALABI:v1p260#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p260#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p260#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says no Roman may enter Jerusalem after its restoration except fearing death if discovered.
THALABI:v1p260#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لا يدخلها بعد عمارتها رومي إلا خائفا لو علم به قتل

THALABI:v1p260#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p260#2/r11.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
THALABI:v1p260#2/r11.claim: Qatada and Muqatil say Christians could enter Jerusalem only disguised and in fear of punishment and severe beating if caught.
THALABI:v1p260#2/r11.anchor: قتادة ومقاتل: لا يدخل بيت المقدس أحد من النصارى إلا متنكرا

THALABI:v1p260#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p260#2/r12.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v1p260#2/r12.claim: Al-Suddi explains their fear as fear of paying the poll tax.

THALABI:v1p260#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p260#2/r13.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v1p260#2/r13.claim: Ahl al-maʿānī read the statement as a command to drive them out by jihad so none enters except fearing death or captivity; its apparent report carries a prohibition, as in 33:53.

THALABI:v1p261/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p261/r1.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v1p261/r1.claim: Qatada identifies worldly disgrace as killing for a combatant and the poll tax for a protected non-Muslim.
THALABI:v1p261/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: هو القتل للحربي والجزية للذمي

THALABI:v1p261/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p261/r2.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
THALABI:v1p261/r2.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi say the disgrace is conquest of Constantinople, Rome, and Amorium.
THALABI:v1p261/r2.anchor: مقاتل والكلبي: فتح مدائنهم الثلاثة: قسطنطينية ورومية وعمورية

THALABI:v1p261/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p261/r3.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v1p261/r3.claim: Al-Suddi places the disgrace at the end of time: when the Mahdi appears, Constantinople is conquered, its fighters killed, and children captured.
THALABI:v1p261/r3.anchor: إذا قام المهدي [في آخر الزمان] فتحت قسطنطينية فقتل مقاتليهم

THALABI:v1p261/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p261/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p261/r4.claim: The great punishment in the Hereafter is Hellfire.
THALABI:v1p261/r4.anchor: ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم وهو النار

THALABI:v1p261/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p261/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v1p261/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Heraclius's city will be conquered, callers will give the call to prayer, wealth will be shared to satisfaction, then news of the Dajjal will send them to fight him.
THALABI:v1p261/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: لا تقوم الساعة حتى تفتح مدينة هرقل ويؤذن فيها المؤذنون ويقسم فيها المال بالترضية

THALABI:v1p261/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p261/r6.speaker: عطاء وعبد الرحمن بن عوف
THALABI:v1p261/r6.claim: ʿAta and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf say the verse concerns Meccan polytheists barring Muhammad and his Companions from pilgrimage and prayer at the Sacred Mosque at Hudaybiyya; preventing worship there was ruin, linked to 9:17.
THALABI:v1p261/r6.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في مشركي عرب مكة وأراد بالمساجد المسجد الحرام

THALABI:v1p261/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p261/r7.speaker: عطاء وعبد الرحمن بن عوف
THALABI:v1p261/r7.claim: For the Meccan reading, entry except in fear means God would open the sanctuary to the Muslims so they could enter and become its rightful people.
THALABI:v1p261/r7.anchor: يعني أهل مكة يقول: أفتحها عليكم حتى تدخلوها أو تكونوا أولى بها منهم

THALABI:v1p261/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p261/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p261/r8.claim: After the conquest, the Prophet ordered an announcement that no polytheist could perform Hajj after that year and no one could circumambulate the House naked.
THALABI:v1p261/r8.anchor: فنادى: ألا لا يحجن بعد هذا العام مشرك ولا يطوفن بالبيت عريان

THALABI:v1p261/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p261/r9.speaker: عطاء وعبد الرحمن بن عوف
THALABI:v1p261/r9.claim: In this interpretation, worldly disgrace is humiliation, killing, captivity, and expulsion.
THALABI:v1p261/r9.anchor: لهم في الدنيا خزي الذل والقتل والسبي والنفي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r1.claim: The interrogative man is the subject and aẓlam its predicate.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {ومن أظلم} الآية، (من) ابتداء، وخبره أظلم، وهو استفهام معناه: وأي أحد أظلم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r2.claim: The question rhetorically means: who could be more unjust?
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r2.anchor: وهو استفهام معناه: وأي أحد أظلم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r3.claim: One occasion-of-revelation report from Ibn Abbas places the verse among the Romans who destroyed Jerusalem; masjid refers to the Jerusalem sanctuary and its prayer niches.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس في نزول هذه الآية روايتان: الأولى: أنها نزلت في أهل الروم، لأنهم خربوا بيت المقدس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r4.claim: A second Ibn Abbas report says Meccan polytheists prevented Muslims from remembering God in the Sacred Mosque.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r4.anchor: والثانية: أنها نزلت في مشركي مكة، لأنهم منعوا المسلمين من ذكر الله في المسجد الحرام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r5.claim: On the Meccan report, striving to ruin mosques means preventing worship there, since a mosque is made flourishing through worship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r5.anchor: وكل من منع من عبادة الله في مسجد فقد سعى في خرابه؛ لأن عمارته بالعبادة فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r6.claim: Saʿy first means quick walking, then walking generally, and then work because work usually entails effort; in this verse it means action or work.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p250#2/r6.anchor: وأصل السعي في اللغة: الإسراع في المشي، قال الله عز وجل: {وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى} [القصص: 20]. ثم يسمى المشي سعيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p252/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p252/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p252/r1.claim: On the Jerusalem reading, Ibn Abbas says no Roman could enter the sanctuary after Muslims rebuilt it except in fear of being killed; Mujahid, Qatada, Muqatil, and al-Farra also hold this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p252/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس على الرواية الأولى: لم يدخل بيت المقدس بعد أن عمره المسلمون رومي إلا خائفا لو علم به قتل (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p252/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p252/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p252/r2.claim: On the Meccan reading, Ibn Abbas takes this as God's promise to the Prophet and Emigrants that they would conquer Mecca, enter safely, and become its rightful owners; Ata and Ibn Zayd share this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p252/r2.anchor: وقال على الرواية الثانية: هذا وعد من الله لنبيه والمهاجرين، يقول: أفتح مكة لكم حتى تدخلوها آمنين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p252/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p252/r3.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p252/r3.claim: An alternative treats the statement as a command: fight and overcome them so none enters without fear of death or captivity, like the prohibition phrased as a report in 33:53.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p252/r3.anchor: وقيل (¬3): إنه أمر في صيغة الخبر، يقول: جاهدوهم واستأصلوهم بالجهاد؛ كيلا يدخلها أحد منهم إلا خائفا من القتل والسبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p252/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p252/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p252/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj extends the verse to all disbelievers who unite against Islam and prevent prayer anywhere; every place of worship is a mosque, as the Prophet said the earth was made a mosque, so the unjust person is any opponent of Islam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p252/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج حاكيا: إن هذه الآية مما يعنى به جميع الكفار الذين تظاهروا على الإسلام ومنعوا جملة المساجد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p254/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p254/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p254/r1.claim: God declares that Muslims will prevail over their opponents, leaving no adversary able to enter their mosques except in fear; the author links this to 9:33.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p254/r1.anchor: أعلم الله عز وجل أن أمر المسلمين يظهر على جميع من خالفهم، حتى لا يمكن دخول مخالف إلى مساجدهم إلا خائفا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p254/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p254/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p254/r2.claim: The clause an yudhkara fīhā ismuhu is accusative as the second object of the verb منع and functions with its verb like a verbal noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p254/r2.anchor: وقوله: {أن يذكر فيها اسمه} موضع (أن) نصب؛ لأنه المفعول الثاني للمنع، وهو مع الفعل بمنزلة المصدر (¬4).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p254/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p254/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p254/r3.claim: Commentators explain worldly disgrace as killing for a belligerent and jizya for a protected non-Muslim; the author refers to his discussion at 2:85.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p254/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون: يريد القتل للحربي، والجزية للذمي (¬5). وذكرنا معنى الخزي عند قوله: {فما جزاء من يفعل ذلك منكم إلا خزي} [البقرة: 85].

QASHANI:2:113-114/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:113-114/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:113-114/r3.claim: God judges their disputes at the great Resurrection and the manifestation of essential unity at the Mahdi's emergence; a report says people recognize God in forms of their beliefs, then deny Him when He changes form, leaving only the unconditioned monotheist unveiled.
QASHANI:2:113-114/r3.anchor: إن الله يتجلى لعباده في صورة معتقداتهم فيعرفونه

QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r1.claim: The mosques are hearts, the places where God is known and worshipped through annihilation of the self in the divine essence; the Greatest Name manifests there with all attributes, or a particular name manifests the perfection suited to each heart's capacity.
QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r1.anchor: مواضع سجود الله التي هي القلوب التي يعرف فيها فيسجد بالفناء الذاتي

QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r2.claim: The special divine name is the Greatest Name, whose manifestation is the essence with all attributes, or the particular name and perfection required by the heart's preparedness.
QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r2.anchor: لا يتجلى بهذا الاسم إلا في القلب، وهو التجلي بالذات مع جميع الصفات أو اسمه المخصوص بكل واحد منها

QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r3.claim: Ruining hearts means clouding them with cold fanaticism and overpowering desires, and barring prepared people through turmoil and conflict among soul powers, satanic promptings, and illusion.
QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r3.anchor: بتكديرها بالتعصبات الباردة وغلبة واستيلاء التمنيات عليها، ومنع أهلها المستعدين عنها بالهرج والمرج

QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r4.claim: Those who enter the hearts should come humbled and broken before the manifest theophany of the Real.

QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r5.claim: Their worldly disgrace is exposure and humiliation as their religion and belief are invalidated by the true religion and they are defeated and regretful.
QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r5.anchor: افتضاح وذلة بظهور بطلان دينهم ومعتقدهم، وفسخه بدين الحق

QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:113-114#2/r6.claim: Their great afterlife punishment is being veiled from God by their religion.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:113-114/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:113-114/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:113-114/r6.claim: The mosques meant are Jerusalem and its sanctuaries; the verse was revealed concerning the Romans who destroyed Jerusalem.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:113-114/r6.anchor: { ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله } يعني: بيت المقدس ومحاريبه. نزلت في أهل الروم حين خربوا بيت المقدس

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:113-114/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:113-114/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:113-114/r7.claim: Those referred to are the Romans.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:113-114/r7.anchor: { أولئك } يعني: أهل الروم { ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:113-114/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:113-114/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:113-114/r8.claim: After Muslims rebuilt Jerusalem, a Roman entering it would fear being discovered and killed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:113-114/r8.anchor: لم يدخل بيت المقدس بعد أن عمره المسلمون رومي إلا خائفا لو علم به قتل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:113-114/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:113-114/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:113-114/r9.claim: Worldly disgrace means execution for a belligerent and jizya for a protected non-Muslim.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:113-114/r9.anchor: { لهم في الدنيا خزي } يعني: القتل للحربي، والجزية للذمي.

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r1.claim: The verse condemns those who block God's remembrance in mosques or work to ruin, disable, or repurpose them; such people have no relation to Paradise.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r1.anchor: Allah’ın mescidlerini içlerinde ism-i ilâhî zikredilmekten men‘eden

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r2.claim: Zulm is putting something outside its rightful place; the farther it is displaced, and the more sacred it is, the greater the injustice.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r2.anchor: Her şeyin hakkı, lâyık olduğu mevki‘e konulmak, zulüm de bir şeyi mevzi‘inin gayriye koymaktır.

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r3.claim: Attacking mosques violates the rights of God, the mosques, and people, and opens perpetrators to every kind of wrongdoing.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r3.anchor: hem Allah’ın, hem mescidlerin, hem de insanların

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r4.claim: Shirk is the greatest injustice; other verses use the same rhetorical question to say no greater rank of injustice exists.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r4.anchor: Nitekim وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r5.claim: God's mosques applies generally to every mosque, without exception.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r5.anchor: مَسَٰجِدَ ٱللَّهِ terkîbi hiçbir istisnası olmayarak bütün mescidlere şâmildir ve âyetin hükmü umûmîdir.

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r6.speaker: Cumhûr-i müfessirîn
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r6.claim: The majority of exegetes identify the original occasion as the Temple's destruction and say the verse concerns Romans and Christians.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r6.anchor: Cumhûr-i müfessirînin beyânına göre asıl sebeb-i nüzul, Beyt-i Makdis’in tahrîbi meselesi olup âyet Rum ve Nasârâ hakkındadır.

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r7.speaker: Bazı müfessirîn
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r7.claim: Some exegetes instead say the verse concerns the polytheists.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r7.anchor: Bazı müfessirîn müşrikler hakkında olduğunu da beyan etmişlerdir.

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r8.claim: Elmalılı prefers that the verse encompass both Christians and polytheists because of their shared polytheistic traits and participation in mosque persecution; Roman Christians remain the principal target.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r8.anchor: En doğrusu her ikisi, yani Nasârâ’nın müşrikîn ile müşterek bulundukları hısâl-i şirk hakkındadır.

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r9.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Titus attacked Jerusalem, killed its people, enslaved their descendants, burned the Torah, destroyed the Temple, and left slaughtered pigs and carcasses inside.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r9.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretlerinden rivayet olunduğu vechile “Roma kayserlerinden Titos Kudüs’e hücum edip ahâlisini katl eylemiş, zürriyetlerini esir almış, Tevrat’ı yakmış, Beyt-i Makdis’i tahrip etmiş

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r10.claim: Historical accounts say Nebuchadnezzar first devastated the Temple and ended the Israelite state; Persian Ardashir Bahman later rebuilt it.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r10.anchor: Tarihlerin beyânına göre Beyt-i Makdis ilk defa Buhtunassar tarafından pek fecî bir surette tahrip edilmiş ve Benî İsrâil devletine nihâyet verilmiş idi.

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r11.claim: After the Persian reconstruction Israelites regrouped under Persian rule, then came under Greek and Roman rule; Zechariah and John were martyred in that period.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r11.anchor: Benî İsrâil yine toplanmış ve İran tâbiiyetinde bir hükûmet-i mahalliyeye nâil olmuştu, bilâhare Yunanlıların ve daha sonra Romalıların idaresine geçtiler

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r12.claim: About forty years after Jesus' ascension, the Temple's second destruction began under Vespasian, Nero's successor, and was completed by Titus.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r12.anchor: Hazret-i Îsâ’nın ‘urûcundan kırk sene kadar sonra da Kudüs’ün ve Beyt-i Makdis’in ikinci tahrîbi vâki‘oldu.

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r13.claim: Titus massacred Jerusalem's inhabitants, enslaved their children, plundered and destroyed the city and Temple, burned its books, and ended Israelite rule; Roman histories blame Israelite rebellion and excess.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r13.anchor: Titus da buraya şiddetle hücum ederek gizlenip kaçabilenlerden mâ‘adâ ahâlisini Yahudî olsun Hıristiyan olsun hep katliam ve zürriyetlerini tamamen esir etmiş

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r14.claim: Elmalılı says Israel's punishment accords with the divine account that they disbelieved, killed prophets unjustly, disobeyed, and transgressed.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r14.anchor: beyân-ı ilâhîsi de bunu göstermiş idi.

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r15.claim: Ibn al-Athir says Emperor Hadrian, after sensing opposition, massacred many Jewish and Christian residents and destroyed the Temple for the last time.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r15.anchor: İbn Esîr’in Târîh-i Kâmil’de beyânına göre

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r16.claim: Hadrian rebuilt Jerusalem seven or eight years later, settled Romans and Greeks there, and erected a large statue to Venus; the city was renamed Ilya, reportedly meaning House of the Lord.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r16.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh yedi sekiz sene sonra şehri imar etmiş, Rum’dan, Yunan’dan birçok halk iskân eylemiş ve Zühre nâmına bir de büyük heykel bina etmiş

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r17.claim: Helena went to Jerusalem to find the cross Christians believed Jesus was crucified on and buried with; its discovery became the Christian Feast of the Cross.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r17.anchor: Roma’da Nasraniyet’i kabul ve ilan eden İstanbul bânîsi Kostantin’in anası Hilana (Eleni) Nasârâca Hazret-i Îsâ’nın üzerinde asıldığı

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r18.claim: Elmalılı says Helena built the Holy Sepulchre over Jesus's supposed tomb, ordered the Temple remains cleared and rubbish dumped there, and Christians kept it a refuse heap and barred worship until Umar's time.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r18.anchor: o zamandan Hazret-i Ömer zamanına kadar Nasârâ orayı mezbele yapmışlar, orada Allah’a ibadet ve dua etmek isteyenleri men‘eylemişlerdi.

ELMALILI:2:114-115/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r19.claim: Umar found the site as a rubbish heap; Muslims then built al-Aqsa Mosque there.
ELMALILI:2:114-115/r19.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer orayı mezbele halinde bulmuştu ve o zaman Mescid-i Aksâ Müslümanlar tarafından bina edilmiş idi.

ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r1.claim: Elmalılı concludes that Roman Christians joined and prolonged the Chaldean and Roman polytheists' persecution of the Temple, bearing greater responsibility; Jews also helped cause or failed to prevent its ruin.
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r1.anchor: ve hatta daha devamlı bir surette iştirak etmişler

ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r2.claim: The verse summarizes these historical injustices, especially condemning Christians who shared in them, and generalizes reverence to all mosques.
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r2.anchor: İşte bütün bu târihî mezâlimi icmal eden bu âyet-i kerîme bilhassa Nasârâ’nın müşriklere iştirak ettikleri bu zulme

ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r3.claim: Its scope includes Jews, Christians, and polytheists, including Meccan polytheists barring the Prophet and Muslims from the Kaaba, and every past or future ban or destruction of a mosque.
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r3.anchor: Ve binâen‘aleyh siyâk-ı âyet hem Yahudî ve hem Nasârâ’ya

ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r4.claim: The oppressors have no right to enter those mosques except fearfully; if they enter, they should tremble for their lives, and God will eventually enforce this.
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r4.anchor: Bunların o mescidlere korka korka girmeden başka hakk-ı duhulleri yoktur.

ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r5.claim: Elmalılı sees the prophecy fulfilled when Jerusalem left Roman control, the Temple was rebuilt, and former oppressors could enter only fearfully; he draws a lesson for Muslims today.
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r5.anchor: Nitekim Kur’ân’ın bu mucizesi zuhur etmiş, Kudüs Rumların elinden çıkmış, Beyt-i Makdis imar olunmuş

ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r6.claim: Worldly disgrace means great calamity and deprivation: the perpetrators will lose state, strength, and power, and fall into subjection and ruin.
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r6.anchor: o men‘ü zulmü yaptıran devletlerini, kuvvet ü şevketlerini zâyi‘edecek, mahkûmiyete düşecek, perişan olacaklardır.

ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r7.speaker: Süddî
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r7.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the worldly disgrace as the loss of Constantinople, the conquest of Istanbul.
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r7.anchor: Şâyân-ı dikkattir ki Süddî tefsîrinde bu hızy u felâketten murad Kostantiniye şehrinin ellerinden çıkması

ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r8.claim: Because al-Suddi's interpretation and its transmission in early authorities predate the conquest by centuries, Elmalılı treats it as a prophetic miracle transmitted by report.
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r8.anchor: Bunlar İstanbul’un fethinden asırlarca mukaddem yazılmış olduğuna ve hele eslâf-ı müfessirînden olan Süddî beş altı asır mukaddem bulunduğuna

ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r9.claim: In addition to worldly disgrace, these oppressors face immense afterlife punishment, which God will impose on Judgment Day.
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r9.anchor: bunlara dünyadaki o hızy u felâketten başka âhirette de pek büyük bir azab vardır.

ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r10.claim: Those barred from mosques and sincere worship should not despair or abandon God and worship; their opponents' claim to exclusive Paradise is unjust.
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r10.anchor: me’yus olmamalı, ve o mescidlerden men‘edildik diye Allah’tan

ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r21.claim: Elmalılı turns from the mosque oppressors to the Jews and Christians' further likeness to polytheists, introducing the following discussion.
ELMALILI:2:114-115#2/r21.anchor: bunların müşriklere iştirâki sade bu kadar da değil daha var, dinleyiniz:

QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r1.claim: The unjust person who ruins worship’s sanctuaries destroys the worshippers’ souls, which are the homes of worship.
QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r1.anchor: الظالم من خرب أوطان العبادة بالشهوات

QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r2.claim: Ruining the homes of gnosis means spoiling the knowers’ hearts through wishes and attachments.

QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r3.claim: Ruining the homes of love means corrupting the spirits of those who experience it through self-interests and complacent intimacy.

QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r4.claim: Ruining the homes of witnessing means diverting the unifiers’ secrets toward attention to devotional acts.
QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r4.anchor: وخرب أوطان المشاهدات بالالتفات إلى القربات

QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r5.claim: For people of spiritual allusion, worldly disgrace is the abasement of veiling, and afterlife punishment is being denied the degrees of nearness.
QUSHAYRI:v1p62/r5.anchor: لأهل الإشارة خزي الدنيا بذل الحجاب

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r1.claim: Masjid literally means a place of prostration and technically denotes a place set aside for Muslims' prayer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r1.anchor: Sözlükte “secde edilen yer” anlamına gelen mescid (çoğulu mesâcid) terim olarak, müslümanların namaz kılmalarına ayrılmış mekânı ifade eder.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r2.speaker: hadith
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r2.claim: A hadith says a believer is nearest to God while prostrating; because prostration is prayer's chief pillar and symbolizes prayer, mosques take their name from prostration.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r2.anchor: bir hadise göre müminin Allah’a en yakın bulunduğu an olduğu (Müslim, “Salât”, 215; Nesâî, “Mevâk^t”, 35)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r3.claim: Jami means a gathering place and originally referred to large mosques for Friday prayer; later Turkish usage called neighborhood prayer houses masjids and all large mosques, including those for daily prayers, jami.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r3.anchor: Sözlükte “toplayan, bir araya getiren” anlamına gelen cami ismi ise başlangıçta sadece cuma namazlarının kılındığı büyük mescidleri ifade ederken

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r4.claim: Musalla denotes open spaces for Eid and funeral prayers; namazgah denotes roadside prayer places built open-air.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r4.anchor: Ayrıca bayram ve cenaze namazlarının kılındığı açık alanlara musallâ, yol boylarında üstü açık olarak inşa edilen mescidlere de namazgâh denilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r5.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r5.claim: Tabari prefers identifying the group working to ruin the temples as Christians, who destroyed Jerusalem's Temple of Solomon with Nebuchadnezzar's help and later prevented Israelites from worshipping there.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r5.anchor: Taberî, âyette mescidlerin harap olması için çalıştıkları bildirilen zümrenin hıristiyanlar olduğunu, zira onların Kudüs’teki Beytülmakdis’i (Süleyman Mâbedi) tahrip ettiklerini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r6.claim: The author rejects the Christian identification: Nebuchadnezzar destroyed Jerusalem's temple in 586 BCE, long before Jesus and Christianity, and Christians also revered it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r6.anchor: Buhtunnasr’ın Kudüs’ü işgal ederek Beytülmakdis’i yıktırması Hz. Îsâ’dan ve dolayısıyla hıristiyanlardan çok önce (m. ö. 586) vuku bulduğu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r7.claim: The Temple of Jerusalem was also burned during Rome's 70 CE siege of Jerusalem to suppress a Jewish revolt.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r7.anchor: Romalılar’ın, yahudi ayaklanmasını bastırmak üzere 70 yılında Kudüs’ü kuşatmaları sırasında Beytülmakdis de yanmıştı.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r8.claim: Another view identifies the group as Meccan polytheists who barred the Prophet and Muslims from the Sacred Mosque at Hudaybiyya.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r8.anchor: müşriklerin Hudeybiye Gazvesi sırasında Hz. Peygamber’in ve yanındaki müslümanların Mescid-i Harâm’a girmelerini engellemelerinin kastedildiği yolunda bir görüş daha varsa da (bk. Taberî, I, 499; Râzî, IV, 9, 10)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r9.claim: The author considers that view inaccurate because the verse also speaks of ruining mosques, while Arabs always respected the Sacred Mosque.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r9.anchor: Zira bu âyette, bahsedilen kimselerin mescidleri harap etmeye çalışmalarından da söz edilmektedir. Halbuki Araplar Mescid-i Harâm’a daima saygı göstermişlerdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r10.speaker: Reşîd Rızâ
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r10.claim: Rida's contextual reading takes the temple-destroyers as Roman pagans who burned Solomon's Temple and those barring God's name as Meccan pagans preventing worship at the Sacred Mosque.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r10.anchor: Allah’ın mescidlerinde O’nun adının anılmasına engel olan” ifadesiyle de müslümanların Mescid-i Harâm’a girip ibadet etmelerini engelleyen Mekkeli putperestlerin kastedildiği düşünülebilir (Reşîd Rızâ, I, 431).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r11.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r11.claim: After four interpretations, Razi favors a fifth: Jews could not bear Muslims praying toward the Kaaba, urged polytheists to ruin it, and also worked to destroy the Prophet's Mosque in Medina.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r11.anchor: Fahreddin er-Râzî, bu hususta dört yorum zikrettikten sonra beşinci bir yoruma yer vermekte ve bunu daha güçlü bulmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r12.claim: Beyond proposed historical referents, the verse condemns all hostility to worship and places of worship in any era, including physical or spiritual ruin and any attempt to make them unusable.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r12.anchor: Bu tür yorumlar, âyette mutlak mânada ibadet ve mâbed düşmanlığının hedef alındığını düşünmemize de engel değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r13.claim: Worship keeps a person's relationship with the Creator and consciousness of servitude alive; temples are sacred places established to serve that function, so the verse's core message is their inviolability and freedom of worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r13.anchor: Zira ibadet, insanın yaratıcısıyla ilişkisini sağlamada ve bu suretle onda kulluk bilincini canlı ve sürekli kılmada en önemli işleve sahip düzenli davranış biçimleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r14.claim: The Quran extends respect to churches and synagogues alongside mosques where God's name is invoked, pointing to 22:40.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r14.anchor: Nitekim bu temel yaklaşım dolayısıyla Kur’an, “içinde Allah’ın isminin anıldığı” (ibadetlerin yapıldığı) mescidlerle birlikte kiliselere ve havralara da saygı gösterilmesi gerektiğine işaret etmiştir (Hac 22/40).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r15.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r15.claim: The Prophet allowed a Christian delegation from Najran to enter the Medina Mosque and perform their worship according to their own religion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r15.anchor: Hz. Peygamber, Necranlı bir hıristiyan heyetinin Medine Mescidi’ne girerek burada kendi dinlerine göre âyin yapmalarına bile izin vermiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r16.claim: Those who prevent worship in mosques and work to destroy them are called the greatest wrongdoers; the commentary refers to 2:54 for the Quranic meaning of wrongdoing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r16.anchor: ibadet edilmesine engel olan ve bu mukaddes mekânların tahribine çalışanları zalimlerin en zalimi saymış (zulüm teriminin Kur’anî anlamı için bk. Bakara 2/54)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r17.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r17.claim: Razi reads their fearful entry as fear of believers' strength and capture; the commentary infers that believers must be strong and worship places secured against attack or obstruction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r17.anchor: onların mescidlere, ancak müminlerin gücünden korkarak, onlar tarafından yakalanmaktan korkup çekinerek girebileceklerine (Râzî, IV, 11)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r18.claim: For the phrase “humiliation in this world,” the commentary directs readers to 2:85.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:114/r18.anchor: (“dünyada rezillik” ifadesinin açıklaması için bk. Bakara 2/85).

BURHAN:v1p44/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p44/r7.speaker: أبو الحسين الدهان
BURHAN:v1p44/r7.claim: Al-Dahhān, as quoted by al-Juwaynī, connects the verse to the prior mention of Jerusalem's destruction: do not be deterred; face the qibla, for east and west belong to God.
BURHAN:v1p44/r7.anchor: سمعت أبا الحسين الدهان يقول وجه اتصالها هو أن ذكر تخريب بيت المقدس قد سبق

BURHAN:v4p74/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p74/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p74/r1.claim: One reconciliation assigns each ومن أظلم claim to its own predicate: no one among mosque-preventers is more unjust than its described offender, and likewise for each other class.
BURHAN:v4p74/r1.anchor: تخصيص كل واحد في هذه المواضع بمعنى صلته فكانه قال لا أحد من المانعين أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله

BURHAN:v4p74/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p74/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p74/r2.claim: A second view makes the claim relative to precedence: each group was the first to commit its kind of offense, so later followers do not exceed it in that offense.
BURHAN:v4p74/r2.anchor: حكم عليهم بانهم اظلم ممن جاء بعدهم سالكا طريقتهم

BURHAN:v4p74/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p74/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
BURHAN:v4p74/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān argues that denying anyone “more unjust” does not deny that others are unjust; it permits equality among those described and so avoids contradiction.
BURHAN:v4p74/r3.anchor: وادعى الشيخ أبو حيان الصواب ونفى الاظلمية لايستدعى نفي الظالمية

BURHAN:v4p74/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p74/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
BURHAN:v4p74/r4.claim: On this account the cited offenders are all disbelievers, equal in ultimate injustice because their different offenses converge on unbelief; a disbeliever can still be called more unjust than a sinful believer.
BURHAN:v4p74/r4.anchor: فهم متساوون في الاظلمية وان اختلفت طرق الاظلمية

BURHAN:v3p211/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p211/r1.speaker: الواحدي
BURHAN:v3p211/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī reports that the Syrian codices' reading of Ibn ʿĀmir omits the waw before قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا because its connection to the preceding mosque-preventer passage is already clear.
BURHAN:v3p211/r1.anchor: وقال الواحدي في قوله تعالى ﴿ قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا ﴾ 2 آية البقرة في مصاحف الشام بغير واو

BURHAN:v4p76/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p76/r1.speaker: بعض مشايخنا
BURHAN:v4p76/r1.claim: A teacher objects that the problem is not denial of all injustice but the claim that no one is more unjust than each offender; those repeated claims then appear to conflict.
BURHAN:v4p76/r1.anchor: لم يدع القائل نفي الظالمية فيقيم الشيخ الدليل على ثبوتها وانما دعواه إن ومن اظلم ممن منع مثلا

BURHAN:v4p76/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p76/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p76/r2.claim: The sheikh's reading is correct only by limiting each verse through the others: each denies comparative injustice to some offenders while another verse affirms it for them.
BURHAN:v4p76/r2.anchor: وقول الشيخ إن المعنى لا أحد اظلم ممن منع وممن ذكر صحيح ولكن لم يستفد ذلك إلا من جهة التخصيص

BURHAN:v4p76/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p76/r3.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
BURHAN:v4p76/r3.claim: Some later scholars say a literal denial of any more unjust offender entails either equal maximal injustice for all or separate maximality for each offense, both of which they find problematic.
BURHAN:v4p76/r3.anchor: طريقة بعض المتأخرين فقال متى قدرنا لا أحد اظلم لزم

BURHAN:v4p76/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p76/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p76/r4.claim: Zarkashī prefers keeping the interrogative force as figurative hyperbole: the act is so appalling that nothing seems to surpass it, without asserting a literal universal ranking.
BURHAN:v4p76/r4.anchor: وهنا معنى ثالث وهو امكن في المعنى وسالم عن الاعتراض وهو الوقوف مع مدلول اللفظ من الاستفهام

ITQAN:v3p79/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p79/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p79/r2.claim: Repeated claims that no one is more unjust than the fabricator, rejecter, or mosque-prohibitor seem contradictory if each superlative means absolutely that no one else is as unjust.

ITQAN:v3p79/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p79/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p79/r3.claim: One answer restricts each superlative to the class named by its relative clause: among adversaries, fabricators, or mosque-prohibitors, none is more unjust than the specified offender.
ITQAN:v3p79/r3.anchor: منها تخصيص كل موضع بمعنى صلته أي لا أحد من المعاندين أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله

ITQAN:v3p79/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p79/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p79/r4.claim: A second answer makes the offender worst because no one had preceded them in that offense; this ultimately reduces to the first answer’s restriction by offense.
ITQAN:v3p79/r4.anchor: ومنها أن التخصيص بالنسبة إلى السبق لما لم يسبق أحد إلى مثله حكم عليهم بأنهم أظلم ممن جاء بعدهم

ITQAN:v3p79/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p79/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ITQAN:v3p79/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan’s preferred answer is that denying anyone is ‘more unjust’ does not deny that others are unjust; the listed offenders can be equal in extreme injustice without one exceeding another.
ITQAN:v3p79/r5.anchor: وادعى أبو حيان أنه الصواب أن نفي الأظلمية لا يستدعي نفي الظالمية لأن نفي المقيد لا يدل على نفي المطلق

ITQAN:v3p295/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p295/r5.speaker: أبو الحسن الدهان
