ITQAN:v3p295/r5.claim: Al-Dahhan links 2:115 to the earlier mention of Jerusalem's destruction: believers should not be distressed, since east and west belong to God.
ITQAN:v3p295/r5.anchor: سمعت أبا الحسن الدهان بقول وجه اتصاله هو أن أن ذكر تخريب بيت المقدس قد سبق

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p25/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p25/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p25/r2.claim: A report through Ibn Abbas says Quraysh prevented the Prophet from praying at the Kaaba in the Sacred Mosque, occasioning the verse.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p25/r2.anchor: أن قريشا منعوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الصلاة عند الكعبة في المسجد الحرام

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p25/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p25/r3.speaker: زيد
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p25/r3.claim: Zayd says the verse concerns the polytheists who barred the Messenger from entering Mecca at al-Hudaybiya.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p25/r3.anchor: عن زيد قال نزلت في المشركين حين صدوا رسول الله عن مكة يوم الحديبية

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p36/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p36/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p36/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Kalbi, says the verse concerned Titus the Roman and his Christian forces, who killed Israelite fighters, captured their children, burned the Torah, and desecrated and ruined Jerusalem's Temple.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p36/r1.anchor: وقذفوا فيه الجيف. وهذا قول ابن عباس في رواية الكلبي.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p36/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p36/r2.speaker: قتادة والسدي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p36/r2.claim: Qatada and al-Suddi identify the perpetrators as Nebuchadnezzar and his companions, who ruined Jerusalem with assistance from Roman Christians.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p36/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة والسدي: هو بختنصر وأصحابه غزوا اليهود وخربوا بيت المقدس، وأعانتهم على ذلك النصارى من أهل الروم.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p36/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p36/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p36/r3.claim: In the report through Ata, the verse concerns Meccan polytheists preventing Muslims from remembering God in the Sacred Mosque.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p36/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء. نزلت في مشركي أهل مكة ومنعهم المسلمين من ذكر الله تعالى في المسجد الحرام.

DAMGHANI:v1p231/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p231/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p231/r3.claim: In 2:114, God's masājid specifically refers to the Temple in Jerusalem.
DAMGHANI:v1p231/r3.anchor: ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r1.claim: A masjid is a place of prostration; conventionally it is an Islamic building for prayer, analogous to a church for Jews and a sales (church) for Christians.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r1.anchor: المسجد : اسم لموضع السجود . وجمعه : مساجد

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r2.claim: The first Qur'anic referent is the Jerusalem sanctuary, in the verse about preventing God's name from being mentioned in His mosques.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r2.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن المسجد في القرآن على سبعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r3.claim: The second referent is the Sacred Mosque, cited in two verses about the polytheists not maintaining God's mosques and about the Sacred Mosque itself.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r3.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن المسجد في القرآن على سبعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r4.claim: A third referent is the Prophet's Mosque in Medina, while another view identifies the cited mosque as Quba.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r4.anchor: والثالث : مسجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم . ومنه قوله تعالى في براءة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r5.speaker: قيل
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r5.claim: An alternative identification of the mosque founded on piety is the mosque of Quba.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r6.claim: A fourth referent is the Mosque of Dhirar, the mosque built to cause harm and disbelief.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r6.anchor: والرابع : مسجد الضرار . ومنه قوله تعالى في براءة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r7.claim: A fifth referent is Mecca and its sanctuary, in passages about the Sacred Mosque and the expulsion of its people or barring access to it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r7.anchor: والخامس : مكة والحرم . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r8.claim: A sixth sense is all mosques, in the verse listing monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques that would otherwise be demolished.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r8.anchor: والسادس : [ جميع ] المساجد . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحج

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r9.claim: A seventh sense is the human limbs on which one prostrates, applied to the mosques belonging to God; some exegetes group this with the preceding all-mosques sense.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p567/r9.anchor: والسابع : أعضاء الإنسان التي يسجد عليها . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة الجن

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p61#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p61#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p61#2/r1.claim: He says the passage was revealed about the Romans after they prevailed over Jerusalem and ruined it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p61#2/r1.anchor: نزلت في "الروم" حين ظهروا على "بيت المقدس" (4) فخربوه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p61#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p61#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p61#2/r2.claim: The Romans would never enter it except in fear.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p61#2/r2.anchor: فلا يدخله أحد أبدا منهم إلا خائف.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p61#2/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p61#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p61#2/r4.claim: The commentators report that their city, Rome, would be conquered.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p61#2/r4.anchor: ذكر المفسرون: أنه فتح مدينتهم رومية.

NAHHAS:v1p256/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p256/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p256/r12.claim: The opening is a subject-predicate construction meaning “and who is more unjust?”
NAHHAS:v1p256/r12.anchor: ابتداء وخبر أي وأي أحد أظلم

NAHHAS:v1p256/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p256/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p256/r13.claim: An may be an accusative substitute for masājid; alternatively, min is understood before it, omitted because the phrase is long or its verb makes the relation clear.
NAHHAS:v1p256/r13.anchor: أن في موضع نصب على البدل من مساجد ويجوز أن يكون التقدير من أن يذكر

NAHHAS:v1p256/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p256/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p256/r14.anchor: ( وسعى ) معطوف على منع ( أولئك ) مبتدأ والجملة خبر

NAHHAS:v1p256/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p256/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p256/r15.claim: Ulāʾika is the subject, with its following clause as predicate; khāʾifīna is circumstantial.
NAHHAS:v1p256/r15.anchor: ( أولئك ) مبتدأ والجملة خبر ( خائفين ) حال ( لهم في الدنيا خزي )

NAHHAS:v1p256/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p256/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p256/r16.claim: Khizyun is raised as a subject; another parse treats the phrase as expressing what is due or obligatory.
NAHHAS:v1p256/r16.anchor: ( لهم في الدنيا خزي ) رفع بابتداء وإن شئت على معنى وجب

SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r1.claim: من is an interrogative subject and أظلم its elative predicate; the question means no one is more unjust.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r1.anchor: " من " استفهام في محل رفع بالابتداء، و " أظلم " أفعل تفضيل خبره

SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r2.claim: The same formula concerns fabricating lies about God, rejecting His signs, and lying about Him, raising how each can be the most unjust.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r2.anchor: ولما كان المعنى على ذلك أورد بعض الناس سؤالا: وهو أن هذه الصيغة قد تكررت في القرآن

SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r3.speaker: السائل
SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r3.claim: One answer restricts each superlative to its class: among preventers, forgers, and liars, no one exceeds the named offender in that class.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r3.anchor: أحدها: - ذكره هذا السائل - وهو أن يخص كل واحد بمعنى صلته

SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r4.claim: A second answer says they are worst because they were first to commit such acts; later followers do not surpass those who initiated the practice.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r4.anchor: الثاني: أن التخصيص يكون بالنسبة إلى السبق، لما لم يسبق أحد إلى مثله

SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r5.claim: A third answer says denying anyone greater injustice does not deny injustice itself: the groups may tie for maximal injustice despite different means.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114/r5.anchor: الثالث: أن هذا نفي للأظلمية، ونفي الأظلمية لا يستدعي نفي الظالمية

SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r1.claim: من may be relative, leaving its following clause without a syntactic position, or descriptive, making the clause a genitive adjective.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r1.anchor: و " من " يجوز أن تكون موصولة فلا محل للجملة بعدها، وأن تكون موصوفة

SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r2.claim: مساجد is the first object of منع and a plural of مسجد, a place of prostration; its kasra pattern is irregular where fatḥa is expected, though مسجد with fatḥa is heard and jīm may become yāʾ in مسيد.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r2.anchor: و " مساجد " مفعول أول لمنع، وهي جمع مسجد وهو اسم مكان السجود

SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r3.claim: أن يذكر may be the second object of منع, as in منعته كذا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r3.anchor: أنه مفعول ثان لمنع، تقول: منعته كذا

SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r4.claim: It may instead express purpose, meaning lest His name be mentioned; the shaykh says this needs an omitted مضاف such as entering God's mosques.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r4.anchor: أنه مفعول من أجله أي: كراهة أن يذكر

SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r5.claim: A third analysis makes أن يذكر an appositive of encompassment to مساجد: preventing mention of His name there.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r5.anchor: أنه بدل اشتمال من " مساجد " ، أي: منع ذكر اسمه فيها

SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r6.claim: A fourth analysis deletes a preposition, with الأصل من أن يذكر; the usual positions allow accusative or genitive.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r6.anchor: أنه على إسقاط حرف الجر، والأصل: من أن يذكر

SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqāʾ treats خراب as an اسم مصدر meaning التخريب, annexed to its object because it operates like a verb; the cited عطائك illustrates verbal-noun operation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r8.anchor: هو اسم مصدر بمعنى التخريب كالسلام بمعنى التسليم، وأضيف اسم المصدر لمفعوله

SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r9.claim: Another analysis takes خراب as verbal noun of خرب المكان يخرب, meaning seeking the place itself be ruined through lack of maintenance; it is annexed to its subject, as in منزل خراب and Ghaylān's الخرب.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#2/r9.anchor: هو مصدر خرب المكان يخرب خرابا، فالمعنى: سعى في أن تخرب هي بنفسها

SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r1.claim: لهم is the fronted predicate of كان, and أن يدخلوها its subject as an infinitive phrase; the clause predicates أولئك.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r1.anchor: مقدم على اسمها، واسمها " أن يدخلوها " لأنه في تأويل المصدر

SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r2.claim: خائفين is a حال of the subject of يدخلوها; the exception excludes every state of entry except fear.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r2.anchor: حال من فاعل " يدخلوها " ، وهذا استثناء مفرغ من الأحوال

SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r3.speaker: أبي
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r3.claim: Ubayy reads خيفا, plural of خائف like ضرب for ضارب; its original is خوف like صوم, with both wāws replaced by yāʾs as in صوم/صيم.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبي " خيفا " وهو جمع خائف، كضارب وضرب

SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r4.claim: The construction follows the singular form of من in منع and سعى, then its plural sense in أولئك and what follows.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r4.anchor: فأفرد في قوله: " منع، وسعى " وعلى معناها ثانيا

SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r5.claim: لهم في الدنيا خزي and what follows are independent; they cannot be حال because disgrace is constant, not limited to mosque entry.
SAMIN-DURR:2:114#3/r5.anchor: هذه الجملة وما بعدها لا محل لها لاستئنافها عما قبلها

ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r1.claim: Man is nominative despite its interrogative form, with the sense who is more unjust; aẓlam is the predicate of the initial clause.
ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r1.anchor: موضع (من) رفع ولفظها لفظ استفهام، المعنى: وأي أحد أظلم ممن منع

ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r2.claim: The clause an yudhkara is accusative as an appositive to masājid Allāh, meaning preventing God's name from being mentioned in the mosques.
ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r2.anchor: وموضع أن نصب على البدل من مساجد الله، المعنى: ومن أظلم ممن منع أن يذكر في مساجد الله اسمه

ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r3.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r3.claim: One exegetical identification is the Romans, who entered and ruined Jerusalem's sanctuary.
ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r3.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن هذا يعني به الروم، لأنهم كانوا دخلوا بيت المقدس وخربوه

ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r4.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r4.claim: Another identification is the Meccan polytheists, who sought to stop Muslims from remembering God in the Sacred Mosque.
ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r4.anchor: وقيل يعني به مشركو مكة لأنهم سعوا في منع المسلمين من ذكر الله في المسجد الحرام

ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r5.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r5.claim: Some linguists apply the verse to all unbelievers opposing Islam and preventing prayer throughout the mosques; any place of worship is a mosque, as the Prophet's report that earth was made a mosque and purification indicates.
ZAJJAJ:v1p195#2/r5.anchor: زعم أنه يعني به جميع الكفار الذين تظاهروا على الإسلام، ومنعوا جملة المساجد

ZAJJAJ:v1p196/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p196/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p196/r1.claim: God says the Muslim community will prevail over its opponents until no opponent can enter its mosques except in fear.
ZAJJAJ:v1p196/r1.anchor: أعلم الله في هذه الآية أن أمر المسلمين يظهر على جميع من خالفهم حتى لا يمكن دخول مخالف إلى مساجدهم إلا خائفا

ZAJJAJ:v1p196/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p196/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p196/r2.claim: Khizyun can be nominative as a new subject or as the subject of an implied verb associated with lahum; the sense is that humiliation is due them.
ZAJJAJ:v1p196/r2.anchor: يرتفع (خزي) من وجهتين: إحداهما الابتداء، والأخرى الفعل الذي ينوب عنه (لهم).

ZAJJAJ:v1p196/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p196/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p196/r3.claim: Their worldly humiliation is being killed if they are at war and charged jizya if they are protected non-Muslims.
ZAJJAJ:v1p196/r3.anchor: والخزي الذي لهم في الدنيا، أن يقتلوا إن كانوا حربا، ويجزوا إن كانوا ذمة

ZAJJAJ:v1p196/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p196/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p196/r4.claim: The punishment is described as great because they are the most unjust, as the verse's opening states.
ZAJJAJ:v1p196/r4.anchor: وجعل لهم عظيم العذاب لأنهم أظلم من ظلم لقوله: (ومن أظلم ممن منع).

ASAD-NOTES:2:114#n95/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:114#n95/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:114#n95/r1.claim: Islam requires respect and protection for every God-centered religion's house of worship despite doctrinal disagreement; blocking others from worship is sacrilege.
ASAD-NOTES:2:114#n95/r1.anchor: every religion which has belief in God as its focal point must be accorded full respect

ASAD-NOTES:2:114#n95/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:114#n95/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:114#n95/r2.claim: As an illustration, the Prophet let the Christian deputation from Najran enter his mosque and perform its rites there, despite their beliefs about Jesus and Mary conflicting with Islam.
ASAD-NOTES:2:114#n95/r2.anchor: They were given free access to the Prophet's mosque, and with his full consent celebrated their religious rites there

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f1.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f1.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f1.claim: Khalafallah’s book followed al-Khuli’s interpretive approach and became a prominent source of controversy among the Amin group.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f1.anchor: فقد ترسم نهج الخولي في التفسير

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f2.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f2.speaker: نصر حامد أبو زيد
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f2.claim: Abu Zayd said he aimed to reconnect Qur’anic studies with literary and critical studies after modern conditions had separated them from heritage and its scientific methods.

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f3.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f3.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f3.claim: Both books stirred controversy, and their authors were accused of apostasy while public opinion was mobilized against them.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f3.anchor: وصار كلٌّ من الكتابين مثارًا للجدل

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f4.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f4.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f4.claim: The author places Khalafallah’s 1947 dissertation among three especially controversial Arabic books of the period; the committee rejected it and withheld his doctorate.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f4.anchor: ثلاثة كتب هي الأشد إثارة في الحياة الثقافية العربية في النصف الأول من القرن العشرين

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f5.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f5.speaker: محمد أحمد خلف الله
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f5.claim: Khalafallah argues that Qur’anic narratives should be studied as religious and literary texts, not historical documents: the Qur’an usually obscures time and place, since its aim is religious and social guidance that moves hearts and minds.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f5.anchor: يشرح محمد أحمد خلف الله منهجه في دراسة القصص القرآني

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f6.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f6.speaker: محمد أحمد خلف الله
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f6.claim: He says Qur’anic stories aim at admonition, not teaching history or establishing historical facts; readers should not infer what the Qur’an did not intend.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f6.anchor: ولقد قلت في الرسالة إن قصد القرآن من قصصه

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f7.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f7.speaker: محمد أحمد خلف الله
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f7.claim: Khalafallah allows that some Qur’anic stories may draw on myths without compromising revelation: the Qur’an rejects myths as proof of Muhammad’s authorship, and he surveys nine occurrences of asāṭīr.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f7.anchor: ولا يرى خلف الله بأسًا فيما ذهب إليه بعض المستشرقين

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f8.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f8.speaker: محمد أحمد خلف الله
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f8.claim: He treats Qur’anic narratives as parables and adduces the story of the town’s messengers and the wives of Noah and Lot as examples.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f8.anchor: يذهب خلف الله إلى أن القرآن الكريم إنما يورد هذه القصص

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f9.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f9.speaker: الفخر الرازي
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f9.claim: Al-Razi defines narrative as discourse that guides to religion, truth, and salvation; “truth” points to proofs for justice and prophethood.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f9.anchor: ينقل خلف الله رأيًا للفخر الرازي يبين فيه أغراض القصص في سياق تفسيره للآيتين

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f10.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f10.speaker: توفيق الحكيم
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f10.claim: Tawfiq al-Hakim recounts that some demanded the dissertation be burned before faculty and students, while others demanded Khalafallah’s dismissal.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f10.anchor: كما أشار إلى ذلك توفيق الحكيم بقوله

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f11.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f11.speaker: محمد أحمد خلف الله
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f11.claim: Khalafallah defines a literary story as imagined or reshaped events, including reordered, omitted, added, or exaggerated details that transform historical figures into fictional characters.

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f12.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f12.speaker: محمد الخضر حسين
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f12.claim: Khidr Husayn rejects applying that definition to Qur’anic stories: it suits human works for artistry or pleasure, whereas divine narratives are lessons, examples, and wisdom, not imaginative writing mixing truth with falsehood.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f12.anchor: ثم يرد عليه الشيخُ الخضر حسين بقوله

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f13.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f13.speaker: أحمد أمين
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f13.claim: Ahmad Amin’s report characterizes the dissertation as arguing that Qur’anic stories are artistic creation unconstrained by historical accuracy and that Muhammad was an artist in this sense.

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f14.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f14.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f14.claim: The author calls Ahmad Amin’s report severe and inflammatory, says it catered to official religious opinion and public taste, and attributes a major role in the dissertation’s rejection to it.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f14.anchor: وكان لهذا التقرير أثر كبير في رفض لجنة المناقشة للرسالة

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f15.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f15.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f15.claim: Al-Khuli stood by and praised Khalafallah after the doctorate was withheld; in the third-edition preface he said public prejudice had punished the thesis, which later became a rich contribution to Qur’anic inimitability, and commended its author’s sincerity.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f15.anchor: لم يشأ الشيخ أمين الخولي التنصل من اجتهاد تلميذه

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f16.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f16.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f16.claim: Al-Khuli said he would declare Khalafallah’s thesis true even if no one else in Egypt or the East supported it, accepting the threat of being cast into the fire to clear his conscience.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f16.anchor: كان إصرار أمين الخولي في الدفاع عن تلميذه

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f17.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f17.speaker: طه حسين
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f17.claim: Taha Hussein had earlier argued that Abraham and Ishmael’s appearance in the Torah and Qur’an does not by itself establish their historical existence.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f17.anchor: طه حسين قد سبق خلف الله

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f18.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f18.speaker: محمد عبده
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f18.claim: Muhammad Abduh held that Qur’anic stories serve admonition rather than history or belief in every ancient report; they recount good and bad beliefs, traditions, and customs so the narrative’s form can signal approval or condemnation.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f18.anchor: وقبل طه حسين تحدث الشيخ محمد عبده عن أغراض القصص القرآني فقال

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f19.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f19.speaker: محمد أحمد خلف الله
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f19.claim: To defend his approach, Khalafallah says Muhammad Abduh had already advanced it and cites al-Manar’s account of stories as lessons and signs of God’s ways, not detailed histories of peoples or places.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f19.anchor: بل سبقه إليه الشيخ محمد عبده كما ورد في تفسير المنار

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f20.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f20.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f20.claim: Some writers rejected Khalafallah’s attribution of this position to Muhammad Abduh and Rashid Rida, accusing him of ignorance and misunderstanding.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f20.anchor: لم يقبل عدة كتاب ما نسبه خلف الله لمحمد عبده

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f21.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f21.speaker: محمد إقبال
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f21.claim: Iqbal reads Adam’s descent as an account of humanity’s moral development from instinctual desire to awareness of a free self capable of doubt and disobedience, not the appearance of the first human on earth.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f21.anchor: وفات خلف الله أن يذكر موقف محمد إقبال

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f22.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f22.speaker: محمد أحمد خلف الله
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f22.claim: Khalafallah calls for reading sacred narratives through the symbolic meaning of the language of religion: their purpose is guidance, not a historical account.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f22.anchor: في النصف الأول من القرن الماضي يدعو خلف الله إلى إعادة النظر في التعاطي مع لغة القرآن

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f23.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f23.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f23.claim: The author says this approach remains largely rejected: Qur’anic studies still rely on inherited sciences and interpretive rules shaped by past worldviews, without opening to modern human and social sciences that al-Khuli urged scholars to use.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f23.anchor: إلا أن هذه الدعوة ما زالت غير مقبولة حتى اليوم

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f24.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f24.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f24.claim: The book pioneered a new concept of religious language in Qur’anic studies, yet scholars, including al-Khuli’s students, remained wary; Aisha Abd al-Rahman did not follow its path and stayed within a closed, repetitive historical approach.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f24.anchor: كان كتاب «الفن القصصي في القرآن الكريم» منعطفًا رائدًا

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f25.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f25.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f25.claim: The author presents Aisha Abd al-Rahman, known as Bint al-Shati, as the finest portraitist of al-Khuli the human in her dedication to him.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f25.anchor: أجمل من يرسم صورة أمين الخولي «الإنسان» هي تلميذته

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f26.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f26.speaker: عائشة عبد الرحمن
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f26.claim: In that dedication, Bint al-Shati describes al-Khuli as embodying human grandeur and frailty, and says he sharpened her sense of humanity’s story from its beginning to its end.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/f26.anchor: عائشة عبد الرحمن المعروفة ببنت الشاطئ، في الشهادة التي كتبتها لإهداء كتابها «القرآن وقضايا الإنسان» إليه؛ إذ تقول

NASHR:v1p317/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p317/r1.speaker: ابن مهران
NASHR:v1p317/r1.claim: The discussion reports measures for madd ranks as two, then three, then four alifs, attributed to Ibn Mihran.
NASHR:v1p317/r1.anchor: حتى قدره ابن مهران بألفين، ثم بثلاثة، ثم بأربعة

NASHR:v1p317/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p317/r2.speaker: أبو بكر بن مجاهد، أبو القاسم الطرسوسي، أبو الطاهر بن خلف
NASHR:v1p317/r2.claim: Ibn Mujahid, al-Tarsusi and Ibn Khalaf recognize only two ranks, long and medium, eliminating the lowest and anything above medium.
NASHR:v1p317/r2.anchor: وذهب الأستاذ أبو بكر بن مجاهد وأبو القاسم الطرسوسي وأبو الطاهر بن خلف إلى أنه على مرتبتين: طولى، ووسطى

NASHR:v1p317/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p317/r3.speaker: خلف عن سليم
NASHR:v1p317/r3.claim: Khalaf from Sulaym reports Hamzah's longest madd on open hamzah examples such as jaa ahadahum and his shortest on ulaika.
NASHR:v1p317/r3.anchor: وقد ورد عن خلف، عن سليم قال: أطول المد عند حمزة المفتوح نحو

NASHR:v1p317/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p317/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p317/r4.claim: He rejects the reported shortest madd on ulaika: no imam adopts it, transmission and reasoning oppose it, and its following kasra matches kha'ifin.
NASHR:v1p317/r4.anchor: وليس العمل على ذلك عند أحد من الأئمة، بل المأخوذ به عند أئمة الأمصار في سائر الأعصار خلافه؛ إذ النظر يرده

NASHR:v1p353/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p353/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله بن شريح
NASHR:v1p353/r1.claim: Ibn Shurayh says Hisham lengthens the preceding alif when separating two hamzas, because the second hamza causes the lengthening, as in kha'ifin.
NASHR:v1p353/r1.anchor: أبو عبد الله بن شريح، نص عليه

NASHR:v1p353/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p353/r2.speaker: أبو محمد عبد الواحد بن أبي السداد المالقي
NASHR:v1p353/r2.claim: Al-Malqi assigns the longest inserted-alif madd to Hisham, the shortest to al-Susi, and a middle length to Qalun and al-Duri; all are connected madd.
NASHR:v1p353/r2.anchor: المحقق أبو محمد عبد الواحد بن محمد بن أبي السداد المالقي

NASHR:v1p353/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p353/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p353/r3.claim: Ibn al-Jazari says he read the extended-madd form through al-Kafi in all these cases.

NASHR:v1p353/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p353/r4.speaker: الجمهور
NASHR:v1p353/r4.claim: Most Iraqi reciters, most Egyptians, Syrians, Maghribis and performers disregard the inserted alif because it is incidental and hamzah's cause is weak in pause; some claim consensus.
NASHR:v1p353/r4.anchor: وذهب الجمهور إلى عدم الاعتداد بهذه الألف؛ لعرضها ولضعف سببية الهمز عند السكون، وهو مذهب العراقيين كافة

NASHR:v1p353/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p353/r5.speaker: أبو بكر بن مهران
NASHR:v1p353/r5.claim: Ibn Mihran calls madd between hamzas madd al-hajz, since Arabs insert a buffer against adjacent hamzas, and reports a full alif by consensus.
NASHR:v1p353/r5.anchor: قال الأستاذ أبو بكر بن مهران فيما حكاه عنه أبو الفخر حامد بن حسنويه الجاجاني

NASHR:v1p461/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p461/r1.speaker: أبو هشام، خلف
NASHR:v1p461/r1.claim: Abu Hisham and Khalaf explicitly transmit from Hamzah that in pause he followed the mushaf's rasm, replacing hamzah by the written yāʾ or wāw.
NASHR:v1p461/r1.anchor: أحدهما أن أبا هشام وخلفا رويا، عن حمزة نصا أنه كان يتبع في الوقف على الهمزة خط المصحف

NASHR:v1p461/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p461/r2.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v1p461/r2.claim: Al-Dani applies the known Arabic pause practice of replacing hamzah with the letter matching its own vowel to Hisham and Hamzah, who verify hamzah in connected recitation.
NASHR:v1p461/r2.anchor: قال الداني: فواجب استعمال هذه اللغة في مذهب هشام وحمزة في الكلم المتقدمة؛ لأنهما من أهل التحقيق في الوصل

NASHR:v1p462/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p462/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p462/r1.claim: He rejects the overgeneralized rasm method as untransmitted and corrupting: it produces impossible three-consonant clusters, changes meanings, and is called rasmi, aberrant or abandoned.
NASHR:v1p462/r1.anchor: وهذا كله لا يجوز ولا يصح نقله ولا تثبت روايته عن حمزة ولا عن أحد من أصحابه، ولا عمن نقل عنهم

NASHR:v1p462/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p462/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p462/r2.claim: After surveying qiraat works, he finds only Ibn Mihran citing yāʾ replacement in ta'ibat and wāw replacement in ra'uf; al-Ahwazi reports the latter via al-Tabari.
NASHR:v1p462/r2.anchor: سوى أبي بكر بن مهران، فإنه ذكر في كتابه في وقف حمزة وجها في نحو (تائبات) بإبدال الياء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r1.claim: Qatāda identifies the destroyer as Nebuchadnezzar and his followers, who ruined the Jerusalem Temple with the Christians’ help.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه وسعى في خرابها ﴾ قال هو بختنصر وأصحابه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r2.claim: Qatāda identifies those restricted to entering fearfully as Christians: they could only slip into the mosque secretly, and would be punished if caught.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r2.anchor: قال الله ﴿ أولئك ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين ﴾ وهم النصارى لا يدخلون المسجد إلا مسارقة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r3.claim: Qatāda explains their worldly disgrace as paying the jizya by hand in a state of humiliation.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r3.anchor: ﴿ لهم في الدنيا خزي ﴾ قال يعطون الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r1.claim: منع means interposing between a willing person and what they seek.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r2.speaker: الراغب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r2.claim: Al-Raghib explains that because something may be withheld for protection, منع became common for contested things.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r2.anchor: ولما كان الشيء قد يمنع صيانة، صار المنع متعارفا في المتنافس فيه قاله الراغب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r3.claim: The verb منع يمنع has a fatḥa in its present-tense nūn, as expected because the final root consonant is guttural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r3.anchor: وفعله: منع يمنع، بفتح النون، وهو القياس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r4.claim: The plural المساجد is familiar; Abu Hayyan says he will discuss its singular when it first appears in the Qur'an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r4.anchor: المساجد: معروفة، وسيأتي الكلام على المفرد أول ما يذكر في القرآن، إن شاء الله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r5.claim: السعي first means brisk walking slower than running, then extends to seeking or pursuing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r5.anchor: السعي: المشي بسرعة، وهو دون العدو، ثم يطلق على الطلب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r6.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's lines use السعي for seeking livelihood and lasting glory; the commentators explain it as طلب.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r6.anchor: ولكنما أسعى لمجد مؤثل ... وقد يدرك المجد المؤثل أمثالي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r7.claim: خراب is the opposite of building and a verbal noun; a ruined house is خراب, and خرب is its active participle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p568/r7.anchor: الخراب: ضد العمارة، وهو مصدر خرب الشيء يخرب خرابا، ويوصف به فيقال: منزل خراب، واسم الفاعل: خرب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p569/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p569/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p569/r1.claim: The verse by Abu Tammam, cited in the preceding segment, uses خرب to describe a ruined dwelling; الخرب is also a male bustard, plural خربان.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p569/r1.anchor: ما ربع مية معمورا يطيف به ... غيلان أهي ربا من ربعها الخرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r8.claim: One reported occasion identifies the preventer as the Roman Nantos ibn Isbasianos, who destroyed the Jerusalem temple; it remained ruined until Umar's time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r8.anchor: ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه: نزلت في نطوس بن اسبيسيانوس الرومي، الذي خرب بيت المقدس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r9.claim: A report through ʿAta from Ibn Abbas says Arabian polytheists barred Muslims from remembering God in the Sacred Mosque.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r9.anchor: وقيل في مشركي العرب: منعوا المسلمين من ذكر الله في المسجد الحرام، قاله عطاء، عن ابن عباس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r10.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says Christians wished to ruin Jerusalem and threw filth there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r10.anchor: أو في النصارى، كانوا يودون خراب بيت المقدس، ويطرحون به الأقذار. وروي عن ابن عباس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r11.speaker: قتادة والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r11.claim: Qatada and al-Suddi identify the perpetrators as Romans who helped Nebuchadnezzar destroy Jerusalem after the Israelites killed John son of Zechariah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة والسدي، في الروم الذين أعانوا بخت نصر على تخريب بيت المقدس: حين قتلت بنو إسرائيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r12.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r12.claim: Abu Bakr al-Razi objects that historians agree Nebuchadnezzar lived long before the birth of Jesus.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r12.anchor: قال أبو بكر الرازي: لا خلاف بين أهل العلم بالسير أن عهد بخت نصر كان قبل مولد المسيح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r13.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r13.claim: A further attribution by Qatada identifies Nebuchadnezzar himself as the referent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r13.anchor: وقيل في بخت نصر، قاله قتادة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r14.speaker: ابن زيد وأبو مسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r14.claim: Ibn Zayd and Abu Muslim say the verse concerns Quraysh disbelievers who kept the Messenger from the Sacred Mosque.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p570/r14.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وأبو مسلم: المراد كفار قريش حين صدوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن المسجد الحرام.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p571/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p571/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p571/r1.claim: Despite the reports of particular occasions, the verse's apparent scope is every person who prevents worship and every mosque; the general wording governs rather than a specific cause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p571/r1.anchor: وظاهر الآية العموم في كل مانع وفي كل مسجد، والعموم وإن كان سبب نزوله خاصا، فالعبرة به لا بخصوص السبب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p571/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p571/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p571/r2.claim: The verse follows naturally because the preceding passage mentions Christians and then polytheists, whatever group is taken as its specific occasion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p571/r2.anchor: ومناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها: أنه جرى ذكر النصارى في قوله: وقالت النصارى ليست اليهود على شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p571/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p571/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p571/r3.claim: من is an interrogative in subject position and أظلم its comparative predicate; the question is rhetorical negation, meaning nobody is more unjust than such a preventer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p571/r3.anchor: ومن: استفهام، وهو مرفوع بالابتداء. وأظلم: أفعل تفضيل، وهو خبر عن من. ولا يراد بالاستفهام هنا حقيقته،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p571/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p571/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p571/r4.claim: This is the Qur'an's first occurrence of the recurring formula, which also appears in verses about forging lies against God, denying his signs, and turning away from reminders.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p571/r4.anchor: وقد تكرر هذا اللفظ في القرآن، وهذا أول موارده،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r1.speaker: بعض الناس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r1.claim: To avoid apparent contradiction among verses calling different people most unjust, some restrict each superlative to its own class, such as preventers or fabricators.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r1.anchor: فتأول ذلك على أن خص كل واحد بمعنى صلته، فكأنه قال: لا أحد من المانعين أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r2.speaker: غيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r2.claim: Another view says each group is called most unjust because no one had previously committed that kind of act, making them worse than later imitators.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r2.anchor: وقال غيره: التخصيص يكون بالنسبة إلى السبق، لما لم يسبق أحد إلى مثله، حكم عليها بأنهم أظلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects both construals as foreign to Arabic usage: denying that anyone is most unjust does not deny that people are unjust, so several groups can tie at the maximum.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r3.anchor: وهذا كله بعد عن مدلول الكلام ووضعه العربي، وعجمة في اللسان يتبعها استعجام المعنى. وإنما هذا نفي للأظلمية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r4.claim: He answers that all these passages address disbelievers, equal in supreme injustice because they share unbelief, though their forms of wrongdoing differ; believers can still be less unjust by comparison.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r4.anchor: لأن هذه الآيات كلها إنما هي في الكفار، فهم متساوون في الأظلمية، وإن اختلفت طرق الأظلمية.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan takes من in ممن منع as a relative pronoun meaning the one who; its syntax is then straightforward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r5.anchor: ومن في قوله: ممن منع، موصولة بمعنى الذي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r6.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows من to be an indefinite noun qualified by the following clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p572/r6.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن تكون نكرة موصوفة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r1.claim: The continuation lists parses for the clause as a second object, a purpose phrase with an omitted noun such as دخول, an inclusive apposition to mosques, or a complement with من elided; grammarians differ on its case.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r1.anchor: ثانيا لمنع، أو مفعولا من أجله، فيتعين حذف مضاف، أي دخول مساجد الله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r2.claim: Mentioning God's name stands for all prayer and devotion in mosques, inward and bodily; alternatively, it highlights that the preventers barred even the easiest act, so barring other worship is still worse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r2.anchor: وكنى بذكر اسم الله عما يوقع في المساجد من الصلوات والتقربات إلى الله تعالى بالأفعال القلبية والقالبية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r3.claim: The passive omits the doer for brevity because the perpetrators are too numerous; the prepositional phrase is fronted before the passive subject to echo the earlier mention of mosques.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r3.anchor: وحذف الفاعل هنا اختصارا، لأنهم عالم لا يحصون. وجاء تقديم المجرور على المفعول الذي لم يسم فاعله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r4.claim: The possessive construction honors the mosques, as in the declaration that mosques belong to God; the word masjid highlights prostration as the clearest posture of submission.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r4.anchor: وأضيفت المساجد لله على سبيل التشريف، كما قال تعالى: وأن المساجد لله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r5.claim: The Prophet's saying that a servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating supports the choice of masjid: the worshipper submits fully and places the face, the body's noblest part, on dust.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r5.anchor: أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the verse covers anyone who bars a mosque forever or destroys an Islamic city, since the whole earth is a mosque even without a formal endowment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذه الآية تتناول كل من منع من مسجد إلى يوم القيامة، أو خرب مدينة إسلام،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari asks why the plural mosques is used when either Jerusalem or the Sacred Mosque alone was prevented or destroyed; Abu Hayyan replies that a general ruling can arise from a particular case.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573/r7.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: كيف قيل مساجد الله؟ وإنما وقع المنع والتخريب على مسجد واحد وهو بيت المقدس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r2.speaker: غيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r2.claim: Another view explains the plural because the Kaaba is the qibla of Muslim mosques and Jerusalem is the qibla of others.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r2.anchor: وقال غيره: جمعت لأنها قبلة المساجد كلها، يعني الكعبة للمسلمين، وبيت المقدس لغيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r3.claim: Seeking to ruin mosques can mean literal demolition, as of Jerusalem, or figuratively disabling remembrance there and barring worshippers, which leads to ruin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r3.anchor: إما حقيقة، كتخريب بيت المقدس، أو مجازا بانقطاع الذكر فيها ومنع قاصديها منها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r4.claim: The verse calls preventing remembrance ruin and treats sustained remembrance and prayer as building the mosques; both are figurative usages.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r4.anchor: فجعل المنع خرابا، كما جعل التعاهد بالذكر والصلاة عمارة، وذلك مجاز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r5.speaker: المروزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r5.claim: Al-Marwazi says the question teaches that corrupt belief causes mosque destruction, while sound belief causes their flourishing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r5.anchor: وقال المروزي: قال ومن أظلم ليعلم أن قبح الاعتقاد يورث تخريب المساجد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r6.claim: The declarative wording predicts what will occur, a Qur'anic report of the unseen and glad tidings that Islam will prevail over its enemies.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r6.anchor: هذه جملة خبرية قالوا تدل على ما يقع في المستقبل، وذلك من معجز القرآن، إذ هو من الإخبار بالغيب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r7.claim: Khāʾifīna is accusative as a circumstantial accusative; the exception is an unrestricted exception from circumstances.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r7.anchor: إلا خائفين: نصب على الحال، وهو استثناء مفرغ من الأحوال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r8.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r8.claim: Ubayy reads illā khīfan, a broken plural of khāʾif; its form reflects that he did not treat it as a verse-end rhyme, with wāw changed to yāʾ as in ṣawm/ṣaym.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبي: إلا خيفا، وهو جمع خائف، كنائم ونوم، ولم يجعلها فاصلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r9.claim: One reported explanation makes their fear the humiliation, subjection, and jizya that would be imposed on them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r9.anchor: هو ما يلحقهم من الصغار والذل والجزية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r10.claim: Another reported explanation is fear that believers will attack them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r10.anchor: أو من أن يبطش بهم المؤمنون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r11.claim: A further explanation locates the fear in the course of litigation, which itself entails fear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r11.anchor: أو في المحاكمة، وهي تتضمن الخوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r12.claim: Another view says Christians enter Jerusalem fearing a painful beating.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r12.anchor: أو ضربا موجعا، لأن النصارى لا يدخلون بيت المقدس إلا خائفين من الضرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r13.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers that they should enter God's mosques fearing God and dreading His punishment; a house appointed for worship should be honored, maintained, and entered reverently.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r13.anchor: والظاهر أن المعنى: أولئك ما ينبغي لهم أن يدخلوا مساجد الله إلا وهم خائفون من الله وجلون من عقابه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r14.claim: He illustrates the blame by analogy: one who meets a friend of God ought to honor him, so killing him is a gross reversal of the proper response.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p573#2/r14.anchor: ما كان له أن يلقاه إلا معظما له مكرما أي هذه حالة من يلقى وليا لله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r1.claim: The offenders deserve great blame because they did the opposite of the reverence and honor that mosques should receive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r1.anchor: ففي ذلك تقبيح عظيم على ما وقع منه، إذ كان ينبغي أن يقع ضده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r2.claim: The future-event interpretation misses the force of mā kāna lahum, which denies that entering this way was proper or sought; a plain prediction would say mā yadkhulūnahā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r2.anchor: لكان اللفظ: أولئك ما يدخلونها إلا خائفين، ولم يأت بلفظ: ما كان لهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r3.claim: Another reading takes the phrase as God's decree in the Preserved Tablet to support believers until unbelievers enter mosques only in fear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r3.anchor: ما كان لهم في حكم الله، يعني أن الله قد حكم وكتب في اللوح المحفوظ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r4.speaker: بعض الناس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r4.claim: Some infer that unbelievers may enter mosques if afraid; Abū Ḥayyān rejects that inference in light of his preferred reading of the verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r4.anchor: قال بعض الناس: وفيها دلالة على جواز دخول الكفار المساجد على صفة الخوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r5.claim: A further view treats the declarative form as a command to Muslims to make unbelievers afraid, prompted by predictions of later entry and destruction of the sanctuary.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r5.anchor: لفظه لفظ الخبر، ومعناه الأمر لنا بأن نخيفهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r6.claim: A Prophetic report says that the Ethiopian ذو السويقتين will demolish the Kaaba stone by stone; it was cited to argue against reading the verse as a future prediction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r6.anchor: أن ذا السويقتين من الحبشة يهدم الكعبة حجرا حجرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān finds the imperative reading and its appeal to later events far-fetched; his interpretation removes the alleged contradiction and defeats these alternatives.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r7.anchor: ودلالتها على الأمر لنا بالإخافة لهم بعيدة جدا، وإذا حملنا الآية على ما ذكرناه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r9.claim: Awlāʾika follows the semantic sense of man in the opening, not its grammatical form; matching form or meaning is possible for relative, conditional, and interrogative man.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r9.anchor: أولئك، حمل على معنى من في قوله: ومن أظلم، ولا يختص الحمل فيها على اللفظ وعلى المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r10.speaker: بعض الناس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r10.claim: Some take the verse as proof that unbelievers may not enter a mosque; Abū Ḥayyān says the entry question belongs to jurisprudence and the verse, on his reading, does not prove it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p574/r10.anchor: وقال بعض الناس في قوله تعالى: ومن أظلم: الآية، دليل على منع دخول الكافر المسجد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r1.claim: The penalties mirror the offenses: worldly abasement answers silencing remembrance, while the fire's bodily destruction answers their attempt to ruin mosques; 4:56 describes renewed skin after burning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r1.anchor: وأما العذاب العظيم في الآخرة، فهو العذاب بالنار، وهو إتلاف لهياكلهم وصورهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r2.claim: Worldly disgrace needs no qualifier because its legal forms are equivalent whether a belligerent is killed or captured or a protected person pays jizya.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r2.anchor: لم يحتج إلى وصف. ولما كان العذاب متفاوتا، أعني عذاب الكافر وعذاب المؤمن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r3.claim: The afterlife punishment is called great to distinguish an unbeliever's torment from a believer's, since their punishments differ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r3.anchor: ولما كان العذاب متفاوتا، أعني عذاب الكافر وعذاب المؤمن، وصف عذاب الكافر بالعظم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r4.claim: One reported gloss identifies worldly disgrace with Islamic conquests, naming Constantinople, Amorium, and Rome.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r4.anchor: وقيل: الخزي هو الفتح الإسلامي، كالقسطنطينية وعمورية ورومية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the worldly disgrace as the jizya imposed on protected non-Muslims.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r5.anchor: وقيل: جزية الذمي، قاله ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r6.claim: Another gloss identifies the disgrace as their expulsion from the Sacred Mosque.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r7.speaker: المروزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r7.claim: Al-Marwazi says the disgrace will be the Mahdi's killing of them when he appears.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r7.anchor: وقيل: قتل المهدي إياهم إذا خرج، قاله المروزي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r8.claim: A further reported gloss takes the disgrace as exclusion from mosques.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r9.speaker: بعض معاصرينا
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r9.claim: A contemporary says every unbelieving group suffers worldly humiliation: Jews and Christians through killings, expulsions, conquests, jizya, and imposed marks or terms; Arab polytheists through defeat, idol-breaking, expulsion from Arabia, and death unless they convert.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r9.anchor: قال بعض معاصرينا: إن على كل طائفة من الكفار في الدنيا خزيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r10.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the disgrace is promised for the end of the world, when Muslims will conquer the Romans, a conquest not yet realized.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r10.anchor: وقال الفراء: معناه في آخر الدنيا، وهو ما وعد الله به المسلمين من فتح الروم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r11.speaker: القشيري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r11.claim: Al-Qushayrī allegorizes ruined sanctuaries as hearts, souls, spirits, and inner secrets ruined by desire and attachment; disgrace is the veil and torment comes from settling for spiritual ranks.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r11.anchor: قال القشيري: في قوله تعالى: ومن أظلم الآية، إشارة إلى ظلم من خرب أوطان المعرفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r12.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls this allegory strange and says Qur'anic wording does not support it, as with most interpretations of this group.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p575/r12.anchor: وهذا تفسير عجيب ينبو عنه لفظ القرآن، وكذا أكثر ما يقوله هؤلاء القوم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p594/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p594/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p594/r1.claim: The greatest excess in wrongdoing is disabling God’s houses from remembrance and seeking their ruin; their offenders should enter only fearful and mindful of their purpose, and face disgrace here and great punishment hereafter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p594/r1.anchor: الإخبار عن مجاوزة الحد في الظلم ممن عطل بيوت الله من الذكر وسعى في خرابها،

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r1.claim: One occasion report identifies the perpetrators as the Roman Titus ibn Isyanus and his companions, who attacked Israel, killed its fighters, captured children, burned the Torah, and desecrated the Jerusalem sanctuary, left ruined until ʿUmar rebuilt it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r1.anchor: نزلت في طيطوس بن إسيانوس الرومي وأصحابه وذلك أنهم غزوا بني إسرائيل فقتلوا مقاتليهم وسبوا ذراريهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that it was revealed about Arab polytheists who barred Muslims from remembering God in the Sacred Mosque.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r2.anchor: وروى عطاء عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما إنها نزلت في مشركي العرب منعوا المسلمين من ذكر الله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r3.claim: On the first occasion, the verse connects the story to the Christians' preceding claim, adding a narrative of their offenses.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r3.anchor: عطف قصة على قصة تقريرا لقبائحهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r4.claim: On the second occasion, the verse is an extended parenthesis describing the polytheists between two coordinated statements, showing the enormity of the People of the Book's wrongdoing.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r4.anchor: وعلى الثاني تكون اعتراضا بأكثر من جملة بين المعطوف أعني قالوا أتخذ والمعطوف عليه أعني قالت اليهود

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r5.claim: The wording is general for every person who bars worship and every mosque; the particular occasion does not restrict its scope.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r5.anchor: وظاهر الآية العموم في كل مانع وفي كل مسجد وخصوص السبب لا يمنعه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r6.claim: Aẓlam is a comparative predicate of man; the question is rhetorical and means that no one is more unjust.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r6.anchor: أفعل تفضيل خبر عنمنولايراد بالإستفهام حقيقته وإنما هو بمعنى النفي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r7.claim: The same superlative formula occurs in verses about turning from God's signs, fabricating lies about God, and denying His signs, raising a question about apparent contradiction.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r7.anchor: إلى غير ذلك فإذا كان المعنى على هذا لزم التناقض

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r8.claim: One proposed answer limits each claim by its relative clause or to later offenders of the same kind, so each is first in that form of wrongdoing.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r8.anchor: وأجيب بالتخصيص إما بما يفهم من نفس الصلات أو بالنسبة إلى من جاء بعد من ذلك النوع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī objects that such restriction departs from the Arabic construction and makes the meaning awkward.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r9.anchor: واعترض بأن ذلك بعد عن مدلول الكلام ووضعه العربي وعجمة في اللسان يتبعها استعجام المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r10.claim: His preferred answer is that the formula denies anyone more unjust than the named offenders without denying that several named groups can be equally unjust.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r10.anchor: فالأولى أن يجاب بأن ذلك لا يدل على نفي التسوية في الأظلمية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r11.claim: Like saying no one is more learned than Zayd, ʿAmr, and Khālid, the wording only excludes someone above those named; it does not rank them against one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r11.anchor: كما أنك إذا قلت لا أحد أفقه من زيد وعمرو وخالد لا يدل على أكثر من نفي أن يكون أحد أفقه منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r12.claim: Though one offense may seem less grave than combining it with another, these examples concern unbelievers, whose shared unbelief is one and equal in kind; comparison with sinful believers differs.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363/r12.anchor: لأن هذه الآيات إنما هي في الكفار وهم متساوون فيها إذ الكفر شيء واحد لا يمكن فيه الزيادة بالنسبة لإفراد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r1.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r1.claim: The conventional question “who is more unjust?” denies that anyone equals or surpasses the named wrongdoer, although the syntax alone does not state that denial.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r1.anchor: وقد قال غير واحد إن قولك : من أظلم ممن فعل كذا إنكار لأن يكون أحد أظلم منه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r2.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the earlier answers with their relevant qualification, or a hyperbolic threat that makes no factual claim about comparative rank; either removes the objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r2.anchor: فلعل الأولى الرجوع إلى أحد الجوابين مع ملاحظة الحيثية وإن جعلت ذلك الكلام مخرجا مخرج المبالغة في التهديد والزجر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r3.claim: The phrase may be the second object of “prevent,” a causal phrase, or an explicative genitive construction with an omitted second object; alternatively, people are the object and the verb takes one object.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r3.anchor: أن يذكر فيها أسمه مفعول ثان لمنع أو مفعول من أجله بمعنى منعها كراهية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r4.claim: Mentioning God's name stands for the prayers and devotional acts, inward and outward, that are permitted in mosques.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r4.anchor: وكنى بذكر أسم الله تعالى عما يوقع في المساجد من الصلوات والتقربات إلى الله تعالى بالأفعال القلبية والقالبية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r5.claim: Seeking to ruin the mosques means demolishing them and disabling their use.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r5.anchor: وسعى في خرابها أي هدمها وتعطيلها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r6.claim: “Those” refers to the wrongdoers who prevent worship and seek to ruin the mosques.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r6.anchor: أولئك الظالمون المانعون الساعون في خرابها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r7.claim: On one reading, the lām expresses fitting entitlement and fear means awe of God; the clause answers what conduct would suit them and treats injustice as putting things out of place.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r7.anchor: اللامفي ( لهم ) إما للاختصاص على وجه اللياقة كما في الحل للفرس والمراد من الخوف الخوف من الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, the lām expresses deserved entitlement and fear means fear of believers; this answers what right the mosque-destroyers had and frames injustice as violating another's right.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r8.anchor: وإما للاستحقاق كما فيالجنة للمؤمن والمراد من الخوفالخوف من المؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r9.claim: Alternatively, the clause states what God decreed would happen in the future: the disbelievers would enter only fearfully. It is a parenthetical promise to aid believers and free the mosques from them.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r9.anchor: في علم الله تعالى وقضائه ( أن يدخلوها ) فيما سيجيء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r10.claim: An unnamed report says that Christians entered Jerusalem's sanctuary only in disguise and stealthily.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r10.anchor: فقد روى أنه لا يدخل بيت المقدس أحد من النصارى إلا متنكرا مسارقة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r11.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r11.claim: Qatada says any Christian found in Jerusalem was beaten and severely punished.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة : لا يوجد نصراني في بيت المقدس إلا انتهك ضربا وأبلغ إليه في العقوبة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r12.claim: The Crusader capture of Jerusalem for over a century before Saladin retook it does not refute the promise: it need only have been fulfilled at some point, not repeatedly.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r12.anchor: ولا نقض بإستيلاء الأقرع وبقاء بيت المقدس في أيدي النصارى أكثر من مائة سنة إلى أن أستخلصه الملك صلاح الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r13.claim: Some read the negation as a prohibition against enabling their entry, which entails fearful entry; Al-Alusi prefers from the outset the direct reading as a promise of believers' victory and recovery of the mosques.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r13.anchor: وقيل : النفي بمعنى النهي ومعناه على طريق الكناية النهي عن التخلية والتمكين من دخولهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r14.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r14.claim: Abu Hanifa allows non-Muslims to enter mosques generally, citing this verse, the Prophet's lodging the Thaqif delegation in the mosque, and the sanctuary-safety report; he reads the prohibition as disapproval or as limited to entering the Haram for pilgrimage.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r14.anchor: فجوزه الإمام أبو حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنه مطلقا للآية فإنها تفيد دخولهم بخشية وخشوع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r15.speaker: مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r15.claim: Malik bars non-Muslims from mosques, citing 9:28 and the duty to purify mosques from impurity, though the passage also reports permission for need.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r15.anchor: ومنعه مالك رضي الله تعالى عنه مطلقا لقوله تعالى : ( إنما المشركون نجس ) والمساجد يجب تطهيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r16.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r16.claim: Al-Shafi'i distinguishes the Sacred Mosque from other mosques and regards the cited hadith as abrogated by the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r16.anchor: فرق الإمام الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه بين المسجد الحرام وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r17.speaker: عبدالله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r17.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allah gives “إلا حنيفا.”
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r17.anchor: وقرأ عبدالله ( إلا حنيفا ) وهو مثل صيم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r18.claim: Their worldly disgrace includes killing their leaders and chiefs, breaking idols, exposing their folly, and expelling them from Arabia, or imposing the jizya on those made protected subjects.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r18.anchor: خزي أي عظيم بقتل أبطالهم وأقيالهم وكسر أصنامهم وتسفيه أحلامهم وإخراجهم من جزيرة العرب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r19.claim: The great punishment of the hereafter is Hell, matching the great scale of their wrongdoing.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r19.anchor: ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم وهو عذاب النار لما أن سببه أيضا وهو ما حكى من ظلمهم كذلك في العظم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r20.claim: Putting the locative phrases first in both clauses builds anticipation for the punishment that follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r20.anchor: وتقديم الظرف في الموضعين للتشويق لما يذكر بعده

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r21.claim: In the inward reading, God's mosques are hearts where He is known and worshipped through self-annihilation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r21.anchor: مواضع السجود لله تعالى وهي القلوب التي يعرف فيها فيسجد له بالفناء الذاتي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r22.claim: The divine name may mean the Supreme Name, whose theophany occurs in the heart as the manifestation of the Essence with all attributes, or each person's name suited to their capacity.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r22.anchor: الاسم الأعظم إذ لا يتجلى بهذا الاسم إلا في القلب وهو التجلي بالذات مع جميع الصفات

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r23.claim: Inward ruin is clouding hearts with fanaticism and passion, and stirring conflicts among the soul's powers, satanic impulse, and illusion.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r23.anchor: بتكديرها بالتعصبات وغلبة الهوى ومنع أهلها بتهييج الفتن اللازمة لتجاذب قوى النفس وداعي الشيطان والوهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r24.claim: They can approach these hearts only fearful and humbled before the manifestation of the Real.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r25.claim: In the inward reading, worldly disgrace exposes their falsehood and the afterlife punishment is veiling from God.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p363#2/r25.anchor: وافتضاح وذلة بظهور بطلان ما هم عليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r1.claim: One occasion of revelation is the Roman Titus and his men, who invaded Israel, killed its fighters, enslaved its children, burned the Torah, and desecrated and destroyed Jerusalem's Temple; it remained ruined until Muslims rebuilt it under ʿUmar.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r1.anchor: الآية نزلت في طيطوس بن إسبيسبانوس الرومي وأصحابه، وذلك أنهم غزوا بني إسرائيل فقتلوا مقاتلتهم وسبوا ذراريهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r2.speaker: قتادة والسدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r2.claim: Qatāda and al-Suddī identify the perpetrators as Nebuchadnezzar and his men, who invaded the Jews and destroyed Jerusalem's Temple, aided by the Christians and Titus's Romans.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة والسدي: هو بختنصر وأصحابه غزوا اليهود وخربوا بيت المقدس وأعانهم على ذلك النصارى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r3.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says the Christians helped because the Jews had killed John son of Zechariah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r3.anchor: قال السدي: من أجل أنهم قتلوا يحيى بن زكريا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r4.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r4.claim: Qatāda says some Jews induced the Christians to help Nebuchadnezzar the Babylonian Magian.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: حملهم بعض اليهود على معاونة بختنصر البابلي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r5.claim: “Who is more unjust” means more unbelieving and more defiant.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r6.claim: The mosques intended are Jerusalem's Temple and its sanctuaries.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r6.anchor: منع مساجد الله} يعني بيت المقدس ومحاربيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says that after Jerusalem was rebuilt no Roman could enter it except fearfully, for he would be killed if discovered.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: لم يدخلها يعني بيت المقدس بعد عمارتها رومي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r9.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r9.claim: Qatāda and Muqātil say Christians could enter Jerusalem only in disguise, fearing punishment if caught.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r9.anchor: قال قتادة ومقاتل: لا يدخل بيت المقدس أحد من النصارى إلا متنكر لو قدر عليه لعوقب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r10.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r10.claim: Al-Suddī says their fear was caused by the jizya.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r11.claim: An alternative treats this as a command to drive them out through jihad so that none enter except in fear of death or enslavement.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r11.anchor: وقيل: هذا خبر بمعنى الأمر، أي أجهضوهم بالجهاد حتى لا يدخلها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r12.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r12.claim: Qatāda explains worldly disgrace as killing for belligerents and jizya for protected non-Muslims.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r12.anchor: قال قتادة: هو القتل للحربي والجزية للذمي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r13.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r13.claim: Muqātil and al-Kalbī say their worldly disgrace is the conquest of their three cities: Constantinople, Rome, and Amorium.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r13.anchor: قال مقاتل (والكلبي) (2) تفتح مدائنهم الثلاثة قسطنطينية، ورومية، وعمورية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r14.claim: The great punishment in the Hereafter is Hell.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r15.speaker: عطاء وعبد الرحمن بن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r15.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd say the verse concerns Meccan polytheists who barred the Prophet and his Companions from pilgrimage and prayer at the Sacred Mosque at al-Ḥudaybiyya.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r15.anchor: وقال عطاء وعبد الرحمن بن زيد: نزلت في مشركي مكة، وأراد بالمساجد المسجد الحرام منعوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه من حجه والصلاة فيه عام الحديبية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r16.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r16.claim: Preventing the Sacred Mosque from being maintained through remembrance counts as striving to ruin it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r16.anchor: وإذا منعوا من أن يعمره بذكر فقد سعوا في خرابه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r17.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r17.claim: In the Meccan interpretation, God promises to open the sanctuary to the Muslims and make them its rightful occupants; after its conquest the Prophet ordered an announcement that no polytheist would perform pilgrimage after that year.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r17.anchor: يعني أهل مكة يقول أفتحها عليكم حتى تدخلوها وتكونوا أولى بها منهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r18.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r18.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r18.claim: The established law forbids allowing a polytheist to enter the sanctuary.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r18.anchor: وثبت في الشرع أن لا يمكن مشرك من دخول الحرم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r19.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r19.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p138/r19.claim: Worldly disgrace includes humiliation, killing, captivity, and exile.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r1.claim: The charge of greatest wrongdoing is general: it applies to anyone who destroys a mosque or works to disable a place designated for prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r1.anchor: عام لكل من خرب مسجدا، أو سعى في تعطيل مكان مرشح للصلاة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r2.claim: One occasion of revelation is the Romans' invasion of Jerusalem, destruction of the sanctuary, and killing of its people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r2.anchor: وإن نزل في الروم لما غزوا بيت المقدس وخربوه وقتلوا أهله.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r3.claim: Alternatively, it concerns the polytheists preventing the Prophet from entering the Sacred Mosque in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyya.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r3.anchor: أو في المشركين لما منعوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يدخل المسجد الحرام عام الحديبية

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r4.claim: The clause an yudhkara fīhā ismuhu is the second object of the verb manaʿa.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r4.anchor: ثاني مفعولي منع { وسعى فى خرابها

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r5.claim: Seeking the mosques' ruin means demolishing them or disabling them from use.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r5.anchor: وسعى فى خرابها } بالهدم، أو التعطيل

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r6.claim: One explanation says the wrongdoers ought only to enter with fear and reverence, since they destroyed the mosque.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r6.anchor: ما كان ينبغي لهم أن يدخلوها إلا بخشية وخشوع فضلا عن أن يجترئوا على تخريبها،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r7.claim: Another explanation says their only rightful entry would be in fear that believers might strike them, let alone their preventing believers from entering.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r7.anchor: أو ما كان الحق أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين من المؤمنين أن يبطشوا بهم، فضلا عن أن يمنعوهم منها،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r8.claim: A third construal refers to God's knowledge and decree, promising believers victory and recovery of the mosques; Bayḍāwī says that promise was fulfilled.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r8.anchor: أو ما كان لهم في علم الله وقضائه، فيكون وعدا للمؤمنين بالنصرة واستخلاص المساجد منهم وقد نجز وعده.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r9.claim: Another interpretation makes the verse forbid allowing them into the mosque. The jurists differ: Abū Ḥanīfa permits entry, Mālik forbids it, and al-Shāfiʿī distinguishes the Sacred Mosque from other mosques.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r9.anchor: وقيل: معناه النهي عن تمكينهم من الدخول في المسجد، واختلف الأئمة فيه فجوز أبو حنيفة ومنع مالك، وفرق الشافعي

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r10.claim: The worldly disgrace may be killing and captivity, or the imposition of the poll tax.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r10.anchor: قتل وسبي، أو ذلك بضرب الجزية
