BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:114/r11.claim: Their great punishment in the afterlife is for their unbelief and wrongdoing.

DURR-FULL:v1p264/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Quraysh barred the Prophet from praying at the Kaaba in the Sacred Mosque, prompting the verse.
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r1.anchor: أخرج ابن إسحق وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v1p264/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies those who barred the mosques as Christians.
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله} قال: هم النصارى

DURR-FULL:v1p264/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r3.claim: Mujāhid also identifies them as Christians, who threw filth in Jerusalem’s sanctuary and prevented people praying there.
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله} قال: هم النصارى وكانوا يطرحون في بيت المقدس الأذى

DURR-FULL:v1p264/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r4.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r4.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the obstructors as Romans who supported Nebuchadnezzar against Jerusalem.
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r4.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله} الآية قال: هم الروم كانوا ظاهروا بختنصر على بيت المقدس

DURR-FULL:v1p264/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r5.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says a Roman can enter Jerusalem only fearing execution, and the Romans are made fearful by paying the jizya.
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r5.anchor: وفي قوله {أولئك ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين} قال: فليس في الأرض رومي يدخله اليوم إلا وهو خائف

DURR-FULL:v1p264/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r6.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r6.claim: Al-Suddī predicts humiliation when the Mahdī appears, conquers Constantinople, and kills them.
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r6.anchor: وفي قوله {لهم في الدنيا خزي} قال: أما خزيهم في الدنيا فإنه إذا قام المهدي وفتحت القسطنطينية قتلهم

DURR-FULL:v1p264/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r7.claim: Qatāda says the Romans, God’s enemies, helped pagan Babylonian Nebuchadnezzar destroy Jerusalem out of hatred for the Jews.
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال: أولئك أعداء الله الروم حملهم بغض اليهود على أن أعانوا بختنصر البابلي المجوسي على تخريب بيت المقدس

DURR-FULL:v1p264/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r8.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r8.claim: Kaʿb says Christians burned Jerusalem after prevailing there; after Muhammad’s mission a Christian could enter only fearfully.
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r8.anchor: عن كعب قال: إن النصارى لما ظهروا على بيت المقدس حرقوه فلما بعث الله محمد أنزل عليه

DURR-FULL:v1p264/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the obstructors as the polytheists who turned the Messenger away from the Sanctuary at al-Ḥudaybiyya.
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r9.anchor: عن ابن زيد في الآية قال: هؤلاء المشركون حين صدوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن البيت يوم الحديبة

DURR-FULL:v1p264/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r10.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r10.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says polytheists may enter the mosque only while in fear.
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r10.anchor: عن أبي صالح قال: ليس للمشركين أن يدخلوا المسجد إلا وهم خائفون

DURR-FULL:v1p264/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r11.claim: Qatāda explains worldly disgrace as paying the jizya submissively.
DURR-FULL:v1p264/r11.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {لهم في الدنيا خزي} قال: يعطون الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون

IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Quraysh prevented the Prophet from praying at the Kaaba in the Sacred Mosque, occasioning the verse.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : ان قريشا منعوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الصلاة عند الكعبة في المسجد الحرام فانزل الله

IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies those who barred worship as the Christians.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس قوله : ومن اظلم ممن منع مساجد الله ان يذكر فيها اسمه قال : هم النصارى .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r3.claim: Mujahid says Christians placed filth in the Jerusalem sanctuary and prevented people from praying there.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد ومن اظلم ممن منع مساجد الله ان يذكر فيها اسمه وسعى في خرابها النصارى كانوا يطرحون في بيت المقدس الاذى

IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r4.speaker: قتادة والحسن والسدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r4.claim: Qatada identifies the destroyer as Nebuchadnezzar and his followers, aided by Christians; al-Hasan and al-Suddi report similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : وسعى في خرابها قال هو بخت نصر ، واصحابه ، خرب بيت المقدس ، واعانه على ذلك النصارى .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r5.speaker: أبو عثمان
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r5.claim: Abu Uthman, a preacher in Jordan, explains the sanctuary’s destruction as killing its people.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r5.anchor: عن أبي عثمان قاص اهل الاردن ومن اظلم ممن منع مساجد الله ان يذكر فيها اسمه وسعى في خرابها قال : خرابها قتل اهلها .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r6.speaker: كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r6.claim: Kaʿb says Christians burned Jerusalem after taking it; the verse means no Christian may enter Jerusalem except fearfully.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r6.anchor: عن ذي الكلاع عن كعب قال : ان النصارى لما ظهروا على بيت المقدس حرقوه ، فلما بعث الله محمد انزل عليه

IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r7.claim: Al-Suddi says Romans helped Nebuchadnezzar destroy Jerusalem; no Roman can enter without fearing execution or being made fearful by jizya.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p210/r7.anchor: عن السدى اولئك ما كان لهم ان يدخلوها الا خائفين فان الروم ظاهروا بخت نصر على خراب بيت المقدس

IBNABIHATIM:v1p211/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p211/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p211/r1.claim: Qatada identifies them as Christians, who enter mosques only furtively.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p211/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قال الله : اولئك ما كان لهم ان يدخلوها الا خائفين وهم النصارى فلا يدخلون المساجد الا مسارقة .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p211/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p211/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p211/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says their worldly disgrace will occur when the Mahdi conquers Constantinople and kills them; similar reports are attributed to Ikrima and Waʾil ibn Dawud.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p211/r2.anchor: عن السدى : اما خزيهم في الدنيا فانه اذا قام المهدي فتح القسطنطينية وقتلهم فذلك الخزي .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p211/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p211/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p211/r3.claim: Qatada explains their worldly disgrace as paying the jizya by hand while humbled.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p211/r3.anchor: عن قتادة : لهم في الدنيا خزي قال : يعطون الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r1.claim: The verse is attached to the preceding statement about Jews and Christians and digresses to expose the polytheists’ analogous misconduct toward Islam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r1.anchor: عطف على { وقالت اليهود ليست النصارى على شيء } ( البقرة : 113 ) باعتبار ما سبق ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r2.claim: According to Ibn Abbas, in a report from Ata, the verse was revealed about Arab polytheists; their exclusion of the Prophet and Muslims from Mecca fits the warning that they would enter the mosques only afraid.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r2.anchor: والآية نازلة في مشركي العرب كما في رواية عطاء عن ابن عباس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r3.speaker: سعد بن معاذ
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur cites the report of Saad ibn Muadh: Abu Jahl challenged him for circumambulating safely after sheltering the converts, and exclusion recurred at Hudaybiyya.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r3.anchor: كما جاء في حديث سعد بن معاذ حين دخل مكة خفية وقال له أبو جهل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r4.claim: An alternative account says the verse concerns Nebuchadnezzar’s three campaigns, which culminated in the plunder and destruction of the Jerusalem sanctuary and city and the exile of Israel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r4.anchor: وقيل نزلت في بختنصر ملك أشور وغزوه بيت المقدس ثلاث غزوات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r5.claim: Another account assigns the verse to the Roman Titus’s conquest of Jerusalem, destruction of the sanctuary, and burning of the Torah; Ibn Ashur says this and the Nebuchadnezzar account do not fit the context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في غزو طيطس الروماني لأورشليم سنة 79 قبل المسيح فخرب بيت المقدس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur prefers Ibn Abbas’s account: it fits the warning about fearful entry and the context, where polytheists, like the People of the Book, obstructed Islamic guidance and barred access to the sanctuary.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p678#2/r6.anchor: والوجه هو التعويل على الرواية الأولى وهي المأثورة عن ابن عباس فالمناسبة أنه بعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r1.claim: The interrogative min is condemnatory; because it is an indefinite noun in a negative rhetorical question, the meaning is “no one is more unjust.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r1.anchor: والاستفهام بمن إنكاري ولما كان أصل من أنها نكرة موصوفة أشربت معنى الاستفهام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r2.claim: Zulm means violating another’s right by an unwelcome use of it, and also putting something where it does not belong; either sense applies here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r2.anchor: والظلم الاعتداء على حق الغير بالتصرف فيه بما لا يرضى به ويطلق على وضع الشيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r3.claim: They are exceptionally unjust because they wronged Muslims, who had the strongest claim to the Sacred Mosque, and brought disgrace on themselves among other peoples.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r3.anchor: فقد ظلموا المسلمين من المسجد الحرام وهم أحق الناس به وظلموا أنفسهم بسوء السمعة بين الأمم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r4.claim: The plural “mosques” may magnify the offense; Ibn Ashur compares its use for Noah’s people, who denied the messengers in the plural.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r4.anchor: إما للتعظيم فإن الجمع يجيء للتعظيم كقوله تعالى : { وقوم نوح لما كذبوا الرسل أغرقناهم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r5.claim: The plural may encompass the Kaaba and adjoining sacred worship places, including the sanctuary, Maqam Ibrahim, Hatim, Khayf, Mina, and al-Mashar al-Haram.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r5.anchor: وإما لما فيه من أماكن العبادة وهي البيت والمسجد الحرام ومقام إبراهيم والحطيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r6.claim: Alternatively, the general plural warns every person who ruins a mosque or obstructs worship by preventing its rites; the polytheists are foremost among those included.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r6.anchor: وإما لقصد دخول جميع مساجد الله لأنه جمع تعرف بالإضافة ووقع في سياق منع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r7.claim: The plural pronoun in “enter them” may favor particular, identifiable mosques, since this worldly punishment does not necessarily apply to every person who obstructs a mosque.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r7.anchor: ولعل ضمير الجمع المنصوب في قوله : { أن يدخلوها } يؤيد أن المراد من المساجد مساجد معلومة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r8.claim: The prohibited obstruction is depriving qualified worshippers of appointed rites such as circumambulation and congregational prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r8.anchor: والمراد من المنع منع العبادة في أوقاتها الخاصة بها كالطواف والجماعة إذا قصد بالمنع حرمان فريق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r9.claim: Ordinary closure outside prayer times, preserving a mosque, excluding those unqualified to enter, and barring the polytheist, non-Muslim, sexually impure, or menstruating are not the offense meant here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p679/r9.anchor: وليس منه غلق المساجد في غير أوقات الجماعة لأن صلاة الفذ لا تفضل في المسجد على غيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r1.claim: Sa‘y originally means walking and conventionally came to mean purposeful causation; “striving in” takes fi to indicate the purpose, as in “he turned away striving.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r1.anchor: والسعي أصله المشي ثم صار مجازا مشهورا في التسبب المقصود كالحقيقة العرفية نحو { ثم أدبر يسعى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r2.claim: On the preferred occasion account, blocking worship is literal and ruin is metaphorical causation; on the other accounts, the rulers caused destruction literally while “preventing” worship is metaphorical.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r2.anchor: فالمنع هنا حقيقة على الرواية الأولى المتقدمة في سبب النزول والسعي مجاز في التسبب غير المقصود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r3.claim: The sentence about their entry stands independently to answer the natural question of what punishment follows such injustice, or it may interrupt the clause before the worldly humiliation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r3.anchor: جملة مستأنفة تغني عن سؤال ناشىء عن قوله : { من أظلم } أو عن قوله : { سعى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r4.claim: The demonstrative gathers the three descriptions into a striking portrait; the passage first displays their extraordinary conduct, then states fitting worldly and afterlife punishments.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r4.anchor: والإشارة بأولئك بعد إجراء الأوصاف الثلاثة عليهم للتنبيه على أنهم استحضروا بتلك الأوصاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r5.claim: “It was not for them to enter except fearfully” denies future entry except in fear; كان is past in form, but this construction with أن and the imperfect does not imply past occurrence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p680/r5.anchor: فإن ما كان إذا وقع أن والمضارع في خبرها تدل على نفي المستقبل وإن كان لفظ ( كان ) لفظ الماضي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p681/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p681/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p681/r1.claim: The lām indicates entitlement: the threat is that God would end their control of the sanctuary and its rites and give them to Muslims; at the conquest, polytheists entered frightened until the Prophet’s herald proclaimed safety.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p681/r1.anchor: وهذا وعيد بأنهم قدر الله عليهم أن ترفع أيديهم من التصرف في المسجد الحرام وشعائر الله هناك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p681/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p681/r2.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p681/r2.claim: Many commentators take all mosques generally and read fear as humble reverence for God, with the lām expressing restriction; Ibn Ashur rejects this because the demonstrative makes the entry condition a consequence of their prior offense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p681/r2.anchor: وهذا الوجه وإن فرضه كثير من المفسرين إلا أن مكان اسم الإشارة المؤذن بأن ما بعده ترتب عما قبله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p682/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p682/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p682/r1.claim: The worldly humiliation is a second independent sentence, given emphasis by not coordinating it; khizyi means abasement, including the Quraysh leaders’ deaths and captivity at Badr and flight at the conquest.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p682/r1.anchor: وقوله : { لهم في الدنيا خزي } استئناف ثان ولم يعطف على ما قبله ليكون مقصودا الاستئناف اهتماما به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p682/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p682/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p682/r2.claim: The afterlife punishment is coordinated with the worldly one to complete the statement that they face two punishments, one in each realm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p682/r2.anchor: عطفت على ما قبلها لأنها تتميم لها إذ المقصود من مجموعهما أن لهم عذابين عذابا في الدنيا وعذابا في الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p682/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p682/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p682/r3.claim: The revelation also rebuts polytheists over the Prophet’s post-Hijra change from facing the Kaaba: their exclusion of Muslims from the Sacred Mosque was graver than facing another direction in prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p682/r3.anchor: نزول هذه الآية مؤذن بالاحتجاج على المشركين من سبب انصراف النبيء عن استقبال الكعبة بعد هجرته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r1.claim: Sufi ishārāt are not alternate Quran interpretations: their authors say a verse suits an analogy or lesson, calling these signals rather than meanings, unlike esoteric Batini claims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r1.anchor: فينبغي أن تعلموا أنهم ما كانوا يدعون أن كلامهم في ذلك تفسير للقرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r2.speaker: الغزالي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r2.claim: Al-Ghazali accepts such allusions and reads the Prophetic report about angels not entering a house with a dog or image as an image of the heart: bad traits bar angelic light.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r2.anchor: فالغزالي يراها مقبولة ، قال في كتاب من الإحياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r3.speaker: الغزالي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r3.claim: Al-Ghazali says he is not replacing the report’s outward meaning; it only prompts reflection on inward states, unlike changing the apparent meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r3.anchor: ولست أقول إن المراد من الحديث بلفظ البيت القلب وبالكلب الصفة المذمومة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r5.claim: Ibn al-Arabi rejects all Sufi allusions and denies that the Quran has an inward layer beyond its outward meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r5.anchor: وابن العربي في كتاب العواصم يرى إبطال هذه الإشارات كلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r6.claim: Ibn al-Arabi praises al-Ghazali’s fight against esoterics and philosophers but says his involvement with Sufism made him depart from the truth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r6.anchor: بعد ما نوه بالثناء على الغزالي في تصديه للرد على الباطنية والفلاسفة قال : وقد كان أبو حامد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r7.claim: Ibn Ashur classifies the signals into three kinds: analogy, associative wordplay, and moral lessons drawn from any experience, including Quranic admonitions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r7.anchor: وعندي إن هذه الإشارات لا تعدو واحدا من ثلاثة أنحاء : الأول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r8.claim: As an analogy, mosques can stand for hearts that submit through knowledge of God; blocking remembrance suggests blocking divine knowledge, and ruining them suggests clouding them with partisanship and passion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p34/r8.anchor: ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه أنه إشارة للقلوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r1.claim: مَن is the subject and أظلم its predicate, meaning that no one is more unjust.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r1.anchor: من رفع بالابتداء، وأظلم خبره، والمعنى لا أحد أظلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others identify the wrongdoers as Christians who harassed worshippers at Jerusalem and threw filth into the sanctuary.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وغيره: المراد النصارى الذين كانوا يؤذون من يصلي ببيت المقدس ويطرحون فيه الأقذار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r3.speaker: قتادة والسدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r3.claim: Qatāda and al-Suddī identify them as the Romans who helped Nebuchadnezzar destroy Jerusalem after the Israelites killed John son of Zechariah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة والسدي: المراد الروم الذين أعانوا بختنصر على تخريب بيت المقدس حين قتلت بنو إسرائيل يحيى بن زكرياء عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r4.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r4.claim: Another view identifies the wrongdoer as Nebuchadnezzar himself.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة والسدي: المراد الروم الذين أعانوا بختنصر على تخريب بيت المقدس حين قتلت بنو إسرائيل يحيى بن زكرياء عليه السلام، وقيل: المعني بختنصر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the wrongdoers as Quraysh, who barred the Messenger from the Sacred Mosque.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r5.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: المراد كفار قريش حين صدوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن المسجد الحرام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r6.claim: The verse applies to anyone who prevents access to a mosque or destroys a Muslim city, since every place on earth is a mosque for this community even without formal endowment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r6.anchor: وهذه الآية تتناول كل من منع من مسجد إلى يوم القيامة أو خرب مدينة إسلام، لأنها مساجد، وإن لم تكن موقوفة، إذ الأرض كلها مسجد لهذه الأمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r7.claim: The common pronunciation is masjid with kasra on jīm, though some Arabs pronounce it with fatḥa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r7.anchor: والمشهور مسجد بكسر الجيم، ومن العرب من يقول مسجد بفتحها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r8.claim: أن يذكر may be accusative after dropping من, an appositive to المساجد, an object of purpose, or genitive after an omitted preposition, as Sībawayh notes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r8.anchor: أن يذكر في موضع نصب: إما على تقدير حذف «من» وتسلط الفعل، وإما على البدل من المساجد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r9.claim: If the referent is Jerusalem, its destruction is literal; if the Sacred Mosque is meant, preventing its flourishing counts as destruction because it leads to that end.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r9.anchor: ومن قال من المفسرين إن الآية بسبب بيت المقدس جعل الخراب الحقيقي الموجود، ومن قال هي بسبب المسجد الحرام جعل منع عمارته خرابا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r10.speaker: قتادة والسدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r10.claim: On the Christian interpretation, Qatāda and al-Suddī report that afterward a Christian entering Jerusalem was beaten severely.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r10.anchor: لا يدخل نصراني بيت المقدس إلا أوجع ضربا، قاله قتادة والسدي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r11.claim: On the Quraysh interpretation, an announcement was made by the Prophet’s order that no polytheist should perform pilgrimage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r11.anchor: ومن جعلها في قريش قال كذلك نودي بأمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن لا يحج مشرك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r12.claim: خائفين is accusative as a circumstantial expression.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r13.claim: The verse does not explicitly state a clear prohibition on their entering the mosques, but points toward it and opens with a promise to believers and warning to unbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199/r13.anchor: وهذه الآية ليست بأمر بين منعهم من المساجد، لكنها تطرق إلى ذلك وبدأة فيها وعد للمؤمنين ووعيد للكافرين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199#2/r1.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199#2/r1.claim: For the Christian referent, one explanation of worldly humiliation is killing enemy combatants and taking jizya from protected non-Muslims.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199#2/r1.anchor: ومن جعل الآية في النصارى قال: الخزي قتل الحربي وجزية الذمي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199#2/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199#2/r2.claim: Another explanation of the Christians’ humiliation is the Islamic conquests, including Amorium and Heraclea.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: الفتوح الكائنة في الإسلام كعمورية وهرقلة وغير ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199#2/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199#2/r3.claim: For the Quraysh referent, worldly humiliation means their defeat and killing at the conquest; the afterlife punishment is for those who died unbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199#2/r3.anchor: ومن جعلها في قريش جعل الخزي غلبتهم في الفتح وقتلهم والعذاب في الآخرة لمن مات منهم كافرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199#2/r4.claim: خزي is a subject with its predicate in the prepositional phrase.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p199#2/r4.anchor: وخزي رفع بالابتداء وخبره في المجرور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وآخرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r1.claim: One occasion reported by Ibn Abbas and others is the Romans' support for Nebuchadnezzar's destruction of Jerusalem's Temple after the Israelites killed John son of Zechariah; corpses were thrown there.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r1.anchor: خراب بيت المقدس من أجل أن بني اسرئيل قتلوا يحيى بن زكريا فخرب وطرحت الجيف فيه قاله ابن عباس في آخرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verse concerns the polytheists who kept the Messenger from entering Mecca at Hudaybiyya.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r2.anchor: بين رسول الله وبين مكة يوم الحديبة قاله ابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r3.claim: The reported meanings of ruining mosques are physically demolishing them or preventing God's name from being mentioned there.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r3.anchor: وفي المراد بخرابها قولان أحدهما أنه نقضها والثاني منع ذكر الله فيها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r4.claim: Al-Suddi reads this as a prediction: thereafter a Roman would enter Jerusalem only fearing execution or being made to pay the poll tax.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r4.anchor: أحدهما أنه إخبار عن أحوالهم بعد ذلك قال السدي لا يدخل رومي بيت المقدس إلا وهو خائف أن يضرب عنقه أو قد أخيف بأداء الجزية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r5.claim: Another reading treats the statement as an injunction to strive against them so that no one enters the mosques except in fear.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p133#4/r5.anchor: والثاني أنه خبر في معنى الأمر تقديره عليكم بالجد في جهادهم كي لا يدخلها أحد إلا وهو خائف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid identify the preventers as Christians, who threw filth into Jerusalem's Temple and stopped people praying there.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه} قال: هم النصارى. وقال مجاهد: هم النصارى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r2.claim: Qatada says Nebuchadnezzar and his followers destroyed Jerusalem's Temple with Christian assistance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وسعى في خرابها} هو بختنصر وأصحابه، خرب بيت المقدس، وأعانه على ذلك النصارى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r3.claim: In another report, Qatada calls the Christians God's enemies and says hatred of the Jews drove them to help the Babylonian Magian Nebuchadnezzar destroy Jerusalem's Temple.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r3.anchor: وقال سعيد، عن قتادة: قال: أولئك أعداء الله النصارى، حملهم بغض اليهود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says Christians backed Nebuchadnezzar's destruction and disposal of corpses in the Temple; the Romans helped because Israel had killed John son of Zechariah, a report also attributed to al-Hasan al-Basri.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: كانوا ظاهروا بختنصر على خراب بيت المقدس حتى خربه، وأمر به أن تطرح فيه الجيف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the preventers as the Meccan polytheists who barred the Prophet at Hudaybiya, forcing him to sacrifice at Dhu Tuwa and make a truce; they objected that he had killed their fathers at Badr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه وسعى في خرابها}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd explains striving to ruin the mosques as cutting off those who maintain them through remembrance and come for pilgrimage or ʿumra.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r6.anchor: وفي قوله: {وسعى في خرابها} قال: إذ قطعوا من يعمرها بذكره ويأتيها للحج والعمرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r7.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbas says Quraysh prevented the Prophet from praying at the Kaaba in the Sacred Mosque, and the verse was revealed about that.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أن قريشا منعوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الصلاة عند الكعبة في المسجد الحرام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r8.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r8.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers the Christian account, arguing that Quraysh did not seek to ruin the Kaaba whereas the Romans did seek to ruin Jerusalem's Temple.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p387#2/r8.anchor: ثم اختار ابن جرير القول الأول، واحتج بأن قريشا لم تسع في خراب الكعبة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p388/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p388/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p388/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers Ibn Zayd's Meccan-polytheist interpretation, also reported from Ibn ʿAbbas; Christians barring Jewish prayer would imply their religion was more upright, although Jewish remembrance then was rejected after their curse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p388/r1.anchor: قلت: الذي (1) يظهر -والله أعلم-القول الثاني، كما قاله ابن زيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p388/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p388/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p388/r2.claim: The sequence moves from rebuking Jews and Christians to the polytheists who expelled the Prophet and his companions and barred them from prayer at the Sacred Mosque; Ibn Kathir cites 8:34, 9:17–18, and 48:25.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p388/r2.anchor: وأيضا فإنه تعالى لما وجه الذم في حق اليهود والنصارى، شرع في ذم المشركين الذين أخرجوا الرسول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p388/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p388/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p388/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir counters that Quraysh did ruin the Kaaba in substance by expelling the believers and occupying it with idols, partners, and polytheism.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p388/r3.anchor: وأما اعتماده على أن قريشا لم تسع في خراب الكعبة، فأي خراب أعظم مما فعلوا؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p388/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p388/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p388/r4.claim: Maintaining mosques means remembering God, establishing His law, and cleansing them of impurity and idolatry, not merely decorating or constructing them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p388/r4.anchor: وليس المراد من عمارتها زخرفتها وإقامة صورتها فقط، إنما عمارتها بذكر الله فيها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r1.claim: The clause is a declarative form carrying a command: when able, Muslims should permit such people to enter mosques only under truce and payment of jizya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r1.anchor: هذا خبر معناه الطلب، أي لا تمكنوا هؤلاء -إذا قدرتم عليهم-من دخولها إلا تحت الهدنة والجزية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r2.claim: After the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet ordered a proclamation at Mina in year nine: no polytheist would make pilgrimage or perform naked circumambulation after that year, while existing covenants ran to term; Ibn Kathir links this to 9:28.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r2.anchor: ولهذا لما فتح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مكة أمر من العام القابل في سنة تسع أن ينادى برحاب منى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r3.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r3.claim: Another interpretation says they should enter only trembling and apprehensive that believers might strike them, rather than seize the mosques and bar believers; that was the rightful order absent unbelievers' injustice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: ما كان ينبغي لهم أن يدخلوا مساجد الله إلا خائفين على حال التهيب، وارتعاد الفرائص من المؤمنين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r4.claim: The verse also foretells Muslim victory over the Sacred Mosque and other mosques, with polytheists entering the Haram only in fear; God fulfilled this by barring them and removing other religions from Arabia to purify the blessed place of the universal Messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r4.anchor: وقيل: إن هذا بشارة من الله للمسلمين أنه سيظهرهم على المسجد الحرام وعلى سائر المساجد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r5.claim: Their worldly humiliation repays their conduct: because they barred believers from the Sacred Mosque, they were barred from it and expelled from Mecca as they had expelled the believers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r5.anchor: وهذا هو الخزي لهم في الدنيا؛ لأن الجزاء من جنس العمل. فكما صدوا المؤمنين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r6.claim: Their afterlife punishment answers their violation of the House's sanctity through setting up idols around it, invoking others there, naked circumambulation, and other condemned practices.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389/r6.anchor: من نصب الأصنام حوله، والدعاء إلى غير الله عنده والطواف به عريا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r1.speaker: كعب الأحبار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r1.claim: Kaʿb al-Ahbar says Christians conquered and ruined Jerusalem's Temple, after which the verse was revealed; no Christian enters Jerusalem except fearfully.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r1.anchor: فقال كعب الأحبار: إن النصارى لما ظهروا على بيت المقدس خربوه (8) فلما بعث الله محمدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says no Roman enters Jerusalem's Temple in his time without fearing beheading or being made afraid by paying jizya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r2.anchor: وقال السدي: فليس في الأرض رومي يدخله اليوم إلا وهو خائف أن يضرب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r3.claim: Qatada says they enter the mosques furtively, as if stealing in.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: لا يدخلون المساجد إلا مسارقة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r4.claim: The Jerusalem account still fits the verse's general meaning: Christians desecrated the rock toward which Jews prayed and were humbled there, while the Jews' even greater disobedience brought a greater punishment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r4.anchor: قلت: وهذا لا ينفي أن يكون داخلا في معنى عموم الآية فإن النصارى ما ظلموا بيت المقدس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r5.speaker: السدي، عكرمة، وائل بن داود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi, ʿIkrima, and Wa'il b. Dawud interpret worldly humiliation as the appearance of the Mahdi.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r5.anchor: وفسر هؤلاء الخزي من الدنيا، بخروج المهدي عند السدي، وعكرمة، ووائل بن داود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r6.claim: Qatada interprets worldly humiliation as payment of jizya in submission.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r6.anchor: وفسره قتادة بأداء الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r7.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir says worldly humiliation is broader than the cited interpretations and quotes a hasan Prophetic supplication seeking protection from worldly humiliation and afterlife punishment; the report is not in the Six Books and Busr b. Artat has only one other report noted here.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p389#2/r7.anchor: وهذا حديث حسن، وليس في شيء من الكتب الستة، وليس لصحابيه وهو بسر (6) بن أرطاة -ويقال: ابن أبي أرطاة

MUSNAD-AHMAD:1050/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:1050/r1.speaker: أبو حية عن علي
MUSNAD-AHMAD:1050/r1.claim: Ali performed ablution by washing each listed limb three times, wiping his head, and drinking the leftover water; he said he copied the Prophet and demonstrated the practice for observers.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:1050/r1.anchor: عن أبي حية الوادعي، قال عبد الرزاق: عن أبي حية، قال: رأيت عليا بال في الرحبة ودعا بماء

MUSNAD-AHMAD:1050/r2.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:1050/r2.speaker: علي
MUSNAD-AHMAD:1050/r2.claim: Ali said the best people after the Prophet were Abu Bakr and then Umar, with later developments left for God to judge.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:1050/r2.anchor: قال: ضرب علقمة بن قيس هذا المنبر، وقال: خطبنا علي رضي الله عنه على هذا المنبر

MUSNAD-AHMAD:1050/r3.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:1050/r3.speaker: علي
MUSNAD-AHMAD:1050/r3.claim: Ali likewise said that Abu Bakr and then Umar were the best of this community after the Prophet.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:1050/r3.anchor: عن عبد خير، قال: سمعت عليا، يقول: " إن خير هذه الأمة بعد نبيها أبو بكر، ثم عمر

JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r1.claim: Manʿ is preventing someone from what they want; ṣadd is similar, and iṭlāq is its opposite.
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r1.anchor: المنع: الحيلولة بين المرء وبين ما يريده، ونظيره: الصد، ونقيضه: الإطلاق.

JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r2.claim: Saʿy is a pace slower than walking, and any action, good or evil, is also called saʿy.
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r2.anchor: والسعي: عدو دون السير، وكل عمل من خير أو شر فهو سعي.

JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r3.claim: A masjid is a place of prostration, and its plural is masājid.

JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r4.claim: Kharāb, ruin, is the opposite of ʿimāra, cultivation or construction.

JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r6.speaker: الأخفش
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash allows taking أن يذكر with an omitted مِن, yielding the sense of barring them from God’s mosques from being used for remembrance.
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r6.anchor: قال الأخفش: يجوز أن يكون على حذف (من)، كأنه قيل: مساجد الله من أن يذكر فيها اسمه.

JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r7.speaker: الأخفش
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash also allows أن يذكر to function as an appositive to مساجد الله.
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون على البدل من مساجد الله

JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj construes the phrase as meaning that they prevented remembrance because they disliked God’s name being mentioned; منع governs it.
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r8.anchor: وقال الزجاج: يجوز على معنى كراهة أن يذكر فيها اسمه، والعامل فيه: منع.

JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والفراء
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r9.claim: One occasion report identifies the perpetrators as Byzantines who ruined Jerusalem until ʿUmar’s time, after which Muslims prevailed and they entered fearfully.
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r9.anchor: قيل: نزلت في الروم؛ لأنهم كانوا خربوا بيت المقدس، وسعوا في خرابه حتى أيام عمر،

JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r10.speaker: الحسن، وقتادة، والسدي
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r10.claim: Another report says the verse concerns Bukhtnaṣṣar’s destruction of Jerusalem; Qatāda adds that Christians helped him out of hatred for Jews.
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في [بختنصر] خرب بيت المقدس، عن الحسن وقتادة والسدي، قال قتادة:

JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r11.speaker: الأصم، وأبو علي، وأبو القاسم، وابن زيد
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r11.claim: A third account applies the verse to western polytheists who barred the Prophet and Muslims from the Sacred Mosque.
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r11.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في مشركي الغرب صدوا النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - والمسلمين عن المسجد الحرام،

JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r12.claim: A broader interpretation applies the verse to all polytheists, who seek to bar Muslims from mosques and ruin them.
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r12.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في سائر المشركين؛ لأنهم يريدون صد المسلمين عن المساجد ويخربونها.

JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r13.claim: If the verse concerns Christians and Jerusalem, it follows the preceding mention of Jews and Christians by directing blame first to one group and then the other.
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r13.anchor: من حملها على النصارى، وخراب بيت المقدس، قال: تتصل بما قبلها من حيث جرى ذكر اليهود والنصارى،

JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r14.claim: If it concerns the Sacred Mosque or all mosques, it follows the mention of Arab polytheists among those without knowledge; it may also introduce what follows or collectively rebuke disbelievers.
JISHUMI:v1p556#2/r14.anchor: وأما من حمله على المسجد الحرام وسائر المساجد، قال: جرى ذكر مشركي العرب في قوله: (كذلك قال الذين لا يعلمون)

JISHUMI:v1p558/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p558/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p558/r1.claim: The question means that no one is more or more gravely unjust than the person who bars God’s mosques from remembrance.
JISHUMI:v1p558/r1.anchor: ومن أظلم أي أشد ظلما وأعظم ممن منع مساجد الله أي لا ظلم أعظم من ظلمه

JISHUMI:v1p558/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p558/r2.speaker: النصارى
JISHUMI:v1p558/r2.claim: One interpretation identifies the wrongdoers as Christians and the mosque as Jerusalem’s temple.
JISHUMI:v1p558/r2.anchor: واختلفوا قيل: هم النصارى، والمسجد بيت المقدس،

JISHUMI:v1p558/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p558/r3.speaker: المشركون؛ عن الأصم وغيره
JISHUMI:v1p558/r3.claim: Another interpretation identifies the wrongdoers as polytheists and the mosque as the Sacred Mosque in Mecca.
JISHUMI:v1p558/r3.anchor: المسجد هو المسجد الحرام، عن الأصم وغيره.

JISHUMI:v1p558/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p558/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p558/r4.claim: A third interpretation takes the wrongdoers to be all disbelievers and the mosques to mean all mosques.
JISHUMI:v1p558/r4.anchor: وقيل: هم سائر الكفار، والمساجد سائر المساجد.

JISHUMI:v1p558/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p558/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p558/r5.claim: The plural can refer to every place containing a mosque, or include mosques built by Muslims; Abū Bakr built a mosque in Mecca that they demolished.
JISHUMI:v1p558/r5.anchor: قيل: كل بقعة فيها مسجد، وقيل: دخل فيها المساجد التي بناها المسلمون

JISHUMI:v1p558/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p558/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p558/r6.claim: Saʿy means deliberately working to ruin the mosques; ruin may mean expelling believers at the Hijra, barring them, or preventing prayer and worship.
JISHUMI:v1p558/r6.anchor: تخريبهم إخراجهم المؤمنين عند الهجرة، وقيل: صدهم، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v1p558/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p558/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p558/r7.claim: Abū Muslim explains the mosques’ ruin as preventing people from entering them; Jishumī says both that and expulsion can be intended.
JISHUMI:v1p558/r7.anchor: وقيل: صدهم، عن أبي مسلم، ويجوز حمله عليهما، وقيل: المراد المنع عن الصلاة

JISHUMI:v1p558/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p558/r8.speaker: قتادة، والسدي
JISHUMI:v1p558/r8.claim: On the Jerusalem reading, Christians may enter the temple only fearfully, and any Christian found there is beaten severely.
JISHUMI:v1p558/r8.anchor: يعني النصارى لا يدخلون بيت المقدس إلا خائفين، ولا يوجد فيه نصراني إلا أوجع ضربا،

JISHUMI:v1p558/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p558/r9.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p558/r9.claim: Abū ʿAlī says a disbeliever enters a mosque only under judicial authority and fearfully, while the Sacred Mosque admits no disbeliever for a lawsuit or otherwise.
JISHUMI:v1p558/r9.anchor: وقيل: لا يدخل كافر مسجدا إلا بحكم، فيدخل خائفا، ولا يدخل المسجد الحرام لحكومة

JISHUMI:v1p558/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p558/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
JISHUMI:v1p558/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd links the threat to the Prophet’s proclamation that no polytheist would make pilgrimage after that year.
JISHUMI:v1p558/r10.anchor: وقيل: نادى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: لا يحج بعد العام مشرك عن ابن زيد،

JISHUMI:v1p558/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p558/r11.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v1p558/r11.claim: Al-Zajjāj reads this as a forecast that Islam would prevail, leaving opponents able to enter mosques only fearfully, as Muslims gained honor.
JISHUMI:v1p558/r11.anchor: وقيل: أعلم الله أن الإسلام يظهر حتى لا يدخل مخالف مساجدهم إلا خائفا، فكأنه قال:

JISHUMI:v1p558/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p558/r12.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v1p558/r12.claim: One account identifies the worldly disgrace as payment of the jizya in a state of subordination.
JISHUMI:v1p558/r12.anchor: لهم في الدنيا خزي قيل: يعطون الجزية وهم صاغرون، عن قتادة،

JISHUMI:v1p558/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p558/r13.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
JISHUMI:v1p558/r13.claim: Another account says their disgrace will be the conquest of Constantinople, Rome, and ʿAmūriyya.
JISHUMI:v1p558/r13.anchor: وقيل: خزيهم: فتح مدائنهم الثلاث: قسطنطينية، ورومية، وعمورية عن مقاتل والكلبي.

JISHUMI:v1p558/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p558/r14.speaker: السدي
JISHUMI:v1p558/r14.claim: Al-Suddī says their disgrace will occur when the Mahdī rises and Constantinople is conquered.
JISHUMI:v1p558/r14.anchor: وقيل: خزيهم إذا قام المهدي، وفتحت

JISHUMI:v1p559/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p559/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p559/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says their disgrace is to be killed if they are at war, or pay jizya if they are protected subjects.
JISHUMI:v1p559/r1.anchor: كانوا ذمة، عن الزجاج. وقيل: خزيهم:

JISHUMI:v1p559/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p559/r2.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p559/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī identifies their disgrace as being barred from entering mosques as believers do.
JISHUMI:v1p559/r2.anchor: وقيل: خزيهم: طردهم عن دخول المساجد كما يدخلها المؤمن، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v1p559/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p559/r3.speaker: جماعة المفسرين
JISHUMI:v1p559/r3.claim: The commentators generally explain the great punishment in the afterlife as Hell on the Day of Resurrection.
JISHUMI:v1p559/r3.anchor: ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم يعني يوم القيامة لهم عذاب جهنم عن جماعة المفسرين

JISHUMI:v1p559/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p559/r4.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v1p559/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says it is the promised Muslim conquest of Byzantium, but Jishumī rejects this as contrary to the apparent meaning and commentators’ view.
JISHUMI:v1p559/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو ما وعد الله المسلمين من فتح الروم، ولم يكن بعد، عن الفراء، وهو خلاف الظاهر،

JISHUMI:v1p559/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p559/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p559/r5.claim: The verse shows how grave it is to prevent worship, mosque entry, or people’s prayerful use of mosques; the threat of fearful entry concerns fear of remaining there.
JISHUMI:v1p559/r5.anchor: الآية تدل على عظم المنع من العبادة ودخول المساجد، والمراد: خائفين من لبثهم،

JISHUMI:v1p559/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p559/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p559/r6.claim: The verse indicates that disbelievers are barred from mosques, though they may enter fearfully under judicial authority; barring public manifestation of tawḥīd, justice, and true religion is still graver.
JISHUMI:v1p559/r6.anchor: وتدل على أن الكفار يمنعون من دخول المساجد. والمراد خائفين من لبثهم،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p204#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p204#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p204#2/r10.claim: “That His name be mentioned” is the second object of “prevent”; alternatively, a preposition is omitted or the phrase expresses the purpose of prevention.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p204#2/r10.anchor: ثاني مفعولي منع لأنك تقول منعته كذا ومثله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p204#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p204#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p204#2/r11.claim: This is a general ruling for mosques: whoever prevents remembrance of God in them commits extreme wrongdoing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p204#2/r11.anchor: وهو حكم عام لجنس مساجد الله وان مانعها من ذكر الله مفرط في الظلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p204#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p204#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p204#2/r12.claim: One occasion was Christians throwing filth into Jerusalem’s temple and preventing prayer there, followed by the Romans destroying it, burning the Torah, and killing or capturing its people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p204#2/r12.anchor: ان النصارى كانوا يطرحون في بيت المقدس الأذى ويمنعون الناس ان يصلوا فيه وان الروم غزوا اهله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p204#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p204#2/r13.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p204#2/r13.claim: Another view says the verse refers to the polytheists preventing the Prophet from entering the Sacred Mosque at Hudaybiyya.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p204#2/r13.anchor: وقيل أراد به منع المشركين رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يدخل المسجد الحرام عام الحديبية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r1.claim: The plural generalization is valid although a single mosque was the immediate case, as when a general rebuke follows harm to one righteous person; he cites 104:1, revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shariq.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r1.anchor: لا بأس ان يجيء الحكم عاما وإن كان السبب خاصا كما تقول لمن آذى صالحا واحدا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r2.claim: Ruining mosques can mean interrupting remembrance there or demolishing their buildings.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r3.claim: “Whoever” is general, like “mosques”; it does not identify only those particular Christians or polytheists.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r3.anchor: منع العموم كما أريد بمساجد الله ولا يراد الذين منعوا بأعيانهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r4.claim: They should enter God’s mosques only fearing believers’ punishment, and certainly should not seize or control them or bar believers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r4.anchor: على حال التهيب وارتعاد الفرائص من المؤمنين أن يبطشوا بهم فضلا ان يستولوا عليها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r5.claim: The rightful arrangement would have kept them fearful, had unbelievers not acted with injustice and arrogance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r5.anchor: والمعنى ما كان الحق والواجب الا ذلك لولا ظلم الكفرة وعتوهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r6.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r6.claim: Alternatively, God had decreed that believers would prevail, leaving the others able to enter only in fear.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r6.anchor: يعني ان الله قد حكم وكتب في اللوح أنه ينصر المؤمنين ويقويهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r7.claim: It is reported that Christians entered Jerusalem only in disguise and furtively.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r7.anchor: روى انه لا يدخل بيت المقدس أحد من النصارى الا متنكرا مسارقة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r8.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r8.claim: Qatada says no Christian was found in Jerusalem except after being severely beaten and punished.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة لا يوجد نصراني في بيت المقدس الا انهك ضربا وأبلغ اليه في العقوبة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r9.claim: The Prophet announced that after that year no polytheist would make pilgrimage and no naked person would circumambulate the House.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r9.anchor:
نادى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
51 ( ألا لا يحجن بعد هذاالعام مشرك ولا يطوفن بالبيت عريان )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r10.speaker: أبو عبد الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r10.claim: Abu Abdullah reads “except khīfan,” a form compared with “ṣiyam.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r10.anchor: وقرا أبو عبد الله ( الا خيفا ) وهو مثل صيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r11.claim: Jurists disagree about non-Muslims entering mosques: Abu Hanifa permits it, Malik forbids it, and al-Shafiʿi distinguishes the Sacred Mosque from other mosques.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r11.anchor: وقد اختلف الفقهاء في دخول الكافر المسجد فجوزه أبو حنيفة رحمه الله ولم يجوزه مالك وفرق الشافعي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r12.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r12.claim: Another explanation prohibits enabling them to enter or leaving access open to them; compare the prohibition on harming the Messenger.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p205/r12.anchor: وقيل معناه النهي عن تمكينهم من الدخول والتخلية بينهم وبينه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p206/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p206/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p206/r1.claim: The disgrace may mean killing and captivity, or humiliation through payment of the poll tax.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p206/r1.anchor: قتل وسبي أو ذلة بضرب الجزية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p206/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p206/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p206/r2.claim: Another interpretation is conquest of their cities: Constantinople, Rome, and Amorium.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p206/r2.anchor: وقيل فتح مدائنهم قسطنطينية ورومية وعمورية

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p174/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p174/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p174/r1.claim: One explanation of worldly disgrace is killing a belligerent non-Muslim and imposing jizya on a protected non-Muslim.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p174/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أنه قتل الحربي وجزية الذمي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p174/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p174/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p174/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the disgrace as conquering their cities: Amorium, Constantinople, and Rome.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p174/r2.anchor: والثاني : أنه فتح مدائنهم عمورية , وقسطنطينية , ورومية , وهذا قول ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p174/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p174/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p174/r3.claim: Their immense punishment in the Hereafter is worse than every punishment because they are more unjust than every wrongdoer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p174/r3.anchor: هو أشد من كل عذاب , لأنهم أظلم من كل ظالم .

MUJAHID:v1p86/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p86/r1.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح
MUJAHID:v1p86/r1.claim: Ibn Abi Najih says the Christians used to throw filth in Jerusalem's sanctuary and prevent people from praying there.
MUJAHID:v1p86/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح في قوله ﴿ وسعى في خرابها ﴾ قال النصارى كانوا يطرحون الأذى في بيت المقدس ويمنعون الناس أن يصلوا فيه

MUQATIL:2:114/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:114/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:114/r1.claim: Muqatil identifies the occasion as the Roman Tyakhus ibn Babilis and his people, Christians who prevented worship at Jerusalem’s temple.
MUQATIL:2:114/r1.anchor: نزلت فى الطياخوس بن ببليس الرومى ومن معه من أهل الروم

MUQATIL:2:114/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:114/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:114/r2.claim: “God’s mosques” refers to Jerusalem’s temple, and remembering God’s name there means affirming His oneness.
MUQATIL:2:114/r2.anchor: يعنى بيت المقدس أن يصلى فيه

MUQATIL:2:114/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:114/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:114/r3.claim: The Romans defeated the Jews, killing and enslaving them, wrecked Jerusalem, dumped corpses there, and slaughtered pigs in the temple.
MUQATIL:2:114/r3.anchor: فقتلوهم وسبوهم وخربوا بيت المقدس، وألقوا فيه الجيف، وذبحوا فيه الخنازير

MUQATIL:2:114/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:114/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:114/r4.claim: Under a second Roman ruler, Ttusir ibn Sanabatous or Stephanos, the Romans again killed Jews and destroyed the temple; it remained unrestored until Muslims rebuilt it under ʿUmar.
MUQATIL:2:114/r4.anchor: ططسر بن سناباتوس، ويقال: اصطفانوس، فقتلهم وخرب بيت المقدس

MUQATIL:2:114/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:114/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:114/r5.claim: The Romans should not enter the holy land after Muhammad’s mission except in fear; a Roman entering Jerusalem must come disguised, and is punished if caught.
MUQATIL:2:114/r5.anchor: يعنى الأرض المقدسة إذ بعث محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUQATIL:2:114/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:114/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:114/r6.claim: Muqatil describes their worldly abasement as Muslim forces killing combatants and enslaving descendants in Constantinople, Rome, and Amorium; their afterlife punishment is fire.
MUQATIL:2:114/r6.anchor: إن لم تقتل مقاتلتهم وتسب ذراريهم بأيدى المسلمين

BURSEVI:v1p166/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166/r1.claim: A Mathnawī poem depicts the fool chasing a bird's shadow, exhausting his life's quiver in a futile hunt because he mistakes the reflection for its source.
BURSEVI:v1p166/r1.anchor: ابلهي صياد آن سايه شود مي دود ندانكه بي مايه شود بي خبر كان عكس آن مرغ هواست

BURSEVI:v1p166/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166/r2.claim: The poem contrasts the illusory shadow with God's shadow, whose guidance frees the seeker from illusion and its shadow.
BURSEVI:v1p166/r2.anchor: سايه يزدان وباشد دايه اش وارهاند ازخيال وسايه اش

BURSEVI:v1p166/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166/r3.claim: Bursevī gives as the occasion the Roman Christian king Titus's invasion: his forces killed Israelite fighters, enslaved children, burned the Torah, and desecrated and ruined Jerusalem's sanctuary.
BURSEVI:v1p166/r3.anchor: أن ططيوس الرومي ملك النصارى وأصحابه غزوا بني إسرائيل فقتلوا مقاتليهم وسبوا ذراريهم وأحرقوا التوراة وخربوا بيت المقدس

BURSEVI:v1p166/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166/r4.claim: He says the sanctuary stayed ruined until Muslims rebuilt it under ʿUmar using spoils from Kisra; Crusaders later held it for over a century until Saladin retook it in 585 AH.
BURSEVI:v1p166/r4.anchor: ولم يزل خرابا حتى بناه أهل الإسلام في أيام عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه

BURSEVI:v1p166/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166/r5.claim: The interrogative من is used here rhetorically as a negation: no one is more unjust.
BURSEVI:v1p166/r5.anchor: ومن في الأصل كلمة استفهام وهي ههنا بمعنى النفي أي لا أحد أظلم

BURSEVI:v1p166/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166/r6.claim: The immediate referent is Jerusalem's sanctuary, but the plural generalizes the ruling to anyone who does this in any mosque; the particular occasion does not restrict it.
BURSEVI:v1p166/r6.anchor: المراد بيت المقدس وصيغة الجمع لكون حكم الآية عاما

BURSEVI:v1p166/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166/r7.claim: The phrase is the second object of منع, which can take both objects directly or take the prohibited matter through عن or من; the preposition is omitted here.
BURSEVI:v1p166/r7.anchor: ثاني مفعولي منع فإنه يقتضي ممنوعا وممنوعا عنه

BURSEVI:v1p166/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166/r8.claim: Remembering God's name here means glorifying and sanctifying Him and praying to Him in the mosque.
BURSEVI:v1p166/r8.anchor: من أن يسبح ويقدس ويصلي له فيها

BURSEVI:v1p166/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166/r9.claim: سعى means to act or strive; خرَاب is destruction, with its root sense of breaking and scattering.
BURSEVI:v1p166/r9.anchor: والخراب اسم للتخريب كالسلام اسم للتسليم وأصله الثلم والتفريق

BURSEVI:v1p166/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166/r10.claim: They ought to enter mosques only with fear and humility, much less presume to destroy them.
BURSEVI:v1p166/r10.anchor: بخشية وخضوع فضلا عن الاجتراء على تخريبها

BURSEVI:v1p166/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166/r11.claim: Worldly disgrace may mean killing and captivity for enemy combatants, or humiliation through the poll tax for protected non-Muslims.
BURSEVI:v1p166/r11.anchor: كالقتل والسبي في حق أهل الحرب والإذلال بضرب الجزية في حق أهل الذمة

BURSEVI:v1p166/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166/r12.claim: Alternatively, worldly disgrace is the Muslims' conquest of Constantinople, Rome, and Amorium.
BURSEVI:v1p166/r12.anchor: أو هو فتح مدائنهم قسطنطينية ورومية وعمورية

BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r1.claim: The great punishment is unending hellfire, proportionate to the immense injustice described as its cause.
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r1.anchor: وهو عذاب النار الذي لا ينقطع لما أن سببه أيضا وهو ما حكي من ظلمهم كذلك في العظم

BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r2.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r2.claim: Another reported occasion is the Arab polytheists' obstruction of the Prophet's preaching in Mecca and their barring him and his Companions from the sanctuary at Hudaybiyya in year six AH.
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : نزلت الآية في مشركي العرب

BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r3.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r3.claim: On that account, the mosque meant is the Sacred Mosque in Mecca.
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r3.anchor: فعلى هذا يكون المسجد الذي نزلت الآية فيه المسجد الحرام

BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r4.claim: For the Meccan reading, seeking the mosque's ruin means disabling it from remembrance and worship, not physically demolishing it; without its intended worship it is as if never built or destroyed.
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r4.anchor: فالمراد بالخراب في قوله وسعى في خرابها تعطيلهم المسجد الحرام عن الذكر والعبادة دون تخريبه وهدمه حقيقة

BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r5.claim: A mosque is maintained both by construction and repair and by attending and abiding in it; even the angels dwelling in heaven are called its maintainers.
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r5.anchor: فإن عمارة المسجد كما تكون ببنائه وإصلاحه تكون أيضا بحضوره ولزومه

BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r6.speaker: عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r6.claim: The Prophet says that when someone habitually attends mosques, one should testify to his faith, invoking the principle that believers maintain God's mosques.
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r6.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم "إذا رأيتم الرجل يعتاد المساجد

BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r7.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r7.claim: ʿAlī lists six marks of manliness: reciting scripture, maintaining God's mosque, and forming friendships for God at home; generosity with provisions, good character, and innocent humor while traveling.
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r7.anchor: قال علي رضي الله عنه ست من المروءة

BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r8.claim: Among the signs of the Hour are tall minarets, ornamented mosques, and their neglect through absence of God's remembrance.
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r8.anchor: وعد من علامات الساعة تطويل المنارات وتنقيش المساجد وتزيينها وتخريبها عن ذكر الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r9.claim: Halting prayer, recitation, and public Islamic observances is an especially vile sin; Bursevī laments that Roman lands open wine houses while closing schools and that religion has become a stranger.
BURSEVI:v1p166#2/r9.anchor: فتعطيل المساجد عن الصلاة والتلاوة وإظهار شعائر الإسلام أقبح سيئة لا سيما إذ اقترن بفتح أبواب بيوت الخمر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r1.claim: Man is a subject in an interrogative and aẓlam its predicate: who is more unjust, meaning none is more unjust.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r1.anchor: موضع من رفع على الابتداء وهو استفهام وأظلم خبره والمعنى أى أحد أظلم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r2.claim: An yudhkara is the second object of manaʿa; the preposition may be omitted before an, or an may express purpose, ‘for fear that His name be mentioned.’
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r2.anchor: وأن يذكر ثانى مفعولى منع لأنك تقول منعته كذا ومثله وما منعنا أن نرسل بالآيات

NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r3.claim: The ruling applies generally to God’s mosques: anyone who prevents remembrance in them is exceedingly unjust, although the reported occasion concerns one mosque.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r3.anchor: هو حكم عام لجنس مساجد الله

NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r4.claim: One reported occasion is that Christians damaged Jerusalem’s sanctuary and prevented people from praying there.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r4.anchor: والسبب فيه طرح النصارى فى بيت المقدس الأذى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r5.claim: Another reported occasion is the polytheists’ preventing the Messenger from entering the Sacred Mosque at al-Ḥudaybiyya.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r5.anchor: أو منع المشركين رسول الله أن يدخل المسجد الحرام عام الحديبية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r6.claim: The wording is general although the occasion is specific, as in 104:1, ‘Woe to every slanderer,’ revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r7.claim: Seeking to ruin the mosques means causing remembrance there to cease; the intended sense is general like ‘God’s mosques.’
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r7.anchor: بانقطاع الذكر والمراد عن العموم كما اريد العموم بمساجد الله

NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r8.claim: Those who bar worship should enter only in fear and trembling that believers might overpower them, rather than seizing mosques and barring believers.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r8.anchor: أى ما كان ينبغى لهم أن يدخلوا مساجد الله

NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r9.claim: Alternatively, the verse prohibits Muslims from enabling them to enter or leaving them free to do so, paralleling the construction in 33:53.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r9.anchor: وقيل معناه النهى عن تمكينهم من الدخول والتخلية بينهم وبينه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r10.claim: A report says Christians entered Jerusalem’s sanctuary only in disguise, fearing they would be killed; no grading is stated.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r10.anchor: روى أنه لا يدخل بيت المقدس أحد من النصارى إلا متنكرا خيفة أن يقتل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r11.speaker: قتادة
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r11.claim: Qatāda says any Christian found in Jerusalem was beaten severely; no grading is stated.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة لا يوجد نصرانى فى بيت المقدس إلا بولغ ضربا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r12.speaker: رسول الله
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r12.claim: The Messenger announced that after that year no polytheist would make pilgrimage; no grading is stated.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r12.anchor: ونادى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ألا لا يحجن بعد هذا العام مشرك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r13.claim: Worldly disgrace means killing and captivity for a belligerent non-Muslim, and the humiliation of paying jizya for a protected non-Muslim.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r13.anchor: قتل وسبى للحربى وذلة بضرب الجزية للذمى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p65#3/r14.claim: The great punishment in the hereafter is the Fire.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r1.claim: مَن is the subject, أظلم its predicate, and the sense is that no one is more unjust.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r1.anchor: «من» رفع بالابتداء، و { أظلم } خبره والمعنى لا أحد أظلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r2.claim: The clause أن يذكر is parsed as an accusative apposition to مساجد; alternatives posit an omitted sense of aversion or a deleted preposition من.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التقدير: كراهية أن يذكر، ثم حذف. ويجوز أن يكون التقدير

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r3.claim: One view identifies the mosques as the Temple in Jerusalem and its prayer niches; others identify them as the Kaʿba or all mosques, with the Kaʿba pluralized because it is their qibla or for honor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r3.anchor: وأراد بالمساجد هنا بيت المقدس ومحاريبه. وقيل الكعبة، وجمعت لأنها قبلة المساجد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r4.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the usual kasra in masjid against the general fatḥa pattern of nouns and verbal nouns from this verb class; some Arabs use fatḥa.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r4.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول: مسجد، بفتحها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r5.claim: With fatḥa, masjad can mean the mark on a man's forehead from prostration; al-Jawharī calls the seven bodily points of prostration the ārāb.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r5.anchor: والمسجد بالفتح: جبهة الرجل حيث يصيبه ندب السجود. والآراب: السبعة مساجد قاله الجوهري

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r6.speaker: المفسرون
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r6.claim: Commentators report that the verse was revealed about Nebuchadnezzar, who destroyed the Temple in Jerusalem.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r6.anchor: فذكر المفسرون أنها نزلت في بخت نصر لأنه كان أخرب بيت المقدس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others say the verse concerns Christians: despite honoring the Temple, they ruined it and barred worshippers in hostility toward Jews.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره: نزلت في النصارى والمعنى كيف تدعون أيها النصارى أنكم من أهل الجنة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r8.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r8.claim: Qatāda reports that Christian hatred of Jews led them to aid the Babylonian Magian Nebuchadnezzar in destroying the Temple; the destruction reportedly lasted until ʿUmar's time.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r8.anchor: روى سعيد عن قتادة قال: أولئك أعداء الله النصارى، حملهم إبغاض اليهود على أن أعانوا بخت نصر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r9.claim: Another account places the verse among polytheists who barred the Prophet and Muslims from the Sacred Mosque at al-Ḥudaybiyya.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r9.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في المشركين إذ منعوا المصلين والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وصدوهم عن المسجد الحرام عام الحديبية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r10.claim: Al-Qurṭubī prefers the general reading: it covers anyone who prevents worship in any mosque until the Resurrection; restricting it to particular people and mosques is weak because the wording is general and plural.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r10.anchor: وقيل: المراد من منع من كل مسجد إلى يوم القيامة، وهو الصحيح لأن اللفظ عام ورد بصيغة الجمع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r11.claim: Mosque destruction can be literal, as in the accounts of Nebuchadnezzar and the Christians, or figurative: blocking prayer and public Islamic rites ruins a mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r11.anchor: خراب المساجد قد يكون حقيقيا كتخريب بخت نصر والنصارى بيت المقدس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r12.speaker: الغزنوي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r12.claim: Al-Ghaznawī names the Roman ruler in an account of the attack as Naṭūs ibn Isbiyāsiyānūs; the attackers killed and captured people, burned the Torah, defiled the Temple, and ruined it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114/r12.anchor: قيل: اسمه نطوس ابن اسبيسانوس الرومي فيما ذكر الغزنوي فقتلوا وسبوا، وحرقوا التوراة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r1.claim: A mosque built beside another to split its congregation and cause discord may be prohibited and demolished; this is an exception to the general permission to build mosques.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r1.anchor: ولا يمنع بناء المساجد إلا أن يقصدوا الشقاق والخلاف، بأن يبنوا مسجدا إلى جنب مسجد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r2.claim: The Prophet instructed people not to prevent God's female servants from attending His mosques.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r2.anchor: " لا تمنعوا إماء الله مساجد الله "

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r3.claim: A mosque may not be demolished, sold, or deactivated even if its neighborhood is abandoned; a nearby mosque intended to divide the congregation and ruin the first may be prohibited and demolished.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r3.anchor: لا يجوز نقض المسجد ولا بيعه ولا تعطيله وإن خربت المحلة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r4.claim: Al-Qurṭubī further holds that a town should not have two congregational mosques, one mosque two imams, or two congregational groups praying in one mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r4.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون في المصر جامعان، ولا لمسجد واحد إمامان، ولا يصلي في مسجد جماعتان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r5.claim: The verse shows the gravity of prayer: since prayer is the best deed and greatest in reward, preventing it is a grave sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r5.anchor: ودلت الآية أيضا على تعظيم أمر الصلاة، وأنها لما كانت أفضل الأعمال وأعظمها أجرا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r6.claim: Any place where God can be worshipped and prostration performed is called a mosque; the Prophet said the earth was made a place of prayer and purification.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r6.anchor: كل موضع يمكن أن يعبد الله فيه ويسجد له يسمى مسجدا قال صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r7.claim: The community agrees that a place explicitly designated for prayer ceases to be private property and becomes common to Muslims; a home prayer room remains private if reserved, but becomes a public mosque if opened to everyone.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r7.anchor: وأجمعت الأمة على أن البقعة إذا عينت للصلاة بالقول خرجت عن جملة الأملاك المختصة بربها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r8.claim: أولئك is the subject, what follows is its predicate, and خائفين is a circumstantial accusative.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r8.anchor: حال يعنى إذا استولى عليها المسلمون وحصلت تحت سلطانهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r9.claim: Once Muslims govern the mosques, an unbeliever can enter only fearing expulsion and discipline; al-Qurṭubī takes the verse as evidence that unbelievers may not enter a mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r9.anchor: يعنى إذا استولى عليها المسلمون وحصلت تحت سلطانهم فلا يتمكن الكافر حينئذ من دخولها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r10.claim: On the Christian interpretation, a report says Christians could not enter Jerusalem's Temple after ʿUmar rebuilt it under Islam without being harshly beaten.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#2/r10.anchor: ومن جعل الآية في النصارى روى أنه مر زمان بعد بناء عمر بيت المقدس في الإسلام لا يدخله نصراني إلا أوجع ضربا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r1.claim: On the Quraysh interpretation, the Prophet ordered a proclamation that after that year no polytheist would perform pilgrimage and no naked person would circumambulate the Kaʿba.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r1.anchor: " ألا لا يحج بعد العام مشرك، ولا يطوف بالبيت عريان "

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r2.claim: Another interpretation treats the statement as declarative in form but imperative in purpose: fight them until none enters the Sacred Mosque except in fear, like the prohibition phrased as a report in 33:53.
