QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو خبر ومقصوده الأمر أي جاهدوهم واستأصلوهم حتى لا يدخل أحد منهم المسجد الحرام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r3.claim: Qatāda says worldly disgrace means killing for a belligerent unbeliever and the jizya for a protected non-Muslim.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r3.anchor: قيل القتل للحربي، والجزية للذمي عن قتادة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r4.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r4.claim: Al-Suddī identifies worldly disgrace with the Mahdī's rise and the conquest of Amorium, Rome, Constantinople, and other cities.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r4.anchor: السدي: الخزي لهم في الدنيا قيام المهدي، وفتح عمورية ورومية وقسطنطينية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r5.claim: On the Quraysh interpretation, disgrace came with the conquest, while the afterlife punishment applies to those who died as unbelievers.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:114#3/r5.anchor: ومن جعلها في قريش جعل الخزي عليهم في الفتح، والعذاب في الآخرة لمن مات منهم كافرا

RAZI-FULL:v4p9/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p9/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p9/r1.claim: The commentators agree that the verse identifies actual people who barred mosque worship and sought ruin, and God's punishment of them, rather than stating only a conditional rule.
RAZI-FULL:v4p9/r1.anchor: اجمع المفسرون على أنه ليس المراد من هذه الآية مجرد بيان الشرط والجزاء

RAZI-FULL:v4p9/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p9/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v4p9/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the perpetrators as a Christian king who invaded Jerusalem, ruined it, cast corpses there, besieged and killed its people, enslaved survivors, and burned the Torah; it remained ruined until Muslims rebuilt it under ʿUmar.
RAZI-FULL:v4p9/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : أن ملك النصارى غزا بيت المقدس فخربه وألقى فيه الجيف وحاصر أهله وقتلهم

RAZI-FULL:v4p9/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p9/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والسدي
RAZI-FULL:v4p9/r3.claim: Al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Suddi say it concerns Nebuchadnezzar's destruction of Jerusalem, aided by some Christians out of hostility to the Jews.
RAZI-FULL:v4p9/r3.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة والسدي : نزلت في بختنصر حيث خرب بيت المقدس وبعض النصارى أعانه على ذلك بغضا لليهود

RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r1.claim: Abu Bakr al-Razi rejects the first two identifications: Christians arose long after Nebuchadnezzar and revered Jerusalem, making their collaboration in its destruction implausible.
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر الرازي في أحكام القرآن : هذان الوجهان غلطان لأنه لا خلاف بين أهل العلم بالسير أن عهد بختنصر كان قبل مولد المسيح

RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r2.claim: A third view identifies the Meccan polytheists, who barred the Prophet and his companions from worshipping and remembering God in the Sacred Mosque and forced him to emigrate.
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r2.anchor: وثالثها : أنها نزلت في مشركي العرب الذين منعوا الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام عن الدعاء إلى الله بمكة وألجؤه إلى الهجرة

RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r3.claim: The account says Abu Bakr built a mosque by his house in Mecca but was prevented and harassed by Quraysh women and children.
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r3.anchor: وقد كان الصديق رضي الله عنه بنى مسجدا عند داره فمنع وكان ممن يؤذيه ولدان قريش ونساؤهم

RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r4.claim: It is said that 17:110 was revealed in this setting to prevent the Prophet from reciting aloud and being harmed.
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : إن قوله تعالى : { ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها } ( الإسراء : 110 ) نزلت في ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r5.claim: The account adds that Abu Jahl placed camel filth on the Prophet's back.
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r5.anchor: وطرح أبو جهل العذرة على ظهر لنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r6.claim: The condemnation concerns people who obstruct Muslims worshipping God alone, praying humbly, reflecting inwardly, remembering God, and submitting their whole bodies to His majesty.
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r6.anchor: فقيل : ومن أظلم من هؤلاء المشركين الذين يمنعون المسلمين الذين يوحدون الله ولا يشركون به شيئا ويصلون له تذللا وخشوعا

RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r7.claim: Abu Muslim identifies those barred as the people who stopped the Prophet from entering the Sacred Mosque from Medina at Hudaybiyya; the fearful-entry clause anticipates God's power and the Prophet's eventual ascendancy, as in 48:25, 8:34, and 33:60–61.
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r7.anchor: ورابعها : قال أبو مسلم : المراد منه الذين صدوه عن المسجد الحرام حين ذهب إليه من المدينة عام الحديبية

RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r8.claim: Al-Razi prefers a fifth view: after the qibla changed to the Kaaba, Jews obstructed prayer toward it and may have induced unbelievers to damage the Kaaba and Prophet's Mosque; the surrounding verses also censure Jews and Christians, so a sudden focus on polytheists is unlikely.
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r8.anchor: وعندي فيه وجه خامس وهو أقرب إلى رعاية النظم : وهو أن يقال : أنه لما حولت القبلة إلى الكعبة شق ذلك على اليهود فكانوا يمنعون الناس عن الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r9.claim: The Christian-destruction reading is weak for Abu Bakr al-Razi's reasons; the surrounding verses focus on Jewish and Christian misdeeds, supporting al-Razi's preferred Jewish reading.
RAZI-FULL:v4p9#2/r9.anchor: وأما حمل الآية على سعي النصارى في تخريب بيت المقدس فضعيف أيضا على ما شرحه أبو بكر الرازي ، فلم يبق إلا ما قلناه

RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r1.claim: On the Christian reading, this follows the claim that Christians alone are people of Paradise: their mosque destruction contradicts that boast.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r1.anchor: النصارى ادعوا أنهم من أهل الجنة فقط ، فقيل لهم : كيف تكونون كذلك مع أن معاملتكم في تخريب المساجد والسعي في خرابها هكذا

RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r2.claim: On a Sacred Mosque reading, the preceding verse's mention of Arab polytheists connects the passage; alternatively, the sequence alternates condemnation of Jews, Christians, and polytheists among all unbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r2.anchor: جرى ذكر مشركي العرب في قوله : { كذالك قال الذين * قبلهم مثل قولهم } ( البقرة : 113 )

RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r3.claim: Some understand God's mosques generally as all mosques.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r3.anchor: قوله : { مساجد الله } عموم فمنهم من قال : المراد به كل المساجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r4.claim: Others limit the phrase to the Sacred Mosque and other mosques in Mecca, including Abu Bakr's mosque, which was ruined before the Hijra.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r4.anchor: ومنهم من حمله على ما ذكرناه من المسجد الحرام وغيره من مساجد مكة

RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r5.claim: Abu Muslim takes the plural as referring only to the Sacred Mosque because he interprets the obstruction as the Prophet's being barred there at Hudaybiyya.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r5.anchor: ومنهم من حمله على المسجد الحرام فقط وهو قول أبي مسلم حيث فسر المنع بصد الرسول عن المسجد الحرام عام الحديبية

RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r6.claim: A plural can describe harm to one righteous person, just as one person who harms a single righteous man may be called one who harms the righteous.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r6.anchor: هذا كمن يقول لمن آذى صالحا واحدا : ومن أظلم ممن آذى الصالحين

RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r7.claim: The Sacred Mosque may itself count as many mosques because it is a place of prostration.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r7.anchor: أن المسجد موضع السجود فالمسجد الحرام لا يكون في الحقيقة مسجدا واحدا بل مساجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r8.claim: One analysis makes the clause a second object of منع, as in constructions meaning to prevent someone from something; the source compares 17:59 and 17:94.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r8.anchor: الأول : أنه ثاني مفعولي منع لأنك تقول : منعته كذا ، ومثله : { وما منعنا أن نرسل بالايات * وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا }

RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r9.speaker: الأخفش
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r9.claim: Al-Akhfash allows an omitted من, yielding the sense that they prevented the mosques from having God's name mentioned in them.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r9.anchor: قال الأخفش : يجوز أن يكون على حذف ( من ) كأنه قيل : منع مساجد الله من أن يذكر فيها اسمه

RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r10.claim: Another analysis treats the clause as a substitute for مساجد الله.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r10.anchor: الثالث : أن يكون على البدل من مساجد الله

RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r11.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r11.claim: Al-Zajjaj permits the phrase to mean preventing mosques out of dislike for God's name being mentioned there, with منع as its governor.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r11.anchor: الرابع : قال الزجاج : يجوز أن يكون على معنى كراهة أن يذكر فيها اسمه ، والعامل فيه ( منع )

RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r12.claim: Seeking a mosque's ruin may mean barring worshippers, devotees, or caretakers from entering, or physically demolishing it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r12.anchor: السعي في تخريب المسجد قد يكون لوجهين . أحدهما : منع المصلين والمتعبدين والمتعهدين له من دخوله

RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r13.claim: Preventing worship and its public rites is itself destruction, so this interpretation can apply to the Sacred Mosque even without its physical demolition.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r13.anchor: لأن منع الناس من إقامة شعار العبادة فيه يكون تخريبا

RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r14.claim: It is also said that Quraysh destroyed Abu Bakr's prayer place when he emigrated.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10/r14.anchor: وقيل : إن أبا بكر رضي الله عنه كان له موضع صلاة فخربته قريش لما هاجر

RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r1.claim: Although the wording appears to call mosque obstruction the greatest injustice, shirk is called great injustice in 31:13, and adultery or murder may seem worse; this is only a general statement subject to specification.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r1.anchor: ظاهر الآية يقتضي أن هذا الفعل أعظم أنواع الظلم وفيه إشكال لأن الشرك ظلم على ما قال تعالى : { إن الشرك لظلم عظيم }

RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r2.claim: The apparent reading makes the very perpetrators who prevented and ruined the mosque the people forbidden to enter except fearfully.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r2.anchor: ظاهر الكلام أن الذين آمنوا وسعوا في تخريب المسجد هم الذين يحرم عليهم دخوله إلا خائفين

RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r3.claim: If the clause is general, one reading is that they ought to enter God's mosques in awe, trembling before believers who might overpower them; oppression made this rightful state unrealized.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r3.anchor: ما كان ينبغي لهم أن يدخلوا مساجد الله إلا خائفين على حال الهيبة وارتعاد الفرائص من المؤمنين أن يبطشوا بهم

RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r4.claim: Another reading promises Muslim dominion over the Sacred Mosque and other mosques: polytheists would fear arrest, punishment, or death unless they became Muslim; the promise was fulfilled by the ban on polytheist pilgrimage after Abu Bakr's Hajj and the Jews' expulsion from Arabia.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r4.anchor: أن هذا بشارة من الله للمسلمين بأنه سيظهرهم على المسجد الحرام وعلى سائر المساجد ، وأنه يذل المشركين لهم حتى لايدخل المسجد الحرام واحد منهم إلا خائفا

RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r5.claim: A third interpretation takes fear as the humiliation and abasement imposed by jizya.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r5.anchor: وثالثها : أن يحمل هذا الخوف على ما يلحقهم من الصغار والذل بالجزية والإذلال

RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r6.claim: A fourth view bars polytheists from the Sacred Mosque except for a proceeding that entails fear, such as a dispute, trial, or argument; 9:17 is cited as evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r6.anchor: أنه يحرم عليهم دخول المسجد الحرام إلا في أمر يتضمن الخوف نحو أن يدخلوا للمخاصمة والمحاكمة والمحاجة

RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r7.speaker: قتادة والسدي
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r7.claim: Qatada and al-Suddi say Christians could enter Jerusalem only fearfully and any Christian there was beaten; al-Razi rejects this because Christians held Jerusalem for over a century, while Muslims could enter only fearfully until Saladin recovered it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r7.anchor: قال قتادة والسدي : قوله : { إلا خائفين } بمعنى أن النصارى لا يدخلون بيت المقدس إلا خائفين

RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r8.claim: Though phrased as a statement, the clause can mean that people must not enable them to enter or leave them free access, as in 33:53.
RAZI-FULL:v4p10#2/r8.anchor: أن قوله : { ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين } وإن كان لفظه لفظ الخبر لكن المراد منه النهي عن تمكينهم من الدخول

RAZI-FULL:v4p11/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p11/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v4p11/r1.claim: Some identify the worldly disgrace as humiliation caused by exclusion from mosques.
RAZI-FULL:v4p11/r1.anchor: فقد اختلفوا في الخزي ، فقال بعضهم : ما يلحقهم من الذل بمنعهم من المساجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p11/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p11/r2.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v4p11/r2.claim: Others identify the disgrace as jizya for protected non-Muslims and execution for those at war.
RAZI-FULL:v4p11/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون بالجزية في حق أهل الذمة وبالقتل في حق أهل الحرب

RAZI-FULL:v4p11/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p11/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p11/r3.claim: All these explanations are possible: disgrace covers any punitive abasement and humiliation, which deters them from persisting in unbelief because present shame turns people from its causes.
RAZI-FULL:v4p11/r3.anchor: واعلم أن كل ذلك محتمل فإن الخزي لا يكون إلا ما يجري مجرى العقوبة من الهوان والإذلال فكل ما هذه صفته يدخل تحته

RAZI-FULL:v4p11/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p11/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p11/r4.claim: The afterlife punishment is called immense in the strongest terms because those just described as committing the greatest injustice deserve a correspondingly immense penalty.
RAZI-FULL:v4p11/r4.anchor: وأما العذاب العظيم فقد وصفه الله تعالى بما جرى مجرى النهاية

RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r1.claim: The attribution of mosques to God and the command not to invoke anyone beside Him establish their special sanctity.
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : { وأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا } ( الجن : 18 ) . أضاف المساجد إلى ذاته يلزم الاختصاص

RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r2.claim: The statement that only believers in God and the Last Day maintain God's mosques uses innamā for restriction, linking mosque maintenance to faith.
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى : { إنما يعمر مساجد الله من ءامن بالله واليوم الاخر } ( التوبة : 18 ) فجعل عمارة المسجد دليلا على الإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r3.claim: The verse about houses God permitted to be raised and His name remembered in them also attests to the virtue of mosques.
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى : { فى بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه يسبح له فيها بالغدو والاصال } ( النور : 36 )

RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r4.claim: The verse calls mosque destroyers among the worst wrongdoers; since its general wording includes idolaters and shirk is great injustice in 31:13, mosque builders thereby attain the highest degree of faith.
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r4.anchor: هذه الآية التي نحن في تفسيرها وهي قوله تعالى : { ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه } فإن ظاهرها يقتضي أن يكون الساعي في تخريب المساجد أسوأ حالا من المشرك

RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r5.speaker: عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r5.claim: When people disliked his plan to build a mosque, ʿUthman said he heard the Prophet promise that whoever builds a mosque for God will receive a corresponding house in Paradise; another version says simply a house there. Al-Razi attributes this to the Two Sahihs.
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r5.anchor: ما روى الشيخان في صحيحيهما أن عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه أراد بناء المسجد فكره الناس ذلك وأحبوا أن يدعه

RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r6.claim: The Prophet says the most beloved places to God are mosques and the most hateful are markets; al-Razi explains that mosques prompt remembrance, while commerce turns people toward worldly distraction and away from reflection on God's path.
RAZI-FULL:v4p11#2/r6.anchor: ما روى أبو هريرة أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال

RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's promise that one who purifies at home and walks to a mosque for an obligatory prayer has one step erase a sin and the other raise a rank; Muslim records it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( من تطهر في بيته ثم مشى إلى بيت من بيوت الله ليقضي فريضة من فرائض الله

RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that God prepares a home in Paradise for whoever goes to the mosque morning or evening; the Two Sahihs record it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r2.anchor: أبو هريرة قال : قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( من غدا أو راح إلى المسجد أعد الله له في الجنة منزلا

RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r3.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb recounts that a man living far from the mosque never missed prayer with the Prophet and rejected moving nearer, hoping his journey and return would be recorded; the Prophet affirmed his full hoped-for reward. Muslim records it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r3.anchor: أبي بن كعب قال : كان رجل ما أعلم أحدا من أهل المدينة ممن يصلى إلى القبلة أبعد منزلا منه من المسجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r4.speaker: جابر
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r4.claim: Jabir reports that when Banu Salimah planned to move nearer the mosque, the Prophet told them to stay in their homes so their footsteps would be recorded; Muslim records it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r4.anchor: جابر قال : خلت البقاع حول المسجد فأراد بنو سلمة أن ينتقلوا إلى قرب المسجد فبلغ ذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r5.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri says 36:12 was revealed about Banu Salimah, recording what people send ahead and their traces.
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r5.anchor: وعن أبي سعيد الخدري أن هذه الآية نزلت في حقهم : { إنا نحن نحى الموتى ونكتب ما قدموا وءاثارهم }

RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r6.claim: Abu Musa al-Ashʿari reports that the greatest prayer reward belongs to those who walk farthest, and waiting for congregational prayer with the imam earns more than praying then sleeping; the Two Sahihs record it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r6.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( إن أعظم الناس أجرا في الصلاة أبعدهم إلى المسجد مشيا

RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r7.speaker: عقبة بن عامر الجهني
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r7.claim: ʿUqba ibn ʿAmir says each step toward the mosque after purification earns ten good deeds; the person waiting is like a devout worshipper and is counted among the praying from leaving home until returning.
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r7.anchor: عقبة بن عامر الجهني أنه عليه السلام قال : ( إذا تطهر الرجل ثم مر إلى المسجد يرعى الصلاة كتب له كاتبه أو كاتباه بكل خطوة

RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r8.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r8.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib relates that an Ansari who was dying asked to be raised and greeted the brothers and companions who were at the mosque.
RAZI-FULL:v4p12/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب قال : حضر رجلا من الأنصار الموت فقال لأهله : من في البيت ، فقالوا : أهلك ، وأما أخوتك وجلساؤك ففي المسجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r1.claim: The dying Ansari said he had kept this Prophetic report private since hearing it, for God's reward: excellent ablution and each step to congregational prayer bring reward or erase sin; praying with the imam brings forgiveness, even when only part is caught.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r1.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : ( من توضأ في بيته فأحسن الوضوء ثم خرج إلى المسجد يصلي في جماعة المسلمين لم يرفع رجله اليمنى

RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that one who performs good ablution and reaches the mosque after the congregation has prayed receives the same reward as those who attended, without reducing theirs.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أنه عليه السلام قال : ( من توضأ فأحسن وضوءه ثم راح فوجد الناس قد صلوا أعطاه الله مثل أجر من صلاها

RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that completing ablution through hardship, many steps to mosques, and waiting between prayers erase sins and raise ranks; this is called ribat and is attributed here to Abu Muslim.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r3.anchor: أبو هريرة قال عليه السلام : ( ألا أدلكم على ما يمحو الله به الخطايا ويرفع به الدرجات ، قالوا : بلى يا رسول الله

RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r4.claim: Abu Salama asks Dawud ibn Salih about 3:200; Abu Hurayra explains that since there was no military ribat in the Prophet's time, it referred to waiting for one prayer after another.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r4.anchor: سمعت أبا هريرة يقول لم يكن في زمان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم غزو يرابط فيه ولكن انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r5.claim: Burayda reports the Prophet's glad tidings of complete light on Resurrection Day for those walking to the mosque in darkness.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r5.anchor: بريدة قال عليه السلام : ( بشر المشائين في الظلم إلى المسجد بالنور التام يوم القيامة )

RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r6.speaker: النخعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r6.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi says early Muslims considered walking to the mosque on a dark night a cause of reward.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r6.anchor: قال النخعي كانوا يرون المشي إلى المسجد في الليلة المظلمة موجبة

RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r7.speaker: الأوزاعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r7.claim: Al-Awzaʿi says the Prophet's companions and their exemplary successors maintained five practices: congregational life, Sunnah, mosque upkeep, Quran recitation, and jihad.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r7.anchor: قال الأوزاعي : كان يقال خمس كان عليها أصحاب محمد عليه السلام والتابعون بإحسان : لزوم الجماعة واتباع السنة

RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that whoever builds a house for worship from lawful wealth receives a house in Paradise among mansions of ruby.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r8.anchor: أبو هريرة قال عليه السلام : ( من بنى لله بيتا يعبد الله فيه من مال حلال بنى الله له بيتا في الجنة من دور ياقوت

RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r9.claim: Abu Dharr reports that whoever builds a mosque, even as small as a lapwing's nest, will receive a house in Paradise.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r9.anchor: أبو ذر قال عليه السلام : ( من بنى لله مسجدا ولو كمفحص قطاة بنى الله له بيتا في الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r10.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri reports the Prophet's instruction to attest to the faith of a man who regularly attends the mosque, citing 9:18.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13/r10.anchor: أبو سعيد الخدري : قال عليه السلام : ( إذا رأيتم الرجل

RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r1.speaker: بعض أصحاب رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r1.claim: Some Companions say mosques are God’s houses, and God is bound to honor those who visit them there.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r1.anchor: عن بعض أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنهم قالوا : إن المساجد بيوت الله

RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r2.speaker: أنس
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r2.claim: Anas transmits the Prophet’s saying that those who maintain God’s houses are God’s own people.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r2.anchor: أنس قال عليه السلام : ( إن عمار بيوت الله هم أهل بيوت الله )

RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r3.speaker: أنس
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r3.claim: In a divine saying transmitted by Anas, God averts punishment after seeing mosque maintainers, those who love for His sake, and people seeking forgiveness before dawn.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r3.anchor: أنس قال عليه السلام : ( يقول الله تعالى : كأني لأهم بأهل الأرض عذابا

RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r4.speaker: أنس
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r4.claim: Anas transmits that a heavenly calamity is diverted from those who maintain mosques.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r4.anchor: عن أنس : قال عليه السلام : ( إذا أنزلت عاهة من السماء صرفت عن عمار المساجد )

RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r5.speaker: سلمان
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r5.claim: Salman quotes the Prophet that a mosque is every pious person’s home, with assurances of spiritual comfort, mercy, safe passage, and acceptance.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r5.anchor: كتب سلمان إلى أبي الدرداء : يا أخي ليكن بيتك المساجد فإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r6.claim: According to Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam says mosques are supports among people; angels keep their company, ask after them, visit them when ill, and help their needs.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r6.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب : عن عبد الله بن سلام : إن المساجد أوتادا من الناس

RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan transmits a warning that a time will come when people discuss worldly affairs in mosques; believers should avoid their company.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r7.anchor: الحسن قال عليه السلام : ( يأتي على الناس زمان يكون حديثهم في مساجدهم في أمر دنياهم

RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r8.claim: A report attributed to Abu Hurayra lists hypocrites’ signs, including approaching mosques only rarely and prayers only at their end.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r8.anchor: أبو هريرة : قال عليه السلام : ( إن للمنافقين علامات يعرفون بها تحيتهم لعنة

RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r9.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وأبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r9.claim: The Prophet’s seven people shaded on Judgment Day include one whose heart remains attached to the mosque from leaving until returning; al-Razi says the report is in both Sahihs.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r9.anchor: أبو سعيد الخدري وأبو هريرة : قال عليه السلام : ( سبعة يظلهم الله في ظله يوم لا ظل

RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r10.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r10.claim: The Prophet promises ten good deeds for each step taken from home to mosque and counts one waiting for prayer among the praying until returning home.
RAZI-FULL:v4p13#2/r10.anchor: عقبة بن عامر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( من خرج من بيته إلى المسجد كتب له

RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says that although attending a funeral earns one or two qirats, sitting in the mosque to praise, proclaim God’s oneness, and seek forgiveness is dearer, with angels praying for him.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r1.anchor: سمعت سعيد بن المسيب وسأله أبي : أحضور الجنازة أحب إليك أم القعود في المسجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas transmits the Prophet’s statement that he was not commanded to raise mosque buildings high.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r2.anchor: ابن عباس : قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( ما أمرت بتشييد المساجد )

RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r3.claim: Al-Razi explains tashyid as raising a building and making it tall, citing lofty towers in 4:78.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r3.anchor: والمراد من التشييد رفع البناء وتطويله ، ومنه قوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r4.speaker: عمر
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r4.claim: When Umar ordered a mosque built, he told the builder to shelter people from rain and avoid red or yellow decoration that might distract them.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r4.anchor: أمر عمر ببناء مسجد وقال للبناء : أكن الناس من المطر

RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r5.speaker: عثمان
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r5.claim: Uthman saw a gypsum ornament hanging in a mosque and ordered it removed.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r5.anchor: روى أن عثمان رأى أثرجة من جص معلقة في المسجد ، فأمر بها فقطعت

RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r6.speaker: أبو الدرداء
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r6.claim: Abu al-Darda warns that ruin will come upon people who decorate their Qurʾans and embellish their mosques.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r6.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء : إذا حليتم مصاحفكم وزينتم مساجدكم فالدمار عليكم

RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r7.speaker: أنس
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r7.claim: Anas invokes the Prophet’s warning that people will boast about mosques while maintaining them only a little.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r7.anchor: فقال أنس : إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( سيأتي على أمتي زمان يتباهون في المساجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r8.speaker: أبو قتادة السلمي
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r8.claim: In both Sahihs, Abu Qatada transmits the Prophet’s instruction to pray two rakʿas before sitting upon entering a mosque.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r8.anchor: عن أبي قتادة السلمي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : ( إذا دخل أحدكم المسجد فليركع ركعتين

RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r9.speaker: الحسن البصري ومكحول والشافعي وأحمد وإسحق
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r9.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri, Makḥul, al-Shafiʿi, Ahmad, and Ishaq hold that the entrant should pray the two greeting rakʿas.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r9.anchor: واعلم أن القول بذلك مذهب الحسن البصري ومكحول وقول الشافعي وأحمد وإسحق

RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r10.speaker: ابن سيرين وعطاء بن أبي رباح والنخعي وقتادة ومالك والثوري وأصحاب الرأي
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r10.claim: Ibn Sirin, ʿAtaʾ, al-Nakhaʿi, Qatada, Malik, al-Thawri, and the jurists of opinion hold that the entrant sits without praying.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r10.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أنه يجلس ولا يصلي ، وإليه ذهب ابن سيرين وعطاء بن أبي رباح والنخعي

RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r11.speaker: فاطمة بنت رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r11.claim: Fatima reports that the Prophet invoked forgiveness and the doors of mercy when entering a mosque, and forgiveness and the doors of favor when leaving.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r11.anchor: روت فاطمة بنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبيها ، قالت : ( كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا دخل المسجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r12.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits that angels pray for forgiveness and mercy for a person who stays in the place of prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14/r12.anchor: أبو هريرة : قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( الملائكة تصلي على أحدكم ما دام في مصلاه الذي صلى فيه فتقول

RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r1.claim: The continuation of Abu Hurayra’s report says the angels’ prayer lasts as long as the worshipper does not invalidate ablution.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r1.anchor: اللهم اغفر له ، اللهم ارحمه ما لم يحدث

RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r2.speaker: عثمان بن مظعون
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r2.claim: When ʿUthman ibn Mazʿun sought castration, travel, and monastic retreat, the Prophet described fasting, jihad, and waiting in mosques for prayer as their community’s equivalents.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r2.anchor: روى أن عثمان بن مظعون أتى النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام فقال : ائذن لي في الاختصاء

RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r3.speaker: عمرو بن شعيب
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r3.claim: ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb transmits the Prophet’s prohibition of poetry recitations, trading, and pre-prayer Friday circles in mosques.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r3.anchor: عن عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام نهى عن تناشد الأشعار في المساجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r4.speaker: أحمد وإسحق وعطاء بن يسار
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r4.claim: Some scholars, including Ahmad, Ishaq, and ʿAtaʾ ibn Yasar, deem buying and selling in a mosque disliked; sellers were directed to the worldly market.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r4.anchor: وكان إذا مر عليه بعض من يبيع في المسجد قال : عليك بسوق الدنيا فإنما هذا سوق الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r5.speaker: سالم بن عبد الله بن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r5.claim: Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah designated the adjoining open space al-Baṭḥa for idle talk, poetry, or raising one’s voice, telling people to leave the mosque for it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r5.anchor: وكان لسالم بن عبد الله بن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنهم رحبة إلى جنب المسجد سماها البطحاء

RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r6.claim: Al-Razi reads the Friday report as disfavoring pre-prayer circles for studying; worshippers should remember God, pray, and listen to the sermon, while circles after prayer are permissible.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r6.anchor: واعلم أن الحديث الذي رويناه يدل على كراهية التحلق والاجتماع يوم الجمعة قبل الصلاة لمذاكرة العلم

RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r7.claim: Calling out for lost property and raising one’s voice for purposes other than remembrance are disliked; Abu Hurayra says to tell a caller that God should not return it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r7.anchor: وأما طلب الضالة في المسجد ، ورفع الصوت بغير الذكر ، فمكروه عن أبي هريرة

RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s instruction to tell anyone trading in a mosque, “May God not make your trade profitable.”
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r8.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أيضا أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : ( إذا رأيتم من يبيع أو يبتاع في المسجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r9.speaker: أبو سليمان الخطابي
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r9.claim: Al-Khattabi includes all dealings for people’s affairs and collection of their dues among activities for which mosques were not built.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r9.anchor: قال أبو سليمان الخطابي رحمه الله : ويدخل في هذا كل أمر لم يبن له المسجد من أمور معاملات الناس

RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r10.speaker: بعض السلف
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r10.claim: Some early Muslims disliked soliciting alms in mosques, and some held that people should not give to a solicitor who accosts them there.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r10.anchor: السلف المسألة في المسجد ، وكان بعضهم يرى أن لا يتصدق على السائل المتعرض في المسجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r11.speaker: عمر
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r11.claim: Umar ordered a person liable to a fixed punishment to be taken out of the mosque; a similar ruling is attributed to Ali.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r11.anchor: ورد النهي عن إقامة الحدود في المساجد ، قال عمر فيمن لزمه حد : أخرجاه من المسجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r12.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r12.claim: Muʿadh says mosques are kept free of fixed punishments, tax collection, poetry, lost-property calls, and being used as a market.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r12.anchor: وقال معاذ بن جبل : إن المساجد طهرت من خمس : من أن يقام فيها الحدود أو يقبض فيها الخراج

RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r13.speaker: الشعبي ويحيى بن يعمر وشريح
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r13.claim: Some jurists allow adjudication in a mosque, citing the Prophet’s imprecation between al-ʿAjlani and his wife and rulings by Shurayh, al-Shaʿbi, and Yahya ibn Yaʿmar.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r13.anchor: ولم ير بعضهم بالقضاء في المسجد بأسا ، لأن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام لاعن بين العجلاني وامرأته في المسجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r14.speaker: الحسن وزرارة بن أوفى
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r14.claim: Al-Hasan and Zarara ibn Awfa conducted judgments in the open space outside the mosque.
RAZI-FULL:v4p14#2/r14.anchor: وكان الحسن وزرارة بن أوفى يقضيان في الرحبة خارجا من المسجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r1.speaker: عباد بن تميم عن عمه
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r1.claim: In both Sahihs, ʿAbbad ibn Tamim reports from his uncle that he saw the Prophet reclining in the mosque with one leg over the other.
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r1.anchor: عن عباد بن تميم عن عمه أنه رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مستلقيا في المسجد واضعا إحدى رجليه

RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r2.claim: Al-Razi infers that leaning, reclining, and resting in a mosque are permissible as at home, except lying face-down, which the Prophet forbade as hateful to God.
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r2.anchor: وفيه دليل على جواز الاتكاء والاضطجاع وأنواع الاستراحة في المسجد مثل جوازها في البيت ، إلا الانبطاح

RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r3.speaker: نافع
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r3.claim: Nafiʿ reports that ʿAbd Allah was a young unmarried man without a household and used to sleep in the Prophet’s mosque.
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r3.anchor: وعن نافع أن عبد الله كان شابا أعزب لا أهل له فكان ينام في مسجد رسول الله

RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r4.speaker: قوم من أهل العلم وابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r4.claim: Some scholars permit sleeping in a mosque, while Ibn ʿAbbas says it should not be made a place to sleep or nap.
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r4.anchor: ورخص قوم من أهل العلم في النوم في المسجد ، وقال ابن عباس : لا تتخذوه مبيتا أو مقيلا

RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r5.speaker: أنس
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r5.claim: Anas transmits the Prophet’s teaching that spitting in a mosque is a sin and its expiation is burying the spit.
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r5.anchor: عن أنس عن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : ( البزاق في المسجد خطيئة وكفارتها دفنها )

RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r6.speaker: أبو ذر
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r6.claim: In a Sahih report, Abu Dharr says removing harm from a road is a good deed and unburied phlegm in a mosque is a bad deed.
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r6.anchor: وفي الصحيح عن أبي ذر قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( عرضت علي أعمال أمتي حسنها وسيئها فوجدت من محاسن أعمالها الأذى يماط عن الطريق

RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r7.claim: A report says the mosque contracts from phlegm as skin contracts in fire; one interpretation figures the conflict between the mosque’s dignity and the contempt of spitting.
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r7.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( إن المسجد لينزوي من النخامة كما تنزوي الجلدة في النار ) ، أي ينضم وينقبض

RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r8.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r8.claim: Others explain “the mosque contracts” as referring to the people in the mosque, namely the angels.
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r8.anchor: وقال آخرون : أراد أهل المسجد وهم الملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r9.claim: In both Sahihs, Abu Hurayra transmits that during prayer one must not spit ahead while conversing with God or to the right where an angel is, but should spit left or beneath the feet and bury it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r9.anchor: عن همام بن منبه قال : هذا ما حدثنا أبو هريرة عن محمد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( إذا قام أحدكم إلى الصلاة فلا يبصق أمامه

RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r10.speaker: أنس
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r10.claim: Anas reports that after seeing phlegm toward the qibla, the Prophet removed it and instructed worshippers not to spit toward the qibla; al-Bukhari records the report.
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r10.anchor: وعن أنس أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام رأى نخامة في القبلة فشق ذلك عليه حتى رؤي في وجهه فقام فحكه بيده

RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r11.speaker: أنس وابن عمر وجابر
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r11.claim: In both Sahihs, Anas, Ibn ʿUmar, and Jabir transmit that anyone eating the foul-smelling plant should stay away because angels are affected by what affects people.
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r11.anchor: في الصحيحين عن أنس وابن عمر وجابر قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( من أكل من هذه الشجرة المنتنة فلا يقربن مسجدنا

RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r12.speaker: جابر
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r12.claim: Jabir transmits the Prophet’s instruction that anyone eating garlic or onion should keep away from the mosque.
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r12.anchor: وعن جابر أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : ( من أكل ثوما أو بصلا فليعتزل مسجدنا )

RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r13.speaker: جابر
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r13.claim: When given a pot of odorous greens, the Prophet told those present to give it to someone else, since he communes with beings they do not; both Sahihs record it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r13.anchor: وأن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام أتي بقدر فيه خضر فوجد لها ريحا ، فسأل فأخبر بما فيه من البقول

RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r14.speaker: عائشة
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r14.claim: ʿAisha reports that the Prophet ordered mosques to be built in residential areas, cleaned, and perfumed.
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r14.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت : أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ببناء المسجد في الدور

RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r15.speaker: أنس
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r15.claim: When a Bedouin urinated in the mosque, the Prophet stopped companions from interrupting him, taught that mosques are for Qurʾan, remembrance, and prayer, and ordered water poured over it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p15/r15.anchor: أنس بن مالك قال : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في المسجد ومعه أصحابه إذ جاء أعرابي فبال في المسجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r1.claim: Jurists disagree: Abu Hanifa permits non-Muslims in mosques generally, Malik forbids it generally, and al-Shafiʿi bars them from the sanctuary and Sacred Mosque.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r1.anchor: اختلف الفقهاء في دخول الكافر المسجد ، فجوزه أبو حنيفة مطلقا ، وأباه مالك مطلقا ، وقال الشافعي

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r2.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r2.claim: Al-Shafiʿi’s first proof is 9:28: polytheists are impure and must not approach the Sacred Mosque; either “mosque” or the whole sanctuary fits the disputed sites.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r2.anchor: احتج الشافعي بوجوه . أولها : قوله تعالى : { إنما المشركون نجس فلا يقربوا المسجد الحرام

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r3.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r3.claim: Al-Shafiʿi notes that “the Sacred Mosque” can mean the whole sanctuary, as in 17:1, since the Prophet’s night journey began from Khadija’s house.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r3.anchor: قد يكون المراد من المسجد الحرام الحرم لقوله تعالى : { سبحان الذي أسرى بعبده ليلا من المسجد الحرام

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r4.claim: The objection that 9:28 concerns pilgrimage because it says “after this year” is weak: it abandons the apparent meaning without cause.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r4.anchor: فإن قيل : المراد به الحج ولهذا قال : { بعد عامهم هاذا } لأن الحج إنما يفعل في السنة مرة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r5.claim: Al-Razi invokes the legal principle that a ruling attached to a description signals that description as its cause; thus polytheists remain excluded while they remain polytheists.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r5.anchor: ثبت في أصول الفقه أن ترتيب الحكم على الوصف مشعر بكون ذلك الوصف علة لذلك الحكم

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r6.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r6.claim: Al-Shafiʿi’s second proof is that 2:114 says the obstructors may enter only fearfully, implying they are barred and fear expulsion if they enter.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r6.anchor: وثانيها : قوله تعالى : { أولئك ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين } وهذا يقتضي أن يمنعوا من دخول المسجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r7.claim: Al-Razi rejects limiting 2:114 to those who ruined Jerusalem or prevented the Prophet praying at the Kaaba: its general wording covers more cases.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r7.anchor: أن قوله تعالى : { ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله } ظاهر في العموم ، فتخصيصه ببعض الصور خلاف الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r8.claim: Al-Razi rejects the alternative that fear means fear of tax or expulsion: the wording makes fear arise from entering, not from another cause.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r8.anchor: وعن الثاني : أن الظاهر قوله : { ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين } يقتضي أن يكون ذلك الخوف إنما حصل من الدخول

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r9.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r9.claim: Al-Shafiʿi’s third proof is 9:17–18: mosque maintenance includes construction and regular attendance, and 9:18 reserves it for believers.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r9.anchor: وثالثها : قوله تعالى : { ما كان للمشركين أن يعمروا مساجد الله شهدين على أنفسهم بالكفر

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r10.claim: Al-Razi says mosque maintenance can mean building and repairing, or attending and frequenting it; ordinary speech calls a regular attendee one who maintains a mosque.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r10.anchor: وعمارتها تكون بوجهين . أحدهما : بناؤها وإصلاحها . والثاني : حضورها ولزومها

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r11.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r11.claim: The Prophet says that when people see a man frequenting mosques, they should testify to his faith, supporting attendance as a form of maintenance.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r11.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( إذا رأيتم الرجل يعتاد المساجد فاشهدوا له بالإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r12.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r12.claim: Al-Shafiʿi argues that the sanctuary must be honored; enabling unbelievers to enter risks disrespect or defilement because of their beliefs.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r12.anchor: ورابعها : أن الحرم واجب التعظيم لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام في الدعاء : ( اللهم زد هذا البيت تشريفا

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r13.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r13.claim: Al-Shafiʿi combines the command to purify the House in 22:26 with the declaration that polytheists are impure in 9:28 to argue they must be kept away.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r13.anchor: وخامسها : أن الله تعالى أمر بتطهير البيت

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r14.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r14.claim: The argument that even the ritually impure are excluded makes excluding unbelievers more compelling, though Al-Razi notes that this supports Malik’s wider ban from every mosque.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r14.anchor: وسادسها : أجمعنا على أن الجنب يمنع منه ، فالكافر بأن يمنع منه أولى إلا أن هذا مقتضى مذهب مالك

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r15.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r15.claim: Abu Hanifa’s first proof is a report that the Prophet lodged a delegation from Yathrib in the mosque.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r15.anchor: واحتج أبو حنيفة رحمه الله بأمور ، الأول : روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قدم عليه وفد يثرب

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r16.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r16.claim: Abu Hanifa’s second proof is that the Prophet declared entrants to Abu Sufyan’s house or the Kaaba safe; al-Razi says both reports predate and were abrogated by the verse.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r16.anchor: قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( من دخل دار أبي سفيان فهو آمن ومن دخل الكعبة فهو آمن )

RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r17.claim: Abu Hanifa analogizes the Sacred Mosque to other mosques where unbelievers may enter; al-Razi rejects the analogy because the Sacred Mosque has greater sanctity.
RAZI-FULL:v4p16/r17.anchor: المسجد الحرام أجل قدرا من سائر المساجد فظهر الفرق
